proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, secrets management, and privacy-preserving execution boundaries for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation ([AAIF](../governance/technical-committee.md)) responsible for establishing security baselines, threat modeling frameworks, privacy-preserving execution patterns, and runtime defense standards for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. Operating on a bi-weekly cadence under chair leadership, the working group functions as an intersecting layer that applies security and privacy assessments across the architectural deliverables of related AAIF groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope and Core Themes
The working group organizes its technical inquiries and charter deliverables around several foundational areas of agentic security[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d]:
- **Privacy-Preserving Workflows and Protected Data**: Guardrails and isolation patterns for sensitive data, confidential training assets, and regulated domains such as HIPAA. Technical mechanisms under study include zero-knowledge proofs returning boolean assertions, trusted execution environments (TEEs), and encrypted vector databases[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Secrets and Sensitive Data Management**: Policy and token boundaries separating traditional runtime credentials (API keys, environment variables) and proprietary context from generative model pipelines[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Rogue Agent Containment and Blast Radius**: Architectural controls, checkpointing hooks, and runtime isolation to measure and bound the blast radius of compromised, rogue, or derailed agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Commerce and Payment Guardrails**: Security boundaries for transactional agents, preventing unauthorized fund draining, account token leakage, and out-of-scope financial commitments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Penetration Testing and Threat Modeling**: Adversarial red-teaming methodologies, prompt injection mitigation, persuasion resistance, and auditability forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].

## Cross-Group and External Boundaries
The working group maintains explicit boundaries with adjacent efforts:
- **Ethics and Value Judgments**: Ethical determinations, business morality, and value-judgment questions are explicitly deferred to the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Accuracy versus Derailment**: Pure model hallucination and baseline reliability belong to the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), though guardrails addressing non-malicious agent misbehavior, derailment, and accidental sabotage remain an active area of coordination[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].
- **Identity and Delegation**: Coordinates with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) on capability-based authorization, agent-to-agent mutual authentication, and MCP server access restrictions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e].
- **Industry Alignment**: Collaborates with external standards bodies including the OWASP Agentic AI security initiative to minimize cross-industry duplication[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

# Lifecycle History
The working group held its orientation session on February 17, 2026, outlining its governance structure, multi-tier membership participation, and ideation roadmap[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e080ea2d4af5-49d9592e]. On March 3, 2026, Alex Frazer was elected working group chair, and the group established three formal milestones to finalize its mission scope, establish deliverable streams (including an internal shared security taxonomy), and submit its charter to the Governing Board[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-563e910f8be2-6ff86a0d].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group aligning agentic AI architectures with global AI regulations, compliance frameworks, and risk management protocols.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to align autonomous and agentic AI architectures with emerging international legal, regulatory, and compliance frameworks[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. Operating under Linux Foundation pre-competitive collaboration boundaries, the working group focuses on mapping existing standards—such as the European Union AI Act, eIDAS 2, and data protection/GDPR controls—while formulating gap analyses and guidance tailored specifically to autonomous agent operations[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Architecture / Specification

### Three-Step Operational Methodology

The working group organizes its deliverables into a sequential three-phase lifecycle to avoid duplication of established industry frameworks and isolate risks distinct to agentic systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:

1. **Landscape Analysis**: Compiling and cataloging existing international standards, regulatory statutes, compliance regimes (e.g., GDPR, EU AI Act, eIDAS 2), and enterprise deployment use cases[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
2. **Gap Analysis**: Benchmarking current compliance approaches against autonomous agent behaviors to pinpoint structural omissions in oversight, delegation authority, probabilistic risk assessment, and runtime accountability[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
3. **Distilled Guidance and Principles**: Producing practical architectural guidance, risk assessment protocols, and implementation baselines for regulated environments[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

### Scope Boundaries and Foundation Interlocks

- **Governance Alignment**: Governed under the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) with leadership charter approval reporting directly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **External Agency Liaison**: Engaging cross-jurisdictional stakeholders and regulatory sandboxes, including co-creation frameworks with international bodies (such as Singapore regulators)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **Collaboration Cadence**: Conducted on a biweekly cadence with standardized meeting documentation workflows designed for automated indexing and record management[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-19**: Inaugural kickoff meeting; defined antitrust operating boundaries, initiated chair/co-chair nomination timelines, and identified target regulatory benchmarks including the EU AI Act and eIDAS 2[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654].
- **2026-03-05**: Formally ratified the three-step operating model (landscape analysis, gap analysis, distilled guidance) and initiated the problem statement backlog[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654].

# References

- [WG Governance, Risk and Regulatory Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654]
- [Meeting Notes Archive](https://github.com/aaif/wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory/blob/bfcefbf1250c2d3d6b6f2dcf20829a7ab24136a2/meeting-notes/README.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d7a6875f36a3-5c7bc654]

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation managing working groups, project intake, and technical lifecycle policies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary governing technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), operating under the AAIF Governing Board to oversee technical projects, maintain lifecycle policies, and establish working groups[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Adopted on March 3, 2026, the TC Charter formalizes the committee's scope, voting procedures, and operational relationship to the Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Charter and Operations
The Technical Committee assists the Governing Board by evaluating project proposals, advising on strategic technical priorities, and implementing the foundation's lifecycle processes[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Composition and Leadership
- **Membership**: Each Platinum Member of the AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative to the TC[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Chairs**: The TC elects an annual Chair and optional Co-Chair to lead meetings and coordinate operations[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Mandate and Responsibilities
Under Section 2.3 of the Charter, TC responsibilities include[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- Establishing, maintaining, and archiving working groups across AAIF technical domains[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Coordinating technical vision and multi-project collaboration across the community[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Recommending projects to the Governing Board for official acceptance and voting on project advancement across lifecycle stages[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- Recommending resource priorities to the Governing Board to support AAIF technical projects[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

## Voting and Decision-Making
- **Consensus & Lazy Consensus**: The TC prioritizes community consensus, applying a lazy consensus ("silence-as-agreement") mechanism where proposals pass automatically if no formal objection is filed within 72 hours[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Formal Ballots**: When formal voting is required, decisions proceed on a one-vote-per-voting-member basis[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Electronic votes without a meeting mandate a majority vote of all voting members[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Quorum**: Quorum mandates attendance of at least 50% of voting members to take binding votes[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. Unresolvable deadlocks may be escalated to the Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Amendments**: Charter updates require approval from two-thirds of the TC along with Governing Board confirmation[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# References
- Operates alongside technical governance policies including the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) and [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md).

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, privacy engineering practices, and cross-workgroup review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee workstream co-chaired by Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu (Google), chartered to establish open security baselines, threat models, and privacy engineering practices across the agentic ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]. The working group approaches security as a shared discipline among foundation model providers, application builders, consumers, and peer foundation workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

# Mission and Deliverables
On March 31, 2026, the working group adopted its formal mission: *"The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI ecosystem. Producing open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI."*[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

## Planned Deliverables
The working group focuses on five core deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec]:
1. **Taxonomy and Vocabulary**: Living catalog defining agentic security concepts and terms (including definitions of "agentic" and tool boundary security), in coordination with [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
2. **Agentic AI Threat Model Framework**: Pragmatic guidance evaluating prompt injection, social engineering vectors, and tool execution attack surfaces[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
3. **Security Architecture and Design Patterns**: Architectural specifications governing runtime monitoring, isolation boundaries, kill switches, and skill security[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
4. **Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical baseline controls for building, deploying, and operating agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
5. **Cross-Workgroup Review Checklist**: Reusable security and privacy checklists applied when reviewing specifications across AAIF workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].

## Cross-Workgroup Collaboration
To maintain focus without overlapping mandates, the working group has established key boundaries with other working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35]:
- **[Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md)**: Identity and Trust leads decentralized identity and cryptographic authorization protocols, while Security and Privacy provides requirements covering runtime bounding, auditability, and logging[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **[Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md)**: Coordinates on anomaly detection, behavioral forensics, and audit trail schemas[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-822dcec9cbfd-b1d860ec].
- **[Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md)**: Coordinates through cross-group liaisons to establish transaction guardrails and payment safety[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].
- **[Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)**: Security and Privacy focuses on technical "privacy engineering" (data minimization, memory sanitation, confidential compute) rather than interpreting statutory compliance mandates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-f9b60c3f43ba-8b4c1f35].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent observability conventions, session-level trace models, and cross-framework coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG), led by Pavan Sudheendra, advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing shared understanding and conventions for agent observability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Rather than creating a competing standards body, the working group functions as an industry coordination forum that aligns existing telemetry initiatives (such as OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context) and specifies guidance where critical coverage gaps exist[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Charter and Objectives
The OT-WG was created to address industry challenges in multi-turn, multi-modal agent deployments[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:
1. **Fragmentation**: Over a dozen disparate trace conventions and proprietary observability tools risk vendor lock-in and prevent cross-framework interoperability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
2. **Session and Workflow Gaps**: While individual LLM call tracing is well-served, understanding multi-turn reasoning loops, tool interactions, and system state transitions across workflows remains unstandardized[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
3. **Accountability & Multi-Modal Lineage**: Enterprise adoption requires robust auditability, behavioral explanation, and content lineage across modality transformations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

## Guiding Principles
The draft charter codifies six operating principles[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]:
- **Coordinate first, specify only when necessary**: Default to contributing upstream to existing standards bodies; only produce new specifications when clear gaps are confirmed[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Interoperability over innovation**: Compose with and extend established specifications rather than inventing redundant mechanisms[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Observable by default**: Architect agent systems with native, out-of-the-box telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Move at the speed of the ecosystem**: Deliver incremental, practical milestones in step with industry evolution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Adoption is key**: Prioritize implementable conventions with committed ecosystem adoption over abstract designs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- **Vendor and framework neutrality**: Avoid giving structural advantage to any specific platform or product[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

## Focus Areas and Coordination
The OT-WG maintains the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) as its founding focus area to standardize behavioral execution graphs and provenance records[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. It collaborates closely with [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md) regarding forensic audit logging and anomaly detection, as well as [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) for verifiable trace attestation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, privacy reviews, and baseline operational safeguards for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for defining security architectures, threat models, design patterns, and baseline privacy practices across agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. The group collaborates with external standards bodies and ecosystem projects—including Model Context Protocol (MCP) working groups and Linux Foundation security initiatives—to embed security controls into agent interfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical work around agent control and containment, runtime execution boundaries, and cross-cutting reviews [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. Its charter formalizes five initial deliverables across a 3–6 month horizon [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]:

1. **Taxonomy**: Living reference definitions covering security and privacy terms to be contributed directly into the core foundation taxonomy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
2. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Research initiative evaluating whether existing frameworks (such as OWASP or NIST AI RMF) sufficiently cover modern agentic risks, including shared memory stores, trust boundaries, and dynamic neural architectures, documented in [agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Technical guidance cataloging builder patterns for human-in-the-loop controls, hook extensibility, logical/semantic constraint enforcement, and privacy-preserving execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
4. **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical, educational guidelines addressing operational security fundamentals, including secrets management and secure tool invocation, articulated in [agentic-ai-security-best-practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].
5. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Review mechanism adapted from standards body practices to help other AAIF working groups identify security and privacy ramifications early in specification design [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

Additionally, the working group monitors protocol-level extensibility efforts, such as MCP Interceptors for standardized policy hooks and MCP Apps for browser-like agent identity verification [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-04-14, the working group unanimously approved its formal scope and operating charter by member vote, alongside formal approval for its five initial deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151]. Group leadership scheduled formal submission and presentation of the charter to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for final governance ratification [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4cd71dcfd1ce-c26f3151].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Interactive catalog and CNCF landscape2 data pipeline mapping prominent open-source software and open standards projects across the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive catalog and ecosystem map providing an overview of prominent open-source software and open standards in agentic AI [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Hosted at [landscape.aaif.io](https://landscape.aaif.io), the landscape highlights Agentic AI Foundation member projects, community initiatives, and foundational technologies categorized across domain areas [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

The landscape generation pipeline runs on a daily cadence and is powered by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation's `cncf/landscape2` engine [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Taxonomy mappings and categorization principles align with the broader work of the [../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) working group.

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape repository maintains structured declarative definitions and assets that compile into the web application [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:

- **Project Declarations (`landscape.yml`)**: Projects are cataloged in alphabetical order under explicit categories [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Entries may supply an `extra` block detailing granular metadata, links, and operational classifications [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Hosted Logos (`hosted_logos/`)**: Each entry references a vector logo stored as an SVG file [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Logos must include the organization or project name in English, avoid inverted or non-transparent backgrounds, and use stacked variants when alternative orientations exist [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Build & Synchronization Pipeline**: Changes merged into the landscape repository trigger a daily build through `cncf/landscape2`, refreshing repository metrics and synchronized metadata [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Inclusion and Submission Criteria

New projects submitted via pull request must fulfill strict inclusion constraints [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:

- **Open-Source Footprint**: Software projects must be open source and have accumulated at least 1,000 GitHub stars while fitting cleanly into an existing landscape category [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Single Categorization**: An organization is generally represented in a single box reflecting its primary or best-known offering, with exceptions reserved for large multi-product organizations [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Exclusion of Closed Source**: Closed-source software, proprietary standards, commercial hosted distributions of open-source projects, and proprietary solutions implementing open standards are excluded [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Trademark and Ownership Attribution**: The Crunchbase organization associated with an entry must correspond to the entity or company holding control over the project's trademark [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Licensing and Governance

Landscape definitions and repository contents are maintained under Linux Foundation project terms, whereas external organizational data ingested from Crunchbase remains governed by Crunchbase Data Access Terms for Linux Foundation landscape deployments [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with formulating threat models, baseline controls, privacy guidelines, and defensive architectures for autonomous and multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The group collaborates across AAIF workstreams and external protocol ecosystems to identify trust boundary violations, malicious tool invocation, and data leakage across agentic workflows.

Following its initial charter presentation to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group operates under active status while finalizing formal procedural signoff, organizing workstreams to address risk profiles in tool protocols and multi-agent coordination [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group coordinates deliverables across distributed security domains:

- **Cross-Working Group Taxonomy Collaboration**: Serving as the initial cross-WG deliverable within AAIF, the SP WG draft taxonomy acts as the baseline for unifying security, privacy, and identity terms across foundation groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Protocol Trust Boundaries & Interceptors**: Evaluating security surfaces in integration protocols, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors for data redaction and access controls, and MCP Apps where interactive UIs challenge browser security boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Multi-Agent Guardrails & Isolation**: Formulating verification architectures and trust boundaries for multi-agent delegation, isolating untrusted inputs and tool execution through hardware attestation and runtime policies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-28**: Presented charter to Technical Committee; proceeded under active operational footing following four formal approvals and additional verbal endorsements [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **2026-04-28**: WG chairs established taxonomy as the first cross-WG collaboration deliverable, using the SP WG draft as the foundation starting point [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **2026-04-28**: Shifted working structure toward self-organizing asynchronous workstreams backed by bi-weekly checkpoint meetings accommodating global time zones [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Overview

The Working Group Submission Guidelines establish the formal submission and intake process for community members proposing new working groups to the Agentic AI Foundation [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]. All proposals must be submitted through the designated GitHub issue template in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository to ensure standardized review against foundation goals [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake Requirements and Fields

Proposals must supply complete submitter metadata before advancing to Technical Committee review [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c]:
- **Submitter Information**: Proposer's full name, email address, role title, and verified affiliation with an AAIF Member Organization [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Membership Status**: Confirmation of whether the sponsor organization holds Platinum or Gold AAIF membership tier [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Scope and Charter Definition**: Proposed working group name, primary objectives, expected deliverables, and initial workstream breakdown [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

## Review Timelines and Assignment

- **Initial Triage**: Proposals submitted via the `working-group-proposal.yml` template are tagged with the `New` label and assigned for intake triage [^evt-working-group-proposals-pr-1][^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].
- **Review Schedule**: While proposals may be submitted on a rolling basis, formal Technical Committee reviews initiate according to the foundation intake calendar, with initial proposal reviews scheduled to begin on June 1, 2026 [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-cfe1353c].

# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) serves as the primary technical oversight body of the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The committee evaluates working group charters, manages project lifecycle progression, aligns cross-cutting foundational standards, and coordinates foundation-level technical direction in conjunction with the AAIF Chief Technology Officer [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Oversight Mandate

- **Working Group Charter Approval**: The TC functions as the required oversight board that reviews and formally votes on new working group charters before they are established within the AAIF [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. Approval requires formal voting by committee members through pull requests and governance meetings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Cross-Group Harmonization**: The TC and working group chairs align overlapping initiatives across groups, such as establishing unified foundational taxonomy efforts as cross-working group milestones [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-28**: Manik assumed the role of AAIF Chief Technology Officer, succeeding Matt [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

The `aaif/public-agents` repository maintains public, portable agent skills, integration recipes, and automated verification suites for the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-public-agents-file-b248ae41d1f0-0667ce2f][^evt-public-agents-file-ae1d68d00103-0e76c626]. # Architecture / Specification

The repository incorporates continuous integration workflows to test multi-model inference capabilities:
- **GitHub Models Integration**: The `copilot-test-action` workflow queries the GitHub Models catalog endpoint (`https://models.github.ai/catalog/models`) and executes chat completion inferences against selected models under organization-level credentials [^evt-public-agents-file-b248ae41d1f0-0667ce2f].
- **Gemini API Integration**: The `gemini-test-action` workflow verifies connectivity and content generation across Gemini model versions (such as `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-pro`) using direct REST API endpoints [^evt-public-agents-file-ae1d68d00103-0e76c626].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral agent observability conventions, trace formats, and cross-framework telemetry alignment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards organizations to build a shared understanding of agent observability across multi-turn interactions, tool calls, and model boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d] Hosted within the Agentic AI Foundation under Linux Foundation governance patterns, the working group operates primarily as an ecosystem coordination forum rather than a competing standalone standards body.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

# Architecture / Specification

## Mandate and Guiding Principles

The working group addresses vendor fragmentation across agent frameworks and the structural observability gap between single LLM invocation tracing and end-to-end agent workflow execution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d] Key operating principles include:

- **Coordinate First, Specify Only When Necessary**: Default to aligning with and contributing upstream to active standards bodies—including the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context—formulating new specifications only when an unaddressed domain gap is established.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- **Interoperability over Innovation**: Extend and compose with existing observability standards rather than designing incompatible alternatives.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- **Observable by Default**: Encourage out-of-the-box telemetry and semantic hooks across agent execution engines.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]
- **Vendor and Framework Neutrality**: Maintain platform-agnostic conventions that avoid conferring advantage to any single vendor or agent runtime.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

## Focus Area Model

The working group coordinates specialized focus areas and sub-groups. Its founding focus area is the Agent Behavior Trace Model (`../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md`), which addresses session-level lineage, multi-turn reasoning traces, and multi-modal transformations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

# Lifecycle History

The working group charter was ratified by the working group on April 15, 2026, and approved on May 13, 2026, with Pavan Sudheendra serving as primary contact and working group chair.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, delegation, and authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by identifying and promoting vendor-neutral, interoperable viewpoints and standards for agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c] The group enables agents to be discovered across platforms, verify operational origin, represent delegating principals, and establish auditable authority chains across organizational boundaries.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Technical Focus

The working group charter delineates specific technical boundaries covering enterprise and consumer agent deployment models:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Frameworks for identifying agents, authenticating runtime interactions, and conveying operational provenance, including operator identity and host software context.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Mechanisms representing an agent acting on behalf of an individual, role, team, service, or process, defining the boundaries and propagation of delegated authority.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained authorization patterns, policy constraints, and bindings to human approval controls (`../patterns/human-approval-gate.md`).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: Protocols evaluating whether external or cross-domain agents can be trusted to execute requested operations.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]
- **Agent Discovery and Trust Metadata**: Standardized metadata structures supporting discovery, trust establishment, observability, and traceability.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

## Out of Scope Boundaries

The charter explicitly excludes serving as a formal standards development organization (SDO), creating general secure execution architectures (delegated to the Security & Privacy Working Group (`../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`)), formulating broad public policy positions, or building production-grade identity infrastructure and certification programs.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

# Lifecycle History

The working group was formed under the leadership and chair contact of Grant Miller, operating in coordination with Foundation working groups and external standards bodies.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]

# Overview

The Project Proposal Process specifies intake criteria, submission issue templates, triage guidelines, and technical review procedures for incoming open-source projects seeking admission into the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-project-proposals-pr-23] The process operationalizes the admission gates defined in the Project Lifecycle Policy (`../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md`).[^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake Requirements Alignment

Project proposal forms are maintained to ensure intake barriers match the stage-appropriate criteria established by the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`):[^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]

- **Roadmap Artifacts**: Submitting a published roadmap is categorized as an optional submission item rather than a gating prerequisite for initial proposal acceptance.[^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]
- **OpenSSF Best Practices Badge**: Demonstrating an OpenSSF best practices badge is an optional indicator during initial proposal filing, preventing early-stage or incubating projects from being excluded prior to review.[^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]

Reconciling proposal template schemas with underlying lifecycle policy definitions ensures candidate tools and runtimes can be admitted to the Sandbox stage based on core technical merit and community relevance.[^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]

# Lifecycle History

In PR#23 of `aaif/project-proposals`, the intake template fields for roadmap status and OpenSSF badges were adjusted to optional, resolving an inconsistency between the intake issue form and the published Project Lifecycle Policy.[^evt-project-proposals-pr-23]

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security design patterns, privacy frameworks, and containment controls across the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPAA) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Formally led by Chair Alex Frazer and Co-Chair Junjie Bu, the group develops open threat models, shared architectural taxonomies, and reusable design patterns that model providers, runtime authors, and peer working groups can adopt to mitigate autonomous agent risks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Boundaries
The working group focuses on core agent security and autonomy risks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]:
- **Threat Modeling and Attack Analysis:** Identifying agent-specific attack vectors including prompt injection, confused deputy scenarios, authorization boundary traversals, unsafe tool invocation, and memory vulnerabilities.
- **Security Architecture and Design Patterns:** Developing architectural blueprints for execution governance, least-privilege tool access, and runtime isolation, connecting with patterns such as [../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md).
- **Agent Control and Containment:** Designing containment mechanisms and emergency intervention capabilities, including [../patterns/kill-switch.md](../patterns/kill-switch.md).
- **Data Protection and Privacy:** Establishing controls to protect sensitive data traversing multi-agent workflows and delegated service interactions without continuous human supervision.
- **Cross-WG Collaboration:** Producing shared review checklists and threat perspectives for peer groups like [../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) and [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).

Explicitly out of scope are[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]:
- Ethics, bias, and normative value judgments, which are deferred to the [../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) working group.
- Prescribing or interpreting regulatory compliance mandates.
- Formal commercial certification programs for agentic tools or runtimes.

## Deliverables and Operating Model
The working group operates under open consensus with biweekly meetings, escalating governance deadlocks to the [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. Initial deliverables include[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]:
- **Security & Privacy Taxonomy v0:** Harmonized terminology coordinated with [../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist:** Systematic security gate criteria for Foundation technical outputs.
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis:** Systematic benchmarking of existing AI security standards, tracked under [../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).
- **Design Patterns Catalog & Best Practices Guide:** Operational security references for deploying production agent architectures.

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Blog Intake Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Editorial policies, eligibility constraints, content requirements, and intake workflows governing publications on aaif.io.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Blog Intake Guidelines govern editorial standards, submitter eligibility, review timelines, and submission workflows for content published on aaif.io[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. Owned and managed end-to-end by the Linux Foundation and AAIF communications team, the blog serves as an educational and technical outlet spotlighting open-source agentic projects, production case studies, architecture patterns, and ecosystem milestones[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Contributor Eligibility and Submission Rules
Contributions are welcome across five designated community categories, subject to specific constraints[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]:
- **Member Companies:** Posts must remain strictly vendor-neutral. They may include at most one or two concluding sentences with a single external link (such as a company homepage, relevant repository, or open job position).
- **Project Maintainers & Contributors:** Technical updates, release notes, and engineering deep-dives covering AAIF-hosted projects such as Model Context Protocol (MCP), [../resources/goose.md](../resources/goose.md), and AGENTS.md.
- **Working Groups & Technical Committee:** Authoritative progress reports, architectural whitepapers, and specifications endorsed by working groups or the [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md).
- **Community Contributors:** Practical tutorials, how-to guides, and thought leadership. Submissions are capped at two posts per calendar month per contributor.
- **Event Participants:** Recaps, takeaways, and lessons learned from AAIF-affiliated hackathons and community events.

## Editorial Standards and Intake Workflow
All submissions must comply with core editorial requirements prior to intake[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]:
- **Narrative Format:** Content must follow an educational narrative format (typically 600–1,500 words, with longer technical deep-dives permitted) rather than marketing copy or press releases.
- **Vendor Neutrality:** Articles must avoid promotional framing, unsupported superiority assertions, or language disparaging open-source alternatives.
- **Originality & Timeliness:** Submissions must be previously unpublished and represent recent work or announcements, generally within the prior two months.
- **Lead Times:** Contributors must submit finalized drafts through the official Asana intake form with a standard two-week review lead time.

Contributors can automate draft shaping, neutrality checks, and package preparation using the [../skills/aaif-blog-guidelines.md](../skills/aaif-blog-guidelines.md) modular agent skill[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c][^evt-foundation-pr-2].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Blog Guidelines Agent Skill (`aaif-blog-guidelines`) is an open skill specification and automated workflow packaged under [../resources/public-agent-skills.md](../resources/public-agent-skills.md) to help contributors author, revise, and package submissions for aaif.io[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]. Authored by Angie Jones as version 1.0, the skill automates compliance with [../guidelines/blog-guidelines.md](../guidelines/blog-guidelines.md), ensuring submissions are technically useful, vendor-neutral, and ready for Linux Foundation intake triage[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Installation
The skill can be installed globally into compatible agent harnesses using the skills CLI[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c][^evt-foundation-pr-2]:
```bash
npx skills add aaif/public-agents --skill aaif-blog-guidelines --global
```

## Execution Workflow
When assisting an author, the skill enforces a seven-stage intake pipeline[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed]:
1. **Clarify the Story:** Establish target audience, AAIF relevance, news timeliness (within the past two months), practical takeaways, and desired publish timing.
2. **Check Eligibility:** Confirm author category (member company, project maintainer, working group member, or community contributor within monthly submission limits) and prior stakeholder approval.
3. **Shape the Post:** Enforce narrative prose structure over corporate marketing copy or press release formats.
4. **Enforce Neutrality:** Strip sales pitches, product superiority claims, and framing that advantages an individual member over others.
5. **Strengthen Utility:** Inject practical technical depth, code or configuration samples, architectural context (such as MCP or [../resources/goose.md](../resources/goose.md)), and operational lessons learned.
6. **Prepare Submission Package:** Assemble final draft text, proposed title, author biographies, headshots/logos, social amplification copy, and target publish dates.
7. **Set Expectations:** Inform the author of review lead times (minimum two weeks) and direct them to the official Asana intake form.

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body responsible for defining open threat models, security design patterns, privacy frameworks, and cross-working group security review standards for agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. Operating within the AAIF technical committee framework, the group coordinates security baselines across foundation initiatives and establishes shared alignment with external standard-setting bodies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into focused workstreams managed via dedicated asynchronous communication channels and recurring all-hands meetings[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]:

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling and Framework Design**: The primary near-term technical workstream, producing the [threat modeling gap analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md) to benchmark multi-turn autonomous risks against existing standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Sequenced after the threat modeling output, this deliverable catalogues concrete technical implementations—including execution hooks, boundary checkpoints, and human-in-the-loop interfaces—alongside anti-patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: High-level operational and advisory guidance paired with the patterns catalog to establish baseline deployment controls, including [agentic security best practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: An early-stage review rubric designed for chairs of other AAIF working groups to evaluate security and privacy implications during specification drafting[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

### Cross-Working Group and Ecosystem Alignment
Early drafting of agentic terminology originated within this group before being elevated into an AAIF-wide effort stewarded by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]. The working group also conducts outreach and alignment with adjacent industry standards, including the Agentic AI Risk Model (AARM), Model Context Protocol (MCP) applications, and generalized execution hooks in collaboration with the MCP Agent Control Spec (ACS) effort[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Lifecycle History
The working group transitioned charter voting from GitHub to the Linux Foundation LFX platform while establishing standing agenda items like "News You Can Use" to track external ecosystem updates and regulatory publications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Ecosystem Architecture Map is an interactive CNCF Landscape 2 deployment mapping agent runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, observability platforms, commerce rails, and global regulatory frameworks across the agentic AI landscape.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007] Managed cooperatively under the `aaif-landscape` repository and the Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group, the architecture map visualizes community implementations, foundation member initiatives, and ecosystem projects in structured categories.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Tiers and Watchlist
The landscape decouples foundation membership organizations from software projects and categorizes ecosystem technologies into four defined tiers:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]
- **Graduated** (`#00f5d4`): Mature, production-hardened foundational projects.
- **Incubating** (`#9b5de5`): High-potential technologies progressing through foundation incubation.
- **Member** (`#00b4d8`): Upstream projects maintained or sponsored by AAIF member organizations.
- **External** (`#f15bb5`): Significant third-party frameworks, toolkits, and platforms within the broader agentic ecosystem.

A dedicated open-source agentic AI project watchlist section highlights leading external and member initiatives, designed for telemetry alignment with the Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard on LFX Insights.[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]

## CI/CD Validation and Overlays
The landscape configuration is governed and tested through GitHub Actions workflows:
- **Schema Validation**: Automated checks execute `cncf/landscape2-validate-action@v2` across both data (`landscape.yml`) and settings (`settings.yml`) files on pull requests and merge groups.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340]
- **Pull Request Previews**: A preview action comments on incoming pull requests with dynamic overlay links targeting `overlay-data`, `overlay-settings`, and `overlay-logos` on the landscape rendering engine.[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00]

# Lifecycle History
The architecture map was upgraded to the CNCF Landscape 2 platform, decoupling members and projects into distinct groups and introducing automated validation pipelines.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines define the formal eligibility criteria, required proposal sections, and review mechanisms for establishing new Working Groups within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a] Working Groups are structured, time-bound member collaborations organized to address specific technical, policy, safety, or regulatory challenges across agentic AI systems.[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]

# Architecture / Specification

## Eligibility Criteria
Submission of new Working Group proposals is restricted exclusively to Foundation Member organizations in good standing across any membership level.[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a] Proposals originating from non-member organizations are rejected without review.[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]

## Proposal Specification Requirements
To be considered for review, proposals submitted to `aaif/working-group-proposals` must document eight mandatory sections:[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]
1. **Submitter Information**: Proposer name, organizational affiliation, role, contact email, willingness to assume leadership, and organizational membership tier.
2. **Working Group Identity**: Working group title and a jargon-free, one-sentence plain language summary.
3. **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Articulation of the agentic AI gap or opportunity, justification of agent-specific relevance, and alignment with AAIF strategic priorities.
4. **Proposed Scope & Deliverables**: Work boundaries and planned tangible outputs, including technical whitepapers, architectural frameworks, benchmarks, open tooling, or policy guidance.
5. **Timeline & Structure**: Target meeting cadence, milestones, and operational duration within the standard 12 to 24 month charter lifecycle.
6. **Membership & Expertise**: Cross-functional expertise requirements and confirmed participant organizations.
7. **Impact & Urgency**: Industry necessity, measurable outcomes, and ecosystem urgency.
8. **Resource Considerations**: Infrastructure, repository, and operational support requirements from the Foundation.

# Lifecycle History
Formalized in March 2026 to govern working group intake, establishing membership-based submission rules and standardizing the 12–24 month charter lifecycle.[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]

# References
- Lifecycle Governance: [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md)
- Foundation Governance: [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing protocol-neutral capability maps, transaction lifecycle handoffs, and interoperability interfaces for AI-driven commerce.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical working group that catalogs, aligns, and harmonizes open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal, the group provides interoperability guidance and reference architectures across discovery, negotiation, cart validation, payment orchestration, and post-purchase lifecycles without authoring competing commerce protocols[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses strictly on interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns between agentic systems and the broader commerce stack, excluding underlying payment rail internals, fraud mitigation systems, and non-agentic legacy commerce[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

Key areas within scope include:
- **Discovery & Negotiation**: Interfaces governing offers, item availability, commercial terms, and fulfillment options between agents and merchants[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Cart & Checkout**: Cart composition, validation protocols, and transaction handoff mechanisms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Identity & Delegated Authority**: Buyer identity scoping, credential conveyance, and consent enforcement in collaboration with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Agentic Payments**: Intent signaling, authorization, and settlement interaction patterns across cards, instant rails, and on-chain systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Autonomy Boundaries & Oversight**: Alignment with governance primitives like the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and escalation mechanisms[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].
- **Post-Purchase Operations**: Order-status conveyance, claims, and dispute signaling interfaces[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History
The charter was formally ratified and approved on May 15, 2026, establishing its working methods and reporting path to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.description: Operational governance, editorial tone, submission workflows, and platform-specific policies governing official AAIF social media communication channels.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Social Media Governance and Guidelines define the Linux Foundation operational policies, editorial voice, content submission pathways, and brand compliance rules for official Agentic AI Foundation social media presences[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]. Foundation staff maintains final editorial and publishing control to protect consistency, accuracy, and project alignment across all official channels[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

# Architecture / Specification
Official social communication is designed for a global AI engineering and open-source audience, adhering to a neutral, professional, and inclusive tone across three primary channels[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]:
- **X**: Technical announcements, release notes, punchy updates, and threads[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].
- **LinkedIn**: Professional business discussions, member achievements, case studies, and strategic milestones[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].
- **Bluesky**: Conversational technical dialogue and community engagement[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

### Content Intake and Reposting Policies
Community and member contributions are routed via two dedicated intake pathways[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]:
1. **Direct Reposts**: Submitted through the designated AAIF Discord Social Amplification Channel for official releases, working group announcements, and Foundation-led events[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].
2. **Organic Content**: Submitted via the structured Foundation Content Intake Form to undergo editorial review[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

Promotional material, vendor product advertisements, personal code tips, consulting promotions, and unsolicited commercial campaigns are explicitly barred from Foundation reposting and publishing[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]. Community open-source projects are amplified only when directly demonstrating implementation of AAIF standards such as Model Context Protocol or Goose[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

# Lifecycle History
Established under Linux Foundation stewardship as the authoritative social media governance framework for the AAIF community[^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining intake requirements, maturity stages, progression criteria, and the annual review process for AAIF technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy defines the formal governance process by which open technical projects join the Agentic AI Foundation, advance across maturity stages, and undergo recurring annual review[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Governed by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the policy establishes objective expectations for licensing, governance transparency, community adoption, and infrastructure support across the project lifecycle[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Architecture / Specification

### Project Intake and Proposal Requirements
Proposals are submitted through the AAIF project proposals repository under an open intake schema[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Submissions require an OSI-approved permissive license, public repository hosting, automated public validation and release pipelines, an open issue tracker, identified maintainers, documented governance practices, dependency audits, and alignment statements with the AAIF mission[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

### Lifecycle Stages
Projects progress through defined stages reflecting maturity and operational independence[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- **Growth Stage**: Active technical projects demonstrating sustained development, clear adoption evidence, and alignment with AAIF architectural goals[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Impact Stage**: Production-grade reference implementations, protocols, and standard frameworks demonstrating cross-organizational governance, multi-vendor production adoption, and rigorous quality assurance[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].
- **Emeritus Stage**: Projects that are no longer maintained or exhibit little to no activity, preserving historical assets while relinquishing active foundation resources[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171][^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

Progression between stages and active status maintenance is evaluated annually by the Technical Committee against defined criteria[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Lifecycle History
Adopted effective March 18, 2026 as the formal technical project admission and governance framework for the foundation[^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]. Textual corrections to stage definitions and proposal schemas were incorporated via PR #30[^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for defining security architectures, threat models, design patterns, and privacy guardrails for autonomous agentic systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9] Following formal charter approval, the working group executes its mandate across specialized workstreams staffed by community contributors.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its technical outputs across several primary workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Develops architectural baselines and operational controls for mitigating prompt injection, tool abuse, and unintended autonomous side effects; coordinated under `../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Benchmarks agent threat surfaces against existing security standards (including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and NIST AI RMF) and coordinates closely with the cross-working-group taxonomy effort; tracked under `../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Codifies architectural mitigation patterns such as isolated execution, approval gates, and attestation mechanisms.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Provides repeatable review criteria to verify that specifications across other AAIF technical groups meet baseline security and privacy requirements.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Collaboration**: Coordinates with `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` to classify security guardrails, firewalls, and vulnerability enumerations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

## Operational Model
Workstream leadership operates on a self-selection model within dedicated channels, where leads coordinate asynchronous contributions and deliver bi-weekly meeting updates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-26**: Charter officially approved; working group shifted from initial formation to formal deliverable execution, with milestone delivery dates extended by approximately one month.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining application intake, Technical Committee voting thresholds, status labels, and lifecycle classification for AAIF foundation-hosted projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process establishes the operational workflow for open-source initiatives applying to become foundation-hosted projects within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6] It defines application submission mechanisms, issue triage states, voting thresholds within the `../governance/technical-committee.md`, and reapplication criteria aligned with `../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md`.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake and Triage Workflow
Applicants initiate the intake process by completing an issue form on the proposals repository following published submission guidelines.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6][^evt-project-proposals-pr-35] Each submission is tracked through designated issue labels:[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `New`: The proposal is logged and placed in the triage backlog.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers have requested supplementary technical or architectural details.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `Approved`: The project has received favorable TC and board votes for induction.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `Declined`: The proposal was evaluated and rejected with rationale documented in review comments.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `Too Early`: The project requires further maturation before re-evaluation.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]

## Evaluation and Voting Requirements
1. **Review Scheduling**: Candidates prepare a review presentation supported by AAIF staff and present during a scheduled Technical Committee meeting.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
2. **Stage Classification**: The Technical Committee classifies qualifying projects as either Growth or Impact status.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
3. **Voting Threshold**: Induction requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) of all Technical Committee members, followed by referral to the Governing Board for final authorization.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]

## Reapplication and Membership Terms
- **Reapplication Window**: Projects that are declined may submit a new proposal as soon as three months following the decision, provided tangible progress addressing feedback is demonstrated.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- **Membership Decoupling**: Project hosting does not require contributing organizations to hold AAIF membership, nor does project acceptance confer corporate membership tier status or Governing Board seats.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an open catalog and classification schema mapping emerging and established technologies across the agentic ecosystem.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8] Governed within `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`, the landscape structures tools, frameworks, and protocols across seven operational categories aligned directly with AAIF technical working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

# Architecture / Specification

## Taxonomy Category Alignment
The catalog maps ecosystem entries across seven core functional domains:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]
1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Autonomous agent frameworks and orchestration runtimes; aligns with `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md` and `../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Inter-agent communication protocols and discovery registries; aligns with `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Defensive runtime controls, policy proxies, and model firewalls; aligns with `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Telemetry pipelines, distributed traces, and execution logging; aligns with `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Autonomous payment rails, cryptographic wallets, and transaction interfaces; aligns with `../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Compliance frameworks and regulatory tracking; aligns with `../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Benchmark suites, adversarial testing harnesses, and scoring frameworks; aligns with `../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]

## Project Attribution Schema
Entries in `landscape.yml` are categorized by provenance and integration status, distinguishing member projects from external open-source or proprietary components with associated repositories and homepages.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for defining security architectures, threat models, design pattern catalogs, and review checklists for autonomous and agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group produces baseline defensive specifications and security guidance across AAIF projects.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables into four core active workstreams alongside cross-cutting foundation liaison roles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:

- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing operational review standards and security criteria applied across AAIF work products.
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg, maintaining the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guidelines.
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating threats and mapping gap analyses across industry AI security frameworks.
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Sagar Dashora and Dan Kommatas, maintaining architectural security patterns such as attested execution and runtime control gates.

The working group also maintains direct representation in the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md), appointing Jay White and Katherine Druckman as designated delegates [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Governance and Operations
The group operates under an asynchronous monthly reporting model to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) through GitHub pull requests [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Workstream leads coordinate contributors using interest rosters and communicate via dedicated foundation channels.
