proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, multi-agent observability models, and reasoning frameworks for agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body dedicated to developing vendor-neutral observability conventions, telemetry interchange standards, and execution tracing architectures for agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group operates under the governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].

# Architecture / Specification
Technical initiatives within the working group are organized into targeted focus groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]:

- **Observability and Multi-Agentic Systems**: Led by Ty, focusing on distributed interaction traces and cross-agent execution telemetry.
- **Observability and Protocols**: Led by Matthew Lee, standardizing boundary telemetry propagation across protocols such as MCP and tool invocation interfaces.
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Led by Pavan Sudheendra in coordination with Richard and Kevin, developing evaluation and tracing frameworks for internal reasoning steps.

The working group participates actively in the foundation's cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to ensure consistent vocabulary across tracing and telemetry definitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

# Governance and Operations
The group conducts asynchronous review and document management primarily via GitHub pull requests and issues, transitioning away from external documents for formal specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. Progress reports are filed monthly using a standardized template in the working group repository, submitted via pull requests that are reviewed by the Technical Committee with a 7-day review window [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].

mutations.rationale: Record confirmed working group co-chairs and monthly reporting procedures to the Technical Committee based on the adopted reporting template.

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group aligning agentic AI architectures and lifecycle standards with global regulations, risk management frameworks, and compliance policies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body focused on aligning autonomous agent architectures, verification records, and deployment practices with international AI regulations and enterprise risk management standards [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. The working group is chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase) under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).

# Governance and Operations
The working group maintains its operational reporting through a standardized monthly report template committed to its repository [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-4]. Reports are submitted as GitHub pull requests directed to the Technical Committee by the final business day of each reporting period, with an established seven-calendar-day review window prior to merging.

The working group collaborates across technical domains to translate statutory requirements, risk controls, and compliance constraints into actionable specifications such as evidence records, human-in-the-loop gates, and audit trails.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream establishing unified agentic AI terminology, classification schemas, and ecosystem landscape mappings through inter-working-group delegates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation initiative tasked with defining canonical terminology, resolving conflicting definitions, and maintaining ecosystem landscape datasets [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]. Coordinated by Junjie Bu, the workstream serves all AAIF technical committees and working groups by providing a decoupled, version-controlled terminology framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream relies on designated delegates appointed from each active AAIF working group to review proposed terms, reconcile conceptual overlaps, and validate domain-specific vocabularies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7]:

- **Inter-Group Delegations**: Working groups such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) (represented by Jay White and Katherine Druckman) and the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](observability-and-traceability.md) provide domain subject matter expertise for definitions and taxonomy harmonization [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].
- **Decoupled Knowledge Artifacts**: Concepts and landscape mappings are maintained as structured, machine-readable data files and documentation managed via GitHub pull requests open to all community contributors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Governance and Operations
Participation is open across the AAIF community, while formal alignment is sustained through synchronous coordination between working group delegates and asynchronous review across repository pull requests [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-59470fc828ab-4b9461f7].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) body responsible for establishing unified terminology, classification schemas, and ecosystem landscapes for agentic AI architectures[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32]. The workstream is co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Reporting Cadence

The workstream operates under the governance of the AAIF Technical Committee ([`technical-committee`](../governance/technical-committee.md)) and reports monthly on its operational status and deliverables[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32]:

- **Reporting Schema**: Standardized reports document monthly progress against objectives, blockers and operational risks, formal decisions requested from the Technical Committee, and next-month focal areas.

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, security design patterns, and privacy guardrails for autonomous agent architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee body chartered to evaluate agent-specific threat models, define operational security patterns, and develop verification frameworks across multi-agent environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. The group investigates boundary enforcement, credential delegation, prompt injection isolation, and tool invocation vulnerabilities.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group operates under explicit repository and deliverable governance rules[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]:
- **Deliverable Lifecycle**: Deliverables enter as draft files prefixed with `DRAFT-` and cannot transition to final status without an explicit approval decision recorded in formal working group meeting notes[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]. Artifacts handed off to cross-working-group initiatives are preserved in place as redirects marked `Moved`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].
- **Workstreams**:
  - **Threat Modeling**: Co-led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), this workstream assesses frameworks including CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF against agent-specific threats such as multi-agent persuasion, delegated authorization boundaries, and prompt/tool supply-chain integrity, feeding findings into the Design Patterns Catalog and Best Practices Guide[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
  - **Taxonomy Integration**: The group delegates Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) to represent security and privacy terminology inside the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Lifecycle History
The working group maintains its charter under `charter/DRAFT.md` pending formal working group approval[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]. On 2026-06-22, the working group's initial *Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions* deliverable was formally moved to the cross-WG Taxonomy and Landscape repository[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling evaluation benchmarking OWASP, NIST AI RMF, and CSA MAESTRO against agentic AI threat vectors.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a technical guidance document and comparative evaluation conducted by the AAIF [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. The initiative evaluates existing security frameworks to determine whether standard AI guidance adequately addresses autonomous agent behaviors or if agent-specific security gaps necessitate dedicated architectural framework specifications[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Architecture / Specification
The analysis benchmarks prominent existing AI security frameworks—including Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) MAESTRO, OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, and NIST AI RMF—against critical agentic threat dimensions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]:
- **Multi-Agent Persuasion**: Deception, collusion, and unauthorized social influence between cooperating or competing subagents.
- **Tool Invocation Risks**: Exploitation of runtime function calling, parameter tampering, and unexpected lateral API movement.
- **Delegated Authorization Boundaries**: Privilege escalation across agent execution hops and token delegation chains.
- **Supply-Chain Integrity**: Verification of system prompt integrity, model provenance, and tool manifest authenticity.

Findings directly inform the AAIF Design Patterns Catalog and [Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream is co-led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), with contributions from Capsule, Twilio, Semiotic AI, IBM, Global Payments, Huawei, Ericsson, and TELUS[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative establishing unified terminology, classification taxonomies, and architectural landscape maps across all working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. Operating across working group boundaries, it provides a centralized venue for resolving terminology conflicts and publishing shared conceptual definitions via pull requests[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream coordinates delegates designated by participating AAIF technical working groups to maintain decoupled data and consistent cross-domain definitions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]:
- **Leadership**: Chaired by Junjie Bu[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- **Working Group Delegation**: Individual working groups appoint formal delegates to review and resolve nomenclature proposals; the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) delegates are Jay White (Microsoft) and Katherine Druckman (JetBrains)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].
- **Decoupled Governance**: Taxonomy updates are maintained in a standalone repository (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`) with open participation across working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

# Lifecycle History
Following decisions recorded in June 2026, standalone working group taxonomy efforts—including the Security and Privacy Working Group's Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions—were officially merged into this cross-WG initiative on 2026-06-22[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) develops vendor-neutral threat frameworks, architectural design patterns, and baseline security controls for agentic AI deployments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] Operating both as a technical deliverable body and as an intersecting horizontal review layer across the Agentic AI Foundation, the working group audits emergent standards and provides builders with practical hardening guidance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical outputs into distinct workstreams, each defined by designated charter directories and leadership assignments:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]

- **Threat Modeling (`threat-modeling/`)**: Conducts systematic gap analyses benchmarking established AI threat frameworks—such as OWASP, NIST AI RMF, and CSA MAESTRO—against agentic risks including autonomous tool escalation, goal drift, and memory poisoning.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5] This near-term deliverable directly feeds downstream design patterns and best practice guidelines.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]
- **Design Patterns Catalog (`design-patterns/`)**: Curates reusable patterns formatted with problem, context, solution, trade-offs, and accompanying anti-patterns.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4] Focus topics include hooks and checkpointing, human-in-the-loop patterns, privacy-preserving execution (zero-knowledge proofs, trusted execution environments, encrypted vector databases), blast radius containment, secure memory lifecycles, runtime intervention (kill switches, rollback mechanisms, permission downgrades, off-task detection), and agent authorization models.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4] The workstream is led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]
- **Best Practices Guide (`best-practices/`)**: Provides prescriptive builder guidance pairing implementation standards with curated external framework references.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55] Subject areas include secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation suites, and post-incident forensics.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55] Led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist (`review-checklist/`)**: Defines an operational review checklist inspecting sibling working group deliverables through a security and privacy lens.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54] Initial review targets comprise [Identity & Trust](./identity-and-trust.md) (agent identity and delegated authorization), [Observability & Traceability](./observability-and-traceability.md) (behavioral anomaly detection and audit logging), and [Agentic Commerce](./agentic-commerce.md) (payments guardrails, fund draining prevention, account isolation).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54] Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]
- **Taxonomy (`taxonomy/`)**: Originating within the SP WG, the terminology drafting initiative transitioned into the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape](./taxonomy-and-landscape.md) effort, with ongoing representation from SP WG delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]

# Lifecycle History

The formal workstream taxonomy and leadership structure was established via pull request #5 in `aaif/wg-security-and-privacy`.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Practical implementation guidance and external framework alignment for agent secrets, tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation, and forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a practitioner-facing standard developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55] While the related design patterns catalog details exact structural implementations, this guide addresses high-level architectural recommendations and points builders to validated external security frameworks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

# Architecture / Specification

The guidance is organized around five core operational areas and an external reference index:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

- **Secrets Management**: Safe provisioning, storage, credential isolation, and ephemeral rotation for agent tool use.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Boundary validation, schema-enforced parameters, and out-of-band authorization checks on downstream function calls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
- **Guardrails**: Input and output policy boundaries, runtime prompt filtering, and behavioral bounding constraints.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
- **Evaluation Frameworks**: Automated harness criteria and regression suites measuring agent compliance against known adversarial scenarios.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
- **Post-Incident Forensics**: Behavioral trace analysis, cryptographic action reconstruction, and blast radius auditing after an operational anomaly or breach.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]
- **Curated External References**: Direct mapping to recognized third-party security frameworks rather than redundant bespoke definitions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

# Lifecycle History

The workstream is led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) under the Security and Privacy Working Group governance.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55]

# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape workstream is a foundation-wide initiative responsible for standardizing agentic AI terminology and harmonizing conflicting definitions across all AAIF working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] Centralized in the `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` repository on github.com, it manages structured terminology schemas and coordinates review slices across domain-specific working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4]

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates as an asynchronous coordination vehicle supported by weekly 30-minute sync meetings:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]

- **Cross-WG Representation**: Individual working groups appoint formal delegates to resolve linguistic divergences and review domain terms. For example, the [Security and Privacy Working Group](./security-and-privacy.md) appointed Jay White and Katherine Druckman as standing delegates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]
- **Review Slices and Priority Schema**: Contributing working groups evaluate terminology through prioritized section JSON slices (e.g., `s03-boundaries`, `s04-core`, `s05-reliability-dimensions`, `s06-governance`, `s07-grounding`, `s08-failure`, `s09-metrics`, `s10-ecosystem`, `s11-response`) using priority bands (`p0`, `p1`, `p2`) and custom review fields.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4]

# Lifecycle History

The taxonomy effort began as a deliverable draft inside the Security and Privacy Working Group before being elevated to an AAIF-wide initiative on 2026-05-12.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86] Junjie Bu was appointed workstream lead on 2026-05-26, and delegate appointments were finalized in June 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee body chartered to establish threat models, security best practice guides, runtime security design patterns, and cross-working-group review mechanisms for autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9] The group coordinates with external standards and industry efforts, including OWASP ASI, IETF, AARM, and MCP ACS, to harmonize agent security terminology and controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group executes its charter through four core workstreams and dedicated taxonomy delegates:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, benchmarking agentic threats across OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing actionable security architecture guidance for agent developers and platform operators.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, defining modular architectural defense patterns for agent isolation and boundary controls.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing operational review gates across peer AAIF deliverables.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Represented by delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman collaborating with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) lead Junjie Bu on agent archetypes and capability mapping.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the AAIF opened the working group's GitHub repository to the public and designated GitHub as the official system of record for maturing and final deliverables while retaining early brainstorming collaboration tools.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9] The working group also established regular monthly reporting to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) operating on a 7-day review acknowledgment cycle.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling evaluation benchmarking OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF against agentic failure modes and boundary risks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is an evaluative report and framework artifact produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to assess existing security frameworks against agent-specific threat vectors.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9] Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, the analysis evaluates cross-framework coverage across OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Architecture / Specification
The gap analysis methodology correlates framework controls against agentic behavioral primitives, tool execution environments, and multi-agent interaction boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9] Key threat areas cataloged and expanded within the report include:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Memory and Context Poisoning**: Corruption of short-term conversational context, persistent agent memory, or retrieval stores to manipulate agent outputs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Multi-Agent Persuasion and Sabotage**: Adversarial subversion, coercion between agents, or rogue agent emergence leading to compromised execution chains.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Tool Invocation and Excessive Agency**: Unchecked capability execution, lack of blast-radius containment, and unconstrained action execution without human validation gates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Delegated Authorization Boundaries**: Privilege escalation across chained tool integrations, credential forwarding failures, and protocol boundaries such as the Model Context Protocol.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- **Supply Chain Integrity and Transaction Risks**: Vulnerabilities in agent plugins, skill definitions, and risks surrounding commerce and automated payment delegation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, initial report drafts covering Deliverables 2 and 4 were presented to the Security and Privacy Working Group and committed to GitHub as Markdown source records, incorporating empirical vulnerability data such as prompt injection discoveries in tool descriptors and deterministic policy enforcement models.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing vendor-neutral telemetry standards, execution trace schemas, and cross-boundary correlation protocols for AI agent workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4] The group maintains OpenTelemetry alignment guardrails, ensuring that AAIF telemetry proposals function as clean extensions rather than replacements for existing OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its investigations across four technical focus groups and associated telemetry planes:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
- **LLM Primitives**: Led by Zayne, conducting landscape surveys and gap analyses for model invocation telemetry, token usage, and inference events, targeting an audit combining primitive and protocol streams.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]
- **Agent State and Context**: Investigating agent state retention, graph memory, context degradation, and academic landscape patterns, spearheaded by Sergey and Govind.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Analyzing multi-agent dispatch, coordination handoffs, and distributed workflow topologies.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Evaluating white-box tracing, planning graphs, and internal reasoning steps in collaboration with external research inputs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

The group coordinates with the central [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream on core observable terms and planes (orchestration, execution, protocol, and reasoning/context planes).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the working group opened its GitHub repository and issue tracker publicly to support focus group kanban boards and deliverable milestone tracking.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4] The group instituted bi-weekly community presentation sessions and began formal monthly status reporting to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry framework capturing agent reasoning paths, state transitions, execution records, and outcome effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model (ABTM) is a vendor-neutral observability specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to record the execution structure, reasoning processes, and environmental effects of AI agents.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10] The model provides an explicit crosswalk between runtime observation planes and telemetry trace dimensions while preserving strict alignment guardrails with OpenTelemetry standards.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

# Architecture / Specification
The specification organizes agent telemetry across three principal behavioral dimensions mapped to underlying system planes:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
- **Execution Structure**: Traces orchestration, task delegation, and tool invocation sequences across orchestration and execution planes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
- **Reasoning and Planning**: Records cognitive trajectories, prompt assembly, intermediate deliberations, and state evaluations occurring across the reasoning and context planes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]
- **Outcomes and Effects**: Captures tool return payloads, state mutations, and external protocol boundaries across the protocol and execution planes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

The model acts as an extension layer over existing standards rather than replacing existing OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, establishing strict boundaries between general application telemetry and agent-specific behavioral traces.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10]

# Lifecycle History
In mid-2026, the working group initiated a structured 12-month decision process governing ABTM adoption.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12] Under this evaluation plan, the group assesses existing candidates against use-case inventories and gap analysis findings to determine whether to adopt an existing open standard, extend an existing project, or publish a new normative specification only when critical gaps cannot be resolved upstream.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Meeting Notes Agent Instructions
proposed_concept.description: Operational instructions and communication standards governing automated agent meeting notes generation and repository contributions in the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape workstream maintains standardized instructions for automated agents and contributors generating meeting notes and submitting repository text[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]. Managed within the workstream's meeting documentation, these rules govern file naming conventions, template processing workflows, empty section retention, and conversational tone across all repository activities in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].

# Architecture / Specification

### File Naming and Workflow

Notes are generated from `TEMPLATE.md` and saved using the date pattern `YYYY-MM-DD.md`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]. The agent generation sequence requires eight discrete steps:
1. Copy `TEMPLATE.md` to a new date-stamped file[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
2. Update the document heading date[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
3. Populate the Resources section with links to AI summaries, transcripts, and recordings[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
4. Detail the subjects covered under Topics Discussed[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
5. Document formal decisions or mark "None." if none occurred[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
6. Record expected outputs under Deliverables or mark "None." if none occurred[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
7. Construct the Action Items table with owner attribution, descriptions, and due dates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
8. Insert a row at the top of the `README.md` table beneath the header to preserve reverse chronological order, including a link to the full notes and a 1–2 sentence topic summary[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].

### Editorial Constraints

Documentation must adhere to concise bullet points rather than narrative paragraphs, limit topic descriptions to 1–2 sentences, and explicitly attribute action items to individuals[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]. Empty sections must retain their heading and state "None." to ensure consistent document schemas across meetings[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].

### Repository Communication Style

Agents and contributors interacting with the repository—including documentation drafting, commit messages, pull request summaries, and issue responses—must adhere to strict style guidelines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea]:
- Avoid contrastive language[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
- Avoid using horizontal rules for visual line breaks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
- Eliminate sycophantic framing[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
- Maintain directness without relying on partial clauses[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
- Formulate complete thoughts that flow naturally[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].
- Maintain a neutral voice balancing playful tone with professional conduct[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eb9c68e792e7-e45bd7ea].

These automated interaction standards complement the schema routing provided by the [Taxonomy Contributions Skill](../skills/taxonomy-contributions.md).

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing measurement frameworks, failure taxonomies, evaluation protocols, and resilient architecture patterns for enterprise agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) by standardizing benchmarks, measurement frameworks, and engineering patterns required for autonomous AI agents to operate accurately and reliably in enterprise environments.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44] Agentic workloads are fundamentally non-deterministic, creating operational risk when deployments lack visibility into quality drift and failure boundaries.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]

Chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the ARWG focuses on classifying agent failure modes, specifying proactive resilience mechanisms such as verification loops, and defining recovery patterns including safe-state rollbacks and human intervention handoffs.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44] [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

# Scope and Governance

### In Scope
- **Accuracy and Reliability Frameworks**: Defining evaluation dimensions, performance metrics, failure mode catalogs, and quality thresholds for autonomous and semi-autonomous systems.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]
- **Reliable Architecture Patterns**: Specifying architectural patterns including verification loops, deterministic gates, and grounding mechanisms tied to authoritative systems of record.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]
- **Recovery and Corrective Actions**: Formulating standards for safe-state restoration, compensatory workflows, rollback mechanisms, and criteria for human escalation.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]

### Out of Scope
- **Model Training and Internals**: Foundation model training, weights, fine-tuning, and prompt engineering are excluded; agents and multi-agent systems are evaluated holistically.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]
- **Telemetry Emission Mechanics**: Specification of physical trace and log emission formats is delegated to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]
- **Commercial Tooling and Production Runtimes**: Production guardrail software and commercial runtime engines are not maintained by the group.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]
- **Regulatory Policy**: Sector-specific legal compliance rules are excluded in favor of technical evaluation frameworks.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]

### Deliverables and Working Tracks
The canonical deliverable structure encompasses items D1 through D6 and internal item I1:[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]
- **D1 (Accuracy and Reliability Vocabulary & Framing)**: Theoretical architectural frame defining evaluation subjects, output quality, reliability dimensions, observability signals, grounding, and root causes.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis & Benchmark Survey)**: Applied evidence report evaluating enterprise persona requirements (PMs, ops, evaluators), tooling gaps, and interoperability blockers across production B2B use cases.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- **D6 (Evaluation Protocols)**: Standardized testing harness and evaluation methodology seeded from D2 gap findings.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-15**: Working group charter formally approved by the AAIF Technical Committee.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]
- **2026-06-22**: Appointed delegates and coordinated term harmonizations with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
- **2026-06-29**: Delivered first monthly progress report following charter adoption; established alternating schedule of biweekly plenary meetings and deliverable working sessions.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]
- **2026-06-30**: Consolidated deliverable taxonomy across charter documents (D1–D6, I1).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44] [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream coordinates definition alignment and ecosystem mapping across all Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] It prevents siloed terminology, resolves contradictory definitions across technical domains, and catalogs agent frameworks, runtimes, protocols, and developer tools.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]

The workstream operates via a decoupled architecture that pairs a public ecosystem landscape directory with a git-backed, schema-validated taxonomy knowledge repository.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] Technical terms and classifications are reviewed collaboratively with designated delegates and domain editors from each technical working group, including the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](accuracy-and-reliability.md).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]

# Architecture and Operating Model

### Schema and Metadata Standards
- **CNCF-Style Schema**: Baseline taxonomy entries adopt standard cloud-native metadata schemas to record term identifiers, relationships, versions, and contributor citations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
- **Dual-Tier Definitions**: To resolve ambiguity across technical audiences, every taxonomy definition mandates both a concise summary (L0) and an in-depth descriptive scope note (L1/L2).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **Landscape Federation**: The workstream's directory model integrates member-driven projects and external ecosystem projects within unified landscape tooling hosted by the foundation.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]

### Working Group Delegate Governance
- **Delegate Model**: Working group chairs designate official liaisons to review overlapping definitions, validate domain concepts, and establish shared boundaries around core primitives such as autonomous agents.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]
- **PR-Driven Workflow**: Contributions and amendments follow an asynchronous, pull-request-driven review model backed by standardized meeting records and shared review trackers.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-32390fa5133a-785f207f]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-01**: Formally adopted the asynchronous PR contribution model, CNCF-style metadata schemas, and landscape web integration strategy.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]
- **2026-06-22**: Approved cross-working-group review workflows, credentialed group delegates, and initiated joint census on universal cross-domain agent terms.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation body chartered to eliminate siloed terminology, unify conceptual definitions across working groups, and maintain an authoritative directory of agentic AI ecosystem components.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream operates under formal charter approval from the foundation's participating technical working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# Operational Structure and Processes

## Governance and Delegate Model
The workstream coordinates across domain working groups by onboarding one to two official delegates per group to drive terminology curation and conflict resolution.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1] Term definitions follow an asynchronous, PR-driven workflow where proposed additions require sign-off from designated domain editors.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] To prevent early fragmentation, initial seed terms were cleared in June 2026 to re-evaluate submissions through a unified review spreadsheet before authoring pull requests.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

## Schemas and External Alignment
The workstream implements the SKOS-Lite data schema for terminology classification and adopts the CNCF landscape tool format for ecosystem mapping.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] Terminology development requires alignment with established international frameworks, specifically ISO and NIST standards, requiring documented justifications for any deviations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90] The workstream also publishes an automated web portal via GitHub Actions CI/CD to visualize taxonomy and ecosystem landscape artifacts.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# Lifecycle History

- **May 2026**: Workstream kickoff held; established SKOS-Lite and CNCF schema directions, weekly sync cadence, and the domain editor review model.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]
- **June 2026**: Charter finalized and approved across working groups; local portal and publishing pipeline deployed; initial batches of 10–20 core terms gathered per working group for consolidated pre-PR conflict review.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# Related Concepts

- Working group oversight: [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- Domain collaborators: [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) evaluates policy requirements, risk management baselines, and legal constraints governing agentic AI deployments across global jurisdictions.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454] Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the working group harmonizes technical artifacts across the foundation with statutory frameworks such as the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO governance standards.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

# Operational Focus and Deliverables

## Policy and Framework Mapping
The working group establishes baseline reference mappings evaluating how existing public policy frameworks, regulatory guidance, and international risk benchmarks apply to autonomous AI workflows.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454] In June 2026, the working group concluded its initial three-month landscape assessment cataloging relevant agentic AI policy frameworks and standard specifications.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

## Comparative Gap Analysis
Following the completion of the landscape catalog, the working group initiated a three-month sprint focused on comparative gap analysis.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454] The effort identifies disparities between external statutory baselines and agent runtime requirements, identifying operational areas where standard controls fail to cover multi-step agent delegation and runtime tool execution.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

# Lifecycle History

- **June 2026**: Completed three-month landscape assessment of policy frameworks, regulatory guidance documents, and industry standards; initiated three-month sprint on comparative gap analysis.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a17a580f85c2-e56de454]

# Related Concepts

- Governance: [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- Cross-cutting terminology: [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- Policy patterns: [Hard-Constraint Gate](../patterns/hard-constraint-gate.md) and [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, execution logging, and boundary tracing frameworks across agentic software stacks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2] Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group coordinates with other foundation initiatives to provide comprehensive visibility into language model primitives, runtime protocols, and inter-agent coordination.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical scope into five specialized focus groups led by designated coordinators:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

- **LLM Primitives Observability**: Tracing baseline model invocations, prompt-response dynamics, and token-level operations.
- **Protocol Observability**: Standardizing telemetry capture across agent interfaces, client integrations, and transport protocols like MCP.
- **Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination)**: Capturing topology, delegation chains, and swarm interactions across autonomous agents.
- **Agentic State and Context**: Tracking memory lifecycle, context assembly, and persistent state transitions.
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Emitting and structuring reasoning paths, decision branch metadata, and execution traces.

The group develops core baseline deliverables including an Agentic Observability Use Case document and a landscape Gap Analysis evaluating current industry tooling against multi-agent requirements.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2] It also partners directly with the cross-cutting workstream [Taxonomy and Landscape](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to harmonize observability nomenclature across the foundation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

# Lifecycle History
The working group initiated operational execution on its charter deliverables in June 2026, launching its focus groups, establishing transparent tracking via GitHub issues and discussions, and submitting its initial monthly review to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation tasked with creating shared conceptual models, canonical vocabulary, and an ecosystem catalog for autonomous agents.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e] Led by Junjie Bu, the workstream synthesizes cross-group contributions through appointed working group delegates to ensure uniform nomenclature across all foundation technical outputs.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream manages terminology intake and validation through a centralized review workflow targeting an initial v1.0 vocabulary release:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]

- **Terminology Intake**: Each AAIF technical working group submits 10–20 core domain terms to populate a unified working spreadsheet.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]
- **Delegate Engagement**: Accredited delegates from groups such as [Security and Privacy](security-and-privacy.md) and [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) annotate terms with relevance, feedback, and boundary recommendations.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]
- **Consensus Culling and Debate**: Terms are marked with status designations including LGTM, debate, or cull candidates to remove generic software jargon and preserve agent-specific semantics.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]
- **Universal Classification**: Terms applying broadly across domains (e.g., baseline agent definitions, identity) are elevated to a primary universal section pinned at the top of the index.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]

# Lifecycle History
Kickoff was held on 2026-05-21 to adopt a PR-driven taxonomy workflow and align with the existing landscape project.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2] Following charter confirmation in late June 2026, the workstream entered an active review phase in July 2026, establishing dedicated spreadsheet instructions, consensus tracking columns, and one-hour weekly sync meetings to finalize the v1.0 release candidates.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes threat models, defense architectures, security patterns, and audit guidelines for agentic artificial intelligence systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d] Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group coordinates technical safeguards across foundation workstreams and aligns with external security and standards bodies.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its commitments around four primary deliverables:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, evaluating agent vulnerabilities across eight core functional areas against established frameworks including MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices**: Co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, providing actionable security guidelines for agent secret handling, tool invocation guardrails, and runtime sandboxing.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns**: Co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, defining reusable, verifiable architectural design patterns for secure agent interactions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing systematic security and privacy verification criteria for deliverables emitted by other AAIF working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]

In addition, the group appoints delegates (Jay White and Katherine Druckman) to the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define security-specific vocabulary, such as distinguishing "Agent Card" from "Agent Blueprint" and refining the boundaries between bots and agents.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]

# Lifecycle History
The group operates under an asynchronous monthly reporting cadence to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), wherein monthly updates are submitted as pull requests by the final business day of the month with a 7-day review window.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28] In July 2026, the group advanced deliverables in threat modeling and security best practices while actively pursuing coordination with external initiatives including OWASP, AARM, ETSI TC SAI, and the Linux Foundation FINOS AI framework.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for defining threat models, defense architectures, and implementation best practices across autonomous agent systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d] Chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), the group establishes foundational security guardrails and cross-ecosystem alignment with external standards organizations.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical output across five active workstreams supported by dedicated documentation structures:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

- **Threat Modeling**: Focuses on authoring and refining the [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), benchmarking agent failure modes against frameworks like OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **Best Practices**: Develops the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md), formulating concrete guidance for credential management, boundary containment, and tool authorization.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **Cross-WG Taxonomy Coordination**: Terminology efforts were transitioned to the foundation-wide [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as delegates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

# Governance / Operations
Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group maintains open repositories and holds regular bi-weekly synchronization meetings.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d] Operational items include:

- **Ecosystem Liaison**: Actively seeking Technical Committee guidance on the scope and posture of formal coordination with external bodies such as OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **Resource Constraints**: General member and lead availability remains a standing operational risk, pacing deliverable timelines and milestone schedules.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to curate and maintain a unified glossary of agentic AI definitions and an interactive ecosystem map.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b] Approved on June 21, 2026, and led by Chair Junjie Bu (Google) and Co-Chair Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream ensures all AAIF working groups share common terminology and avoid duplicated ecosystem research.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream structures foundational agent concepts and industry landscapes through standardized machine-readable models and automated delivery:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]

- **SKOS-Lite Vocabulary Schema**: Glossary terms are standardized using `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, and `contrastsWith` fields, ingested into a consolidated data repository (`taxonomy-data.js`).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Ecosystem Architecture Map**: Maintained via a living `landscape.yml` conforming to CNCF Landscape 2 conventions, grouping ecosystem tools and platforms through delegate consensus.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Automated Web Publishing**: A GitHub Actions workflow (`deploy-pages.yml`) compiles static distributions of the interactive Shared Taxonomy Explorer and Landscape Map to GitHub Pages, injecting build timestamps and hosting assets.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]

# Governance / Operations
The workstream relies on federated governance across vertical working groups:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

- **Domain Editors**: Each vertical working group (such as [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)) nominates two active delegates to participate in weekly Monday syncs and asynchronous pull request reviews.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Scope Guardrails**: The workstream governs cross-cutting horizontal definitions and high-level ecosystem categorizations, while domain-specific vertical specifications, legal analyses, and protocol standards remain under their respective technical working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry, distributed tracing, and execution observability frameworks across autonomous agents and multi-agent systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5] The group works to align runtime telemetry specifications with industry standards such as [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) and establish cross-boundary auditability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

# Architecture / Specification
The group coordinates technical domains across several focus areas:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

- **Protocols and Primitives**: Focus groups covering protocols and primitives merged to unify the technical language and streamline runtime interface definitions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]
- **Decentralized and P2P Agent Telemetry**: Evaluates peer-to-peer network observability (such as libp2p, Lumina, and IETF initiatives including Agent Proto, DMSC, and Dawn) across multi-cloud deployments, examining trace context propagation, Server-Sent Events (SSE), and cryptographic payload attestation in collaboration with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]
- **Resource Discovery**: Evaluates proposal pipelines for agent skills and [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

# Governance / Operations
- **Taxonomy Harmonization**: The group systematically reviews domain terms alphabetically against the foundation-wide taxonomy maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), advancing foundational observability definitions to universal status.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]
- **Contribution Policy**: Operating under interim guidance pending Governing Council review, external repository contributions are temporarily restricted while internal focus groups align foundational specifications.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing the standards, benchmarks, and engineering methodologies required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under enterprise conditions.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019] The group investigates failure modes, outcome correctness, multi-turn consistency, and operational robustness across production agent deployments.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

# Governance and Operations
The working group is led by Chair Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Co-Chair Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), who were appointed by Platinum and Gold members for a term running from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019] Meetings take place biweekly on Tuesdays at 9:00 AM PT.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019] Operational communication occurs via the public mailing list (`wg-accuracy-reliability@lists.aaif.io`) and a dedicated Discord channel.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

# Deliverables and Workstreams
- **D1 (Terminology and Methodology Support):** A foundational methodology deliverable establishing literature grounding and structured terminology across accuracy and reliability dimensions, contributed to the cross-working group taxonomy in collaboration with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis):** A practitioner-oriented gap analysis categorizing personas, enterprise requirements, and actionable hurdles blocking production agent adoption, supported by targeted industry surveys.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]
- **Inter-Group Liaisons:** Active coordination with related working groups, including the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e]

# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group bridges global AI policy, regulatory developments, and compliance requirements with technical standards developed across the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673] The group provides policy translation, governance frameworks, and risk evaluation guidelines to ensure agentic architectures remain compliant with emerging international legislation.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]

# Governance and Operations
The working group is chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) alongside Co-Chair Deborah Eng (JP Morgan Chase), appointed by Platinum and Gold foundation members for a term spanning March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673] Regular working group meetings occur biweekly on Thursdays at 10:00 AM PT.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673] Public discussions and technical inquiries are conducted over the working group mailing list (`wg-governance-risk-regulatory@lists.aaif.io`) and Discord.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]

# Scope and Technical Alignment
The group operates under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and collaborates with peer technical working groups including the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define common compliance concepts, boundary controls, and audit models.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-b33563055168-432cf673]

# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group catalogs, aligns, and harmonizes open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563] Maintaining strict protocol neutrality, the working group focuses on shared interoperability guidance across agent-led discovery, negotiation, checkout, payment orchestration, and post-purchase interactions rather than publishing competing commerce protocols.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

# Governance and Operations
The working group is led by Chair Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Co-Chair Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), appointed by Platinum and Gold members for the March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 term.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563] Formal meetings convene biweekly on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM PT.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563] Collaboration and asynchronous communication occur via the public mailing list (`wg-agentic-commerce@lists.aaif.io`) and the community Discord channel.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

# Coordination and Reporting
The working group reports directly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), recommending paths forward and highlighting industry convergence across external specifications while participating alongside peer technical initiatives such as the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group establishes a shared workflow execution model, common primitives, and operational design patterns enabling AI agents to coordinate across tools, frameworks, and enterprise runtime environments.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56] The group standardizes vendor-neutral abstractions for multi-step agent tasks, long-running stateful workflows, and reliable external system invocations.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Governance and Operations
The charter for the working group was formally approved on May 13, 2026 and last updated on July 23, 2026.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56] Primary leadership consists of Chair Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Co-Chair Adam Seligman (Workato).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Technical Scope
The working group focuses on three core domains:
- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics:** Developing standardized terminology and representations for [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md), including tasks, branching, subagent handoffs, and deterministic translation layers.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution:** Formulating architecture patterns for execution resilience across minutes, hours, or days, incorporating workflow-level audit systems, state persistence, idempotency, and replayable failure recovery.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Tool Invocation and External System Coordination:** Defining standardized patterns for coordinating agent interactions with APIs, command-line interfaces, and enterprise backends, operating distinctly from runtime trace telemetry handled by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing protocol-neutral capability models, payment handlers, and boundary trust signals for automated agent transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body tasked with cataloging and harmonizing protocol-neutral specifications for automated agent commerce, delegated authority, checkout, and payment orchestration [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]. Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group establishes standardized interfaces and capability models spanning discovery, purchasing, payment processing, fraud signaling, and post-purchase workflows across heterogeneous agent platforms and merchant boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's foundational deliverable is the Agentic Commerce Capability Map, standardizing protocol-neutral interfaces across six transaction phases [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]:
- Discovery: Static capability discovery and transaction-specific merchant eligibility.
- Delegated Authority: Representation of shopper consent, delegation scopes, and intent binding.
- Checkout: Cart assembly, context exchange, and wallet or custom-method attachments.
- Payment: Decoupled payment processing partitioned into handlers, instruments, and credentials.
- Fraud Signaling: Portable trust signals and context propagation across merchant and risk engines.
- Post-Purchase: Receipts, status coordination, and fulfillment tracking.

### Payment Handler Abstractions
The working group models agentic payments around three reusable abstractions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]:
1. Handler: The runtime execution mechanism or gateway coordinating transaction flow.
2. Instrument: The payment vehicle, such as credit mechanisms, digital wallets, or machine-native balances.
3. Credential: The cryptographic token or authorization artifact satisfying payment verification.

The group conducts comparative protocol analysis evaluating payment-handler models across ACP, UCP, and the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) challenge-credential-receipt pattern, specifically isolating delegated tokenization and sensitive data boundaries [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

### Trust and Identity Boundaries
In coordination with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the group investigates the decoupling of agent identity and risk from shopper identity and risk [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]. This includes defining verifiable evidence chains binding the agent, delegation token, user intent, and financial transaction across intermediary boundaries.

# Lifecycle History
- May 2026: Working group charter finalized and approved; initiated comparative payment protocol evaluations and established development of the Agentic Commerce Capability Map [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Agentic Commerce
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing a protocol-neutral capability map, trust boundaries, and reference architectures across discovery, checkout, payment, and post-purchase agent lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (WG Agentic Commerce) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical workstream co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]. Launched in February 2026, the working group serves as a vendor-neutral industry forum addressing protocol fragmentation, merchant integration overhead, fraud attribution, and multi-turn transaction execution when autonomous agents act on behalf of consumers[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].

Rather than standardizing an insular, competing commerce wire protocol, the working group maintains a protocol-neutral mandate focused on external commerce-facing interfaces rather than underlying merchant or model internals[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]. Its core deliverables comprise an Agentic Commerce Capability Map, an industry gap analysis, best practice specifications, and reference architecture implementations scheduled for late 2026 delivery[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

# Architecture / Specification

### Commerce Lifecycle Model

The working group organizes agent interactions around a structured four-phase lifecycle with cross-cutting foundational layers[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]:

1. **Product Discovery**: Delineates asynchronous catalog feeds from live merchant and marketplace queries, standardizing source discovery, data normalization, freshness guarantees, and catalog trust[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
2. **Checkout and Negotiation**: Evaluates stateful, merchant-authoritative cart and price negotiations across protocols like [ACP](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md) and the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), addressing dynamic transport bindings, protocol extensions, and human escalation handoffs[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
3. **Payment and Wallets**: Examines payment handler models, credential exchange, delegation bounds, dynamic eligibility, and protocols including the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP), Agent Payment Protocol (AP2) mandates, and x402 payment responses[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].
4. **Post-Purchase Operations**: Formalizes order lifecycle state machines, distinguishing read-only status observation from authorized state mutations, including cancellations, returns, refunds, adjustments, and dispute remediation[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

### Cross-Cutting Trust and Signal Boundary

Transactions mediated by autonomous agents split context across shoppers, agent platforms, merchants, payment service providers (PSPs), and risk scoring engines[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]. The working group establishes an evidence model separating three distinct identity and risk dimensions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]:
- **Shopper Identity and Risk**: Consumer authorization, KYC, and credential provenance.
- **Agent Identity and Risk**: Autonomous software runtime provenance, operational history, and client trust profile.
- **Delegation Evidence**: Cryptographic binding linking the consumer's explicit transaction mandate to the agent's runtime invocation[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

This framework preserves necessary fraud and trust telemetry without requiring wholesale, indiscriminate cross-boundary data disclosure[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History

- **February 2026**: Working group launched; conducted initial inventory of ecosystem actors (consumers, agents, merchants, payment networks, issuers) and protocols (UCP, ACP, AP2, x402)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].
- **March 2026**: Formulated problem-first landscape method and defined the four-phase commerce lifecycle alongside cross-cutting identity, oversight, and interoperability concerns[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
- **April 2026**: Drafted working group charter; advanced capability mapping across discovery feeds, live queries, and merchant-authoritative ACP/UCP checkout flows[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **June 2026**: Formalized the distributed fraud and trust signal model; established operational dependencies with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- **July 2026**: Advanced post-purchase workflow evaluations (order observation vs. remedy mutation) and wallet integrations utilizing AP2 payment mandates and x402 responses[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].
