proposed_concept.title: Workstream Taxonomy and Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream establishing unified agentic AI terminology, classification schemas, and ecosystem landscape mappings across foundation working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-cutting Agentic AI Foundation working group co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. The workstream reconciles differing conceptual models and operational definitions across the foundation's domain-specific working groups, producing a unified terminology dictionary, schema classification guides, and an interactive open-source landscape catalog[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

In mid-2026, the workstream transitioned from unconstrained term intake to formal group arbitration, processing a 128-term backlog through sequential, cross-working-group review syncs and publishing admitted concepts directly to the foundation's public portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Architecture / Specification

### Two-Phase Term Arbitration Model

To decouple structural consensus on taxonomy membership from protracted semantic debates over formal prose, the workstream enforces a two-phase admission pipeline[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]:

1. **Sequential Backlog Review**: Candidate terms are evaluated sequentially starting from universal foundation terms before descending into domain categories (such as [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md))[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. Each candidate is assigned one of three arbitration outcomes:
   - *Admitted*: Accepted into the canonical taxonomy namespace.
   - *Culled*: Rejected as duplicate, non-standard, or out of foundation scope.
   - *Held*: Flagged for extended cross-working-group debate when member bodies hold divergent architectural definitions (e.g., the foundational definition of `Agent`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
2. **Definition Authoring**: Full text schema definitions, `category`, and `broaderTerm` relationships are deferred until term admission is secured, migrating debate histories from working spreadsheets into version-controlled pull requests adhering to an agreed style guide[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

### Intake Controls

To ensure consistent taxonomy criteria, external community pull requests and issues targeting landscape or terminology updates are gated behind live working group sync reviews before landing in main repositories[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Scaled weekly review syncs to one hour; reviewed 46 candidate terms (admitted 13, culled 11, held 21 for debate)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
- **August 2026**: Merged PR #33 delivering the first 13 admitted entries (8 universal, 4 Identity & Trust, 1 Workflows & Process Integration) to the public portal; processed an additional 21 terms in PR #35, reaching 21 live admitted terms out of 67 reviewed[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

mutations.rationale: Update working group track structure, leadership details, and cross-boundary initiatives based on the July 2026 report and August 2026 meeting proceedings.

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, and agent execution observability across distributed and peer-to-peer runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry models, cross-boundary execution tracing, and runtime observability schemas for autonomous agents and multi-agent systems across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) ecosystem. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group defines behavioral telemetry, auditability profiles, and protocol-level observability specifications spanning local runtime hooks, client-agent boundaries, and distributed peer-to-peer agent networks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical workstreams into three consolidated active execution tracks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]:

1. **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Led by Zayne Turner, this track addresses protocol-layer telemetry, the [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md), [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) telemetry for tracing skill discovery, provenance, governance, and pre-execution trust decisions, and making skills first-class citizens in tracing systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
2. **Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination**: Led by Ty Smith, this track investigates interaction topologies, multi-agent conversational coordination, and modular observability maps spanning heterogeneous runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
3. **Agentic State & Context**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, this track unifies reasoning path telemetry and stateful execution tracking, conducting landscape and gap analyses across agent memory, context preservation, and state capsules[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

The group also explores peer-to-peer telemetry and composable trust frameworks, collaborating with LibP2P and standards bodies to evaluate Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) combined with Agent Action Capsules (AAC) encoded in CBOR for accountable decentralized execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Lifecycle History
- **July 2026**: Consolidated original five focus groups into three active tracks to optimize contributor bandwidth and eliminate overlap between LLM primitives, protocol boundaries, reasoning, and context[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **August 2026**: Initiated formal collaboration on the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) proposal and interoperability bridge recommendations for OpenTelemetry core specifications, alongside P2P network telemetry experiments with LibP2P GossipSub[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

mutations.rationale: Update agent behavior trace model standard with focus group progress, OpenTelemetry core recommendations, and library interoperability goals.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry specification capturing agent reasoning paths, state transitions, tool invocations, and application-layer interoperability with OpenTelemetry core schemas.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open, vendor-neutral telemetry specification defining standardized event schemas, span semantics, and context-propagation protocols for AI agent execution paths. Developed within the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model captures non-deterministic decision loops, internal reasoning chains, tool invocations, and subagent coordination while establishing application-layer interoperability across existing tracing frameworks and upstream OpenTelemetry standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification addresses agent-specific observability requirements beyond traditional request-response distributed tracing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]:

- **Reasoning Path and Decision Spans**: Emits structured attributes recording dynamic agent evaluation cycles, planning prompts, context window snapshots, and model selection.
- **Application-Layer Interoperability**: Establishes a reference library bridging proprietary agent runtime instrumentation with existing OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, formulating specific feature proposals for upstream OpenTelemetry core specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Skill and State Lifecycle Tracking**: Coordinates with the LLM Primitives & Protocol and Agentic State tracks to standardize span attributes for tool execution, skill invocation states, and context memory updates[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

# Lifecycle History
- **July 2026**: Designated as a primary Technical Committee deliverable for WG Observability & Traceability, initiating a dedicated drafting group led by Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **August 2026**: Formatted as a formal pull request proposal, targeting working implementations across application libraries and upstream OpenTelemetry core alignment[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

mutations.rationale: Update cross-boundary observability model to include agentic resource discovery tracing and peer-to-peer transport boundary telemetry.

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model
proposed_concept.description: Multi-layer analysis framework evaluating telemetry propagation, context preservation, and discovery governance across agent, protocol, and transport boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Boundary Observability Model is an analytical framework and reference architecture developed by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to diagnose and bridge telemetry gaps across heterogeneous agent boundaries. The model defines propagation requirements across host runtimes, tool interfaces, protocol gateways, and distributed network layers, ensuring trace continuity, provenance preservation, and trust verification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Architecture / Specification
The model evaluates trace continuity across distinct structural boundaries:

- **Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) Boundary**: Analyzes telemetry requirements during discovery phase operations, capturing skill indexing, catalog resolution, provider provenance, governance checks, and pre-execution trust decisions before an agent invokes an external capability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Protocol and RPC Boundary**: Bridges telemetry across Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and REST/gRPC interfaces, mitigating context stripping and trace context propagation failures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Peer-to-Peer and Transport Boundary**: Extends observability into decentralized networks (such as LibP2P GossipSub), integrating Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO) and Agent Action Capsules (AAC) to maintain cryptographic auditability and metric collection across peer nodes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Lifecycle History
- **July 2026**: Established as an active work item within the merged LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability track under Pavan Sudheendra and Zayne Turner[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **August 2026**: Expanded to incorporate peer-to-peer transport layers and decentralized discovery proposals, connecting cross-boundary telemetry with identity and verification initiatives[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

mutations.rationale: Update working group leadership, meeting cadence, communication channels, and active workstreams based on authoritative repository records.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing a shared workflow model, standardized terminology, and interoperability guidelines for agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87] Its primary objective is enabling agent workflows to operate seamlessly across heterogeneous frameworks, tools, and execution environments.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical output across coordinated workstreams:

- **Taxonomy**: Establishes common workflow terminology and formal definitions to eliminate ambiguity across specifications, reference architectures, and use-case catalogs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]
- **Reference Architectures**: Produces concrete workflow architectures, such as [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) and [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md), evaluated against established validation criteria.
- **Critical Use Cases**: Gathers and evaluates production deployment scenarios to test architectural models against real-world integration boundaries.

## Governance and Operations

- **Leadership**: Chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) with Adam Seligman (Workato) serving as Co-Chair, appointed for terms running March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Meeting Cadence**: Meets biweekly on Thursdays at 8:00 AM Pacific Time.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Communication Channels**: Public mailing list (`wg-workflows-process-integration@lists.aaif.io`) and a dedicated AAIF Discord forum.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Neutrality**: Members contribute as individuals under standard Linux Foundation antitrust policies rather than company delegates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

# Lifecycle History

Chartered by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to address the fragmentation of agent runtime workflows, the working group initiated workstreams across taxonomy, reference architecture patterns, and critical enterprise use cases under its 2026–2027 chair term.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, eval frameworks, and post-incident forensics for autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide provides practical implementation guidance, failure-mode patterns, and control frameworks for hardening autonomous agent runtimes against exploitation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9] Authored within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guideline equips builders with structured decision frameworks balancing operational autonomy with runtime boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification

The guideline structures security controls into five technical domains, each following a failure-pattern, defensive-control, and decision-framework schema:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

1. **Secrets Management**: Isolation of API keys and bearer tokens, ephemeral credential minting, and preventing context contamination with sensitive credentials.
2. **Secure Tool Invocation**: Boundary protection across Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, tool registry supply chain vetting, and strict parameter validation.
3. **Guardrails**: Input and output filtering, behavioral policy enforcement, and deterministic constraints mitigating unexpected non-deterministic behavior.
4. **Evaluation Frameworks**: Structured red-teaming, prompt injection resilience benchmarking, and adversarial test harnesses.
5. **Post-Incident Forensics**: Reconstruction of execution sequences using audit telemetry and verifiable action records.

## Boundary Scope

Identity architectures and delegated authorization standards (including SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693) are explicitly out of scope for this guide, as cross-agent identity and delegation governance are maintained by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

# Lifecycle History

Introduced as Deliverable 4 of 5 under the Security and Privacy Working Group charter, draft v0.1 was submitted via PR #9 to formalize defense-in-depth patterns for agent developers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]

mutations.rationale: Incorporate authoritative working methods, deliverable tracking conventions, and repository-first operating procedures established by the working group.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, and open governance procedures for agent execution visibility.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, cross-boundary tracing architectures, and execution audit protocols across agent runtimes, tool execution engines, and multi-agent coordination environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]. It collaborates closely with related technical bodies such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to ensure verifiable execution auditability.

# Architecture / Specification

## Repository Operating Principles

The working group relies on its primary GitHub repository as the authoritative source of truth for all durable work tracking [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:

- **Issues as Work Items**: Every meaningful deliverable, coordination thread, or architectural decision is tracked as a GitHub issue containing an explicit expected outcome, driver/owner, status, next step, links, and acceptance criteria [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50].
- **Pull Requests**: Code, schemas, and specifications land exclusively via pull requests.
- **Transitional Media**: Real-time communication channels (Slack, Discord) and shared drafting documents (Google Docs) serve transient discussion and early collaborative drafting, but durable artifacts migrate to versioned repository files prior to formal review and publication [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

## Work Item Lifecycle

Deliverables and issue tracking follow a standardized state progression model [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]:

- `needs owner`: The initiative is valid and approved in scope, but lacks an active driver.
- `scoping`: Boundaries, target artifacts, inputs, and acceptance criteria are actively being established.
- `in progress`: Active drafting, research, specification modeling, or cross-group coordination is underway.
- `ready for review`: Drafting is complete and requires peer review or consensus validation.
- `blocked`: Execution cannot advance due to external dependencies, missing inputs, or pending governance decisions.
- `done`: The deliverable is merged, published, or closed [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

## Cadence and Reporting

The working group maintains a synchronized operating rhythm where open issues and pull requests are triaged before meetings, decisions and action items are linked directly to GitHub issues in minutes, and monthly summaries are submitted upward to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].

mutations.rationale: Update working group leadership, deliverable workstreams, autonomous pull request merge authority, and open community policies based on monthly reports and meeting decisions.

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, security design patterns, cross-cutting security checklists, and runtime protection baselines for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPAA) establishes threat models, mitigation guidelines, security design patterns, and cross-cutting security evaluation checklists across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. The group is co-chaired by Alexander Frazer and Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operating Procedures

- **PR Acceptance Authority**: The working group exercises direct merge authority over pull requests that fall within its approved charter, allowing deliverables to iterate and land without blocking on prior [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) approval [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Monthly reports inform the Technical Committee of landed artifacts and escalate blockers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].
- **Public Access Defaults**: Working group meetings, GitHub repositories, and community communication channels are public by default, ensuring all technical deliberations remain accessible across member organizations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## Active Workstreams

1. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Benchmarking threat methodologies across OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI RMF, with extensions into STRIDE and PASTA alignment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
2. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Practical guidelines for secure tool invocation, human-in-the-loop accountability, and authorization [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable architectural security patterns, structured in partnership with overall AAIF architectural pattern frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
4. **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Evaluation criteria and gap analysis ensuring other AAIF deliverables meet core baseline security and privacy expectations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
5. **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define security, guardrail, and constraint terms within the unified foundation taxonomy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## External Liaisons

The group coordinates with external standards initiatives including OWASP, ETSI TC SAI, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) working bodies concerning stateless attestation and cryptographic tool call signing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling evaluation benchmarking existing security frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF, STRIDE, PASTA) against autonomous agent failure modes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a reference evaluation developed within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. It evaluates established threat modeling standards and AI security frameworks to determine where conventional threat modeling paradigms fail when applied to autonomous, multi-turn, tool-invoking AI agent systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

## Framework Benchmarking Scope

The evaluation benchmarks existing coverage and identifies domain gaps across eight core operational areas [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]:

- **OWASP**: Benchmarked against LLM Top 10 and agentic security initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **MITRE ATLAS**: Benchmarked for adversarial tactics, techniques, and procedures targeting autonomous agent chains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **CSA MAESTRO**: Benchmarked for multi-agent ecosystem trust boundaries and authorization layering [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **NIST AI RMF**: Benchmarked for systemic risk governance and verification profiles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **STRIDE & PASTA**: Evaluated for threat identification suitability regarding agentic planning, memory contamination, and privilege escalation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

## Emerging Threat Dimensions

Recent revisions incorporate analysis of:

- **MCP Tool Call Attestations**: Addressing tool-substitution and rug-pull attacks by evaluating signed, stateless tool calls within the Model Context Protocol [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Human-User Agent (HUA) & UI Interactions**: Threat surfaces arising when agents operate on user interfaces or act directly on behalf of human users [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History

Initially drafted by Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor, the first draft was formally published as a pull request in July 2026 for working group review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, human accountability boundaries, and cross-WG identity controls.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a foundational architectural guideline produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. It establishes practical engineering controls for building, deploying, and operating autonomous agents, centering on the fundamental premise that agents perform automated actions while human operators and designated organizational entities retain accountability and responsibility [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Security Controls

- **Accountability and Tool Call Attribution**: Mandating verifiable, auditable human and service-account attribution for every downstream tool invocation and environmental mutation performed by an agent [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Cross-Working Group Identity Boundary**: Identity, delegation token models, and cryptographic attestation mechanisms are coordinated directly with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to ensure single-source authority over authentication protocols [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Human-User Agent (HUA) Safety Controls**: Enforcing guardrails and explicit confirmation gates when agents execute actions across visual user interfaces and interactive clients [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History

Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, the initial skeleton draft was submitted via pull request in July 2026 to begin open peer review within the working group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95] The working group produces open threat models, security design patterns, implementation guidelines, and shared taxonomy deliverables designed for adoption across providers, consumers, and peer working groups.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]

The working group operates openly under the AAIF technical charter, holding public biweekly meetings and collaborating closely with related initiatives such as the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]

# Governance and Operations
The Security and Privacy Working Group is led by appointed chairs representing member organizations for the term spanning March 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]
- **Chair:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer)
- **Co-Chair:** Junjie Bu (Google)

Meetings take place biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM US Pacific Time.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95] Public proceedings, recordings, and AI-generated summaries are indexed through the Linux Foundation LFX platform, and working drafts are maintained under the working group GitHub repository.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]

# Active Workstreams and Deliverables
The working group organizes its deliverables across dedicated workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]
- **Threat Modeling:** Producing baseline risk evaluations and gap analyses comparing agentic operational surfaces with existing paradigms such as OWASP Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS, tracked in [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]
- **Design Patterns:** Formalizing reference security patterns including the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) pattern for deployments where infrastructure operators fall within the threat boundary.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]
- **Security Best Practices:** Formulating baseline engineering guidance covering secret management, secure tool invocation, and human accountability boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape:** Participating in the cross-working-group vocabulary effort to define normative terms such as guardrails, constraints, and agent archetypes.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]

# Lifecycle History
The working group held its initial orientation on February 17, 2026, and elected its chair on March 3, 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974] Following unanimous internal approval of its scope, initial deliverables, and charter on April 14, 2026, the charter was formally approved by the Technical Committee on May 26, 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974] Repositories were made public in June 2026, establishing GitHub as the primary system of record for deliverable review and merging.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]

- [Working Group Meeting Notes Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/main/meeting-notes/README.md)

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security pattern isolating policy enforcement and evidence signing inside hardware-attested environments while excluding agent execution logic.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime is an architectural security pattern for deployments where the infrastructure host or cloud operator sits inside the threat model.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11] Rather than trusting the surrounding host or running unconstrained agent code directly inside a confidential boundary, the pattern moves the Policy Decision Point (PDP) and cryptographic evidence signer into a hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), gating data release on an appraisal issued by an independent verifier.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]

A foundational premise of the pattern is that the agent execution logic remains outside the hardware isolation boundary.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11] Because autonomous agents naturally consume untrusted, attacker-influenced inputs, enclosing agent code within the enclave would unnecessarily inflate the Trusted Computing Base (TCB) with the system component most vulnerable to prompt injection or subversion.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern defines four core architectural invariants, each resolving a specific failure mode when omitted:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
1. **Isolated Enforcement Point (Agent Outside):** The policy decision point and verification checks run inside the enclave, while the agent execution runtime runs externally.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
2. **In-Enclave Key Generation and Evidence Binding:** Cryptographic signing keys are generated inside the enclave boundary and never exposed; evidence records, tool call authorizations, and execution receipts are bound directly to this key.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
3. **Policy Measurement and Release Sealing:** Policy bundles, tool schemas, system prompts, and expected configuration measurements are sealed to the hardware enclave measurement and only unsealed upon successful remote appraisal.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
4. **Independent Per-Unit-of-Work Verifier Appraisal:** An external, independent verifier evaluates the enclave attestation quote per execution unit prior to releasing sensitive context or credentials.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]

## Hardware Targets and Standards
The specification is vendor-neutral and maps directly onto major confidential computing platforms:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
- AMD SEV-SNP (Secure Encrypted Virtualization-Secure Nested Paging)
- Intel TDX (Trust Domain Extensions)
- ARM CCA (Confidential Compute Architecture)
- NVIDIA GPU Confidential Computing
- TPM 2.0 (Trusted Platform Module)

The protocol profile aligns with open industry specifications including RFC 9334 (Remote ATtestation ProcedureS Architecture), RFC 9711 (CBOR Web Token), RFC 8747 (Proof-of-Possession Key Semantics), IETF SCITT, and SLSA provenance frameworks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11] A software-only emulation mode is explicitly supported to facilitate local development, continuous integration, and conformance testing on environments lacking dedicated confidential hardware.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]

## Limitations and Trade-offs
The pattern establishes clear operational trade-offs and does not address all threat vectors:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
- **Prompt Injection:** Because the agent operates outside the enclave, the enclave cannot prevent semantic prompt manipulation or bad planning; it strictly guarantees that unauthorized actions violating verified policy cannot execute undetected.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
- **Side Channels:** Microarchitectural timing and memory bus observation attacks remain potential risks inherent to host-level physical access.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]
- **Operational Dependencies:** Introducing verifier services requires highly available reference value distribution and careful coordination of firmware upgrades and TCB version floors to prevent unintended outages.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]

# Lifecycle History
The Attested Isolated Runtime pattern was introduced in PR #11 of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) design-patterns workstream to establish an open reference model for hardware-isolated agent policy enforcement.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11] Discussion and review were scheduled during the August 2026 working group meetings.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]

# References
- [Attested Isolated Runtime Pattern Draft PR #11](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/11)
- [Security and Privacy Working Group Meeting Notes](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/main/meeting-notes/README.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling evaluation benchmarking existing security frameworks against agentic AI architectural surfaces and failure modes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis is a comparative risk assessment deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8] The document establishes an empirical baseline evaluating where established cybersecurity and AI threat modeling frameworks—such as the OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Models and MITRE ATLAS—fail to cover the unique operational surfaces and autonomous behaviors of agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8]

The gap analysis serves as the architectural foundation for subsequent working group deliverables, including the security best practices guide, vulnerability catalogs, and security design pattern libraries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]

# Architecture / Specification
The deliverable structures its comparative evaluation across multiple architectural seams distinct to agentic workflows:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]
- **Tool and Protocol Boundaries:** Threat surfaces across tool-calling layers (such as the Model Context Protocol), where dynamic tool registrations and untrusted payload deserialization introduce injection risks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]
- **Autonomous Delegation and Coordination:** Multi-agent interaction models and subagent spawning where identity propagation, delegation chains, and cross-boundary privilege escalation are unaddressed by static LLM security models.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]
- **Persistent Cognitive State:** Memory retention architectures, vector store interactions, and session recovery checkpoints subject to data corruption, poisoning, and indirect state manipulation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]
- **Policy Enforcement and Verification:** Boundaries separating non-deterministic model planning from deterministic runtime policy enforcement and out-of-band attestation.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8]

# Lifecycle History
The initial draft (v0.1) was authored by Fernando and submitted via PR #8 to the `wg-security-and-privacy` repository in July 2026.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8] Following presentation and discussion during June and July 2026 meetings, the document moved into formal working group review in August 2026 as the guiding framework for the threat modeling sub-workgroup.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]

# References
- [Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis Draft PR #8](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/8)
- [Security and Privacy Working Group Meeting Notes](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/main/meeting-notes/README.md)

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Agent skill executing read-only first-pass triage on GitHub issues, classifying severity, assessing root causes against historical reviews, and flagging prompt injections.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The issue-analysis skill produces structured, first-pass analyses of filed GitHub issues for repository maintainers by classifying report types, rating severity, hypothesising root causes, and identifying prompt injection attempts [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Maintained within the [submission-analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) repository in accordance with the [Agent Skills standard](../standards/agent-skills.md), the skill operates under strict read-only execution constraints and formats evaluations into an actionable triage template [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

# Architecture / Specification

## Execution Workflow

The triage workflow consists of four sequential phases designed to prevent unverified actions or context contamination [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:

1. **Evidence Ingestion and Injection Isolation**: Issue content is ingested strictly as data inside nonce-delimited blocks. Any directives attempting to override system prompts, reveal credentials, execute tools, or trigger notifications are flagged via `injectionSuspected` and documented in `injectionNotes` rather than executed [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
2. **Repository Grounding**: The agent inspects checked-out repository code paths directly to confirm whether reported behaviors are technically plausible. Network requests, build steps, and file modifications are prohibited during analysis [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
3. **Historical Review Consultation**: The agent consults curated historical reviews in `references/`, selecting relevant past issues by tag and affected components to evaluate severity precedents and known failure patterns [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22]. Synthetic reference examples are excluded from historical citations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].
4. **Structured Drafting**: Findings are authored against a standardized markdown template defining explicit classification criteria [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

## Output Schema and Template Structure

The resulting issue triage report follows a rigid structure [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]:

- **Summary**: Concise one-paragraph restatement of the reported problem from the maintainers' perspective.
- **Classification**: Categorization across `Type` (`bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, `ambiguous`), `Severity` (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `informational`), and `Reproducibility` (`reproducible`, `not-reproducible`, `insufficient-information`, `not-applicable`), supplemented by an impact-grounded severity rationale [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Affected Components**: Precise filesystem paths or module names (e.g., `src/config/loader.ts`) rather than abstract subsystem labels [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].
- **Root-Cause Hypotheses**: Mechanisms presumed responsible alongside criteria to confirm or refute them [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Suggested Actions and Open Questions**: Ranked next steps for human maintainers (diagnostics, target inspections) and clarifying questions for the reporter [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].
- **Related Past Reviews**: Explicit cross-references to past maintainer evaluations that informed the assessment [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

## Adversarial Injection Defenses

The skill incorporates defenses against adversarial prompt injection techniques verified by test fixtures [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:

- **Instruction Overrides**: Explicit commands attempting to override system behavior or force prompt extraction are treated as untrusted input [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Obfuscated Payloads**: Detection accounts for encoded evasion payloads, including Base64, ROT13 ciphers, and Unicode Cyrillic homoglyphs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Notification Flooding**: Mentions attempting to trigger mass alerts (such as `@everyone` or maintainer tags) are neutralized rather than propagated [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI triage agent and test suite evaluating GitHub issues and PRs with read-only repository inspection and prompt injection defense.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Submission Analyser is a headless triage agent and test harness designed to automate first-pass reviews of GitHub issues and pull requests while maintaining rigorous security boundaries [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Operating in automated CI workflows, it deploys specialized capabilities like the [issue-analysis skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md) to parse incoming reports, ground technical assessments in checked-out codebases, and intercept adversarial prompt injections before maintainer escalation [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Triage and Inspection Pipeline

Submission Analyser structures its triage lifecycle into sandboxed evaluation stages [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:

- **Nonce-Delimited Isolation**: Issue titles and bodies are enclosed within unique nonces, treating incoming user input strictly as inert observation data rather than system directives [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Read-Only Context Grounding**: The agent environment mounts repository source trees with read-only permissions, denying arbitrary network access, compilation steps, or write operations to prevent remote code execution and repository tampering during review [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Precedent Matching**: Incoming tickets are matched against historical maintainer reviews stored in `references/` to ensure consistent severity scoring across releases [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

## Injection Defense and Test Harness

The repository incorporates an adversarial fixture suite (`tests/fixtures/injections/`) testing the agent's resilience against varied prompt injection vectors [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6]:

- **Direct Instruction Overrides**: Payloads attempting to reassign the assistant role, force prompt extraction, or elicit canary strings like `PWNED` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Obfuscation and Character Evasion**: Encoded instructions using Base64, ROT13 ciphering, and Cyrillic homoglyphs engineered to bypass basic keyword filters [^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Notification and Mention Exploitation**: Payloads embedding mass pings (`@everyone`, `@here`, maintainer tags) intended to induce notification flooding across connected communication channels [^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].

When detected, injections are recorded as findings via structured flags (`injectionSuspected`, `injectionNotes`) rather than executed [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI triage agent and test suite evaluating GitHub issues and PRs with read-only repository introspection and adversarial injection test fixtures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The submission analyser is a headless continuous integration (CI) triage agent and test suite designed to evaluate incoming GitHub issues and pull requests while maintaining resilience against adversarial inputs. As part of its verification harness, the project maintains an adversarial evaluation test suite that benchmarks triage parsing against indirect prompt injections and untrusted payload executions.

# Architecture / Specification
The analyser's injection test fixture suite exercises resilience against several distinct attack surfaces and evasion patterns commonly encountered in automated issue triage:

- **Environment Exfiltration**: Fixtures evaluate whether untrusted prompt directives can coerce the agent into disclosing runtime environment secrets, API keys, or access tokens within public summary fields or auxiliary metadata[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61].
- **Hidden Markdown and HTML Comments**: Test cases verify that parsing layers neutralize hidden instructions concealed within HTML comments aimed at spoofing approval states or suppressing injection detection flags[^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe].
- **Attacker Link Ingestion**: Tests benchmark vulnerability to external instruction fetching, validating that agents refuse requests to dereference and execute instructions from untrusted external URLs[^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd].
- **Synthetic Tool and Function Invocation**: Fixtures inject fake markdown code blocks and XML function call structures (`tool_call`, `invoke`) to test whether the runtime isolates parser state from tool dispatch execution boundaries[^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].
- **Role-Play and Unicode Obfuscation**: Scenarios employ bidirectional and invisible Unicode characters alongside maintainer persona emulation to probe agent instruction adherence[^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].
- **Nested Formatting and Markup Payloads**: Complex markup scenarios test injection resilience across nested collapsible sections, mention handlers, and embedded tags attempting cross-context manipulation[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].

These test suites ensure that read-only triage agents conform to strict boundary controls as defined in [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) and protect downstream automation workflows.

proposed_concept.title: Goose Agent Runtime Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Open-source general-purpose AI agent framework providing a local multi-turn execution runtime, extension integration via MCP and ACP, and telemetry export to OpenTelemetry and Langfuse.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Goose is an open-source general-purpose AI agent runtime providing an end-to-end execution loop for multi-turn LLM tool execution, security scanning, permission inspection, and protocol extensibility via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]. Operating as a local service binding a user's CLI or desktop environment to models and extension subprocesses, Goose manages session lifecycles, context compaction, and subagent delegation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

# Architecture / Specification

The Goose architecture spans three operational layers:

1. **User Interfaces**: Client interactions are driven through the `goose` CLI, an Electron desktop application, or external ACP-compatible IDE editors (such as JetBrains or Zed) connecting over standard input/output (stdio)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
2. **Server Daemon (`goosed`)**: A local background service implemented in Rust using an Axum routing layer that exposes endpoints for chat sessions (`/reply`, `/session`, `/session_events`), configuration, MCP application proxies, and telemetry export[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]. Session state is persisted locally via SQLite through sqlx[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
3. **Agent Core**: Executes the agent loop (`request` → `provider_chat` → `tool_calls` → `permission_check` → execution) guarded by permission inspectors and a security manager combining heuristic rule patterns with ML scanners[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

### Observability and Telemetry

Goose natively supports dual telemetry export paths:
- **[OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)**: Streams hierarchical spans (`agent_reply`, `provider_chat`, `tool_execution`) over HTTP/protobuf to an OTLP collector on port 4318[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **[Langfuse](../resources/langfuse.md)**: Emits trace observations and token metrics to self-hosted or cloud Langfuse backends for generation-level inspection[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

# Lifecycle History

Donated as a foundational project to the Agentic AI Foundation, Goose v1.39.0 was formally benchmarked and documented by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) in June 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

proposed_concept.title: Linux Device Driver Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Kernel-level driver observability architecture combining structured logging, dynamic debug, tracepoints, and bus-specific tracers across Linux subsystems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux driver tracing encompasses the diagnostic and telemetry mechanisms available to device driver developers and system administrators within the Linux kernel (kernel 4.19+ and 6.x)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]. Positioned between generic kernel tracing infrastructure and hardware diagnostics, it details driver instrumentation surfaces across USB, network, block, GPU/DRM, and SPI/I2C subsystems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

# Architecture / Specification

The driver instrumentation and observability architecture comprises four core layers:

1. **Structured Device Logging**: Device-aware logging macros (`dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, `dev_warn`, `dev_err`) binding log output to specific device topology and bus addresses, streaming through `printk` to the kernel ring buffer[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
2. **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`)**: Zero-overhead runtime switching via `/sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control`, allowing selective activation of debug call sites filtered by module, function, file, or line number without kernel recompilation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
3. **Custom Driver Tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`)**: Static tracepoints declared in driver headers via `<linux/tracepoint.h>` and exposed through `tracefs` (`/sys/kernel/tracing/`), consumable by [FTrace](../resources/ftrace.md), [Linux perf](../resources/linux-perf.md), and [LTTng](../resources/lttng-kernel.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
4. **Subsystem Diagnostic Facilities**: Specialized tracing interfaces including `usbmon` (analyzed using [Wireshark](../resources/wireshark.md)), `blktrace` for block storage I/O tracing, and `devcoredump` for hardware state dumps upon driver crash[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

# Lifecycle History

Documented by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) as part of the unified Linux kernel tracing landscape in June 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Agent skill executing read-only first-pass triage on GitHub issues using dynamic frontmatter matching against a curated historical reference corpus.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Issue Analysis skill executes read-only first-pass triage on incoming repository issues by retrieving project-specific historical precedents and producing structured severity evaluations[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]. It operates inside automated CI triage harnesses such as the [submission-analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md) agent.

# Architecture / Specification

### Reference Corpus Retrieval

To align judgements with specific repository conventions, the skill utilizes a local reference corpus of historical analyses[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5]:
- **Frontmatter Indexing**: Scans metadata headers (`issue-number`, `date`, `issue-type`, `severity`, `tags`, `components`) across reference files[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Precedent Matching**: Matches tags and component paths against the issue under analysis to retrieve the 3–5 most relevant historical precedents into context[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Synthetic Precedent Guardrails**: Marks synthetic fixtures with `example: true` frontmatter, instructing the agent to never cite synthetic files as authoritative precedent[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].
- **Pre-commit Redaction Controls**: Imposes mandatory audit checks before committing reference analyses, preventing exposure of credentials, customer data, internal hostnames, or embargoed security details[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

# Lifecycle History

Packaged in the `aaif/submission-analyser` repository as an operational triage skill conforming to AAIF skill packaging guidelines[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI triage agent and test suite evaluating GitHub issues and pull requests, featuring specialized test fixtures for prompt injection resilience.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is an automated, headless CI triage agent designed to inspect GitHub issues and pull requests, classify incoming reports, and flag security hazards or policy violations without human intervention[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6]. To safeguard automated triage pipelines, it incorporates an adversarial evaluation suite benchmarking model resilience against indirect prompt injection attacks[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61][^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31].

# Architecture / Specification

The analyser runs read-only repository evaluations powered by the [issue-analysis skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md) and maintains adversarial test suites covering specific attack vectors:
- **Authority and Urgency Coercion**: Fixtures simulating fabricated Linux Foundation security directives and urgent policy violation threats designed to force configuration exfiltration[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6].
- **Delimiter Forging**: Injections containing forged closing delimiters (`</untrusted-issue>`) and fake system blocks (`<system nonce="trusted">`) attempting to bypass secret scanning and trigger false positive suppressions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61].
- **Fake Privilege and Egress Override**: Simulated administrative priority overrides purporting to originate from maintainers or AI safety teams to disable injection warnings and leak secret files[^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31].

# Lifecycle History

Maintained by the AAIF as a reference implementation for automated repository triage and security evaluation[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI issue analysis agent built on Flue 2.0 with cross-repository workflow dispatch and out-of-band publishing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Submission Analyser is an automated triage agent engineered to evaluate newly opened or labeled GitHub issues against repository context and historical reviews without requiring write access to monitored source repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. Built on Flue 2.0 and Pi AI, the agent executes headlessly within GitHub Actions, synthesizing technical analysis into a Google Doc and announcing the output to Discord while isolating repository workflows from untrusted issue input [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

Unlike conventional triage bots that post comments directly on the target issue, the Submission Analyser explicitly drops in-repo comment generation to eliminate the requirement for repository write tokens [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. This design addresses the core threat model of agentic CI pipelines: untrusted, user-submitted prompt data processed by an LLM with access to runner execution environments [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].

# Architecture / Specification

### Cross-Repository Workflow Dispatch

The analyst runs within a dedicated tooling repository (`aaif/submission-analyser`) rather than the target issue repositories it inspects [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. When an issue is opened or labeled `needs-analysis` in a monitored target repository, a lightweight dispatch workflow (`examples/target-repo-dispatch.yml`) requests an analysis run [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]:

1. **Dispatch Token Scope**: The target repository holds an `ANALYST_DISPATCH_TOKEN` with fine-grained `Actions: write` scope restricted solely to the analyst repository [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660]. Using `workflow_dispatch` avoids granting `Contents: write` (which a `repository_dispatch` would require), preventing compromised target repositories from pushing changes to analyst workflows [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
2. **Input Validation**: Dispatched inputs (`issue_number`, `target_repo`, `dry_run`) are validated as strict alphanumeric/path types before executing downstream commands [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
3. **Bot Filtering**: Actions skip bot-authored issues early in the dispatch pipeline and verify author metadata during tool execution [^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].

### Runtime and Tool Execution

The runner executes `flue run src/agents/issue-analyst.ts` over the Flue 2.0 hooks runtime [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]:
- **Model Layer**: Default inference is routed via GitHub Copilot enterprise entitlements using Pi's built-in provider, backed by a Gemini fallback strategy [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. Model calls require only `copilot-requests: write` permissions on `GITHUB_TOKEN` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- **Progressive Skill Disclosure**: Triage rules and past analysis exemplars are packaged as Flue skills through `useSkill()`, ensuring reference artifacts are loaded into context only when activated by the model [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec].
- **Single Tool Encapsulation**: The agent is directed via `AGENTS.md` to invoke `analyze_and_publish` exactly once, encapsulating fetching, analysis, document creation, and Discord notification within internal tool code rather than prompt-directed shell commands [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# Threat Model and Defense in Depth

The agent's security profile assumes any public user can submit adversarial prompt injections in issue titles, descriptions, and comments [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6]. Mitigations align with [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md):

- **Zero Repository Write Permissions**: The workflow requests `contents: read` and `copilot-requests: write`, intentionally withholding `issues: write` or write access to source trees [^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. Prompt injections cannot trick the agent into tampering with pull requests, modifying workflows, or commenting maliciously on GitHub [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec].
- **Out-of-Band Egress**: Generated reports are written strictly to authenticated Google Drive directories and an administrative Discord channel via webhook URLs [^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Strict Action Pinning**: Every third-party GitHub Action is pinned to an immutable full commit SHA to protect against upstream tag mutation and credential exfiltration [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].
- **Offline Faux Testing**: CI runs offline verification (`FLUE_FAUX=1`) with zero runner credentials, validating CLI invocation, exit codes, and skill frontmatter without network or model access [^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].
- **Manipulation Reporting**: Agent instructions dictate that suspected prompt injections must not be silently ignored or executed; instead, the agent flags `injectionSuspected: true` with rationale in `injectionNotes` to alert human maintainers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# References

- Skill Implementation: [Issue Analysis Skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md)
- Security Guidance: [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless CI issue analysis agent executing triage via GitHub Actions, using Copilot credentials and publishing out-of-band to Google Docs and Discord.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`submission-analyser` is a headless continuous integration (CI) issue triage agent designed to evaluate repository proposals and issues without write access to the monitored codebases [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]. Built on the Flue runner runtime, the agent executes within GitHub Actions workflows to ingest issue descriptions, conduct multi-model evaluations through GitHub Copilot endpoints, and emit analysis artifacts strictly out-of-band to Google Docs and Discord [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

# Architecture / Specification
## Credential and Privilege Isolation
The agent implements a structural proposal-execution isolation model by stripping all write capabilities from its GitHub execution context [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]. Workflow tokens default strictly to `contents: read` without `issues: write` permissions, eliminating prompt-injection paths that could modify issues, pull requests, or code in the monitored repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e]. When executing across repositories against a distinct `TARGET_REPOSITORY`, it relies on a fine-grained read-only Personal Access Token (PAT) if the target is private [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

Model inference requires no long-lived vendor API keys. Within Actions runs, inference access is obtained by granting `copilot-requests: write` to the workflow's ephemeral `GITHUB_TOKEN` [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e][^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73]. Publication occurs out-of-band using separate credentials:
- `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`: Service account key used to create and populate Google Docs reports [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- `GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID`: Destination folder identifier preventing public folder exposure [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- `DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL`: Webhook URL for broadcasting triage notifications to community channels [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

## Model Specifiers and Fallback Topology
The runtime enforces strict two-part dot-notated specifiers (`<provider-id>/<model-id>`) and restricts model calls exclusively to the `github-copilot` provider [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c]:
- `PRIMARY_MODEL`: `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7` as the default first-pass analyzer [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].
- `FALLBACK_MODEL`: `github-copilot/gpt-5.4` as the automated secondary provider fallback [^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].

Copilot inference endpoints reject raw Personal Access Tokens or server-to-server tokens directly, requiring an exchange against `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` to mint short-lived Copilot bearer tokens with client editor headers [^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].

# References
- [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, and full-stack observability models for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, execution boundary tracking standards, and diagnostic frameworks for AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]. The working group establishes standardized schemas and architectures for tracking agent reasoning, state mutations, and underlying hardware infrastructure interactions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Architecture / Specification
## Five-Layer Observability Stack
The working group models agent observability across a five-layer stack to bridge the gap between application tracing and hardware execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]:
- **Layer 5 (Application/Agent Layer)**: Encompasses high-level agent frameworks, prompt exchanges, tool invocations, and reasoning trajectories; this is the primary focus of standard OpenTelemetry semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Layers 1–4 (Lower Infrastructure & Hardware Layers)**: Spans host network stacks, operating system kernels, CPU scheduling, and hardware accelerators (GPUs and NPUs), which remain opaque to application-level OTel tracing alone [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

## Focus Groups
Technical development is organized into specialized focus groups [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]:
- **Protocols and Primitives**: Focuses on core event specifications, Merkle link graphs for tamper-evident trace trees, and cross-boundary protocol contracts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **State, Context, and Reasoning**: Investigates runtime session-level tracking, replay mechanisms, and addressing semantic trace gaps across diverse agent frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Advanced an initial set of 7–8 observability terms into repository taxonomy pull requests, formalized open participation across the Protocols and Primitives and State Context focus groups, and initiated work addressing OTel session ID and replay limitations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# References
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)
- [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md)
- [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, and forensic evidence standards for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical workstream tasked with standardizing telemetry propagation, distributed session tracing, and tamper-evident audit mechanisms across heterogeneous agent frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2]. Rather than formulating isolated protocols, the working group functions as an open coordination forum aligning emerging agent telemetry specifications with external standards including OpenTelemetry GenAI, OWASP Agentic Security (AOS), and W3C Trace Context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains specifications, analytical matrices, and operational use cases structured across primary functional domains:

- **Behavioral Tracing**: Developing the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) to standardize reasoning traces, state transitions, and distributed agent-to-tool boundaries.
- **Forensic and Compliance Evidence**: Establishing concrete data integrity requirements for audit and dispute resolution (Use Case E4), including Merkle-chained event logs, RFC 3161 timestamps, Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) storage guarantees, and declared-versus-observed verification ladders [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry**: Evaluating telemetry propagation and context preservation across heterogeneous execution boundaries, including [Agent-to-MCP](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md) and [Agent-to-CLI](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md) surfaces.

# Lifecycle History
The working group approved its charter on April 15, 2026, advancing it for formal Technical Committee review on April 21, 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2]. To prevent duplicate specification work, the group instituted active liaison tracking across external initiatives (such as OpenTelemetry, W3C, and OWASP) and internal peer bodies such as the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry specification capturing agent reasoning paths, state transitions, tool invocations, and tamper-evident forensic audit trails.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry specification capturing execution lifecycles, structured reasoning steps, external tool invocations, and state transitions across agentic workflows. Maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the model augments standard distributed tracing spans with agent-specific causality, state divergence records, and forensic integrity guarantees [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification defines behavioral telemetry across layered operational tiers:

- **Execution and Boundary Spans**: Instruments prompt context, model inferences, subagent delegations, and tool invocations across distinct protocol boundaries.
- **Tamper-Evident Evidence Layer (Use Case E4)**: Enforces cryptographic and evidentiary guarantees required for regulatory audits and dispute resolution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. Key components include:
  - Merkle-chained event sequences providing tamper-evident log verification.
  - Integration with RFC 3161 trusted timestamps and immutable WORM storage backends.
  - Declared-versus-observed execution linkage connecting proposed action payloads with verified system observations.
  - Multi-tier evidence-grade ladders grading record reliability from self-reported claims up to cryptographically anchored proofs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Causal Correlation**: Connects behavioral state transitions with underlying distributed traces via standard context propagation and immutable [Action Records](../taxonomy/action-record.md).

# Lifecycle History
Originally focused on operational observability and session debugging, the model was expanded to encompass regulatory compliance and legal admissibility requirements following the adoption of Use Case E4 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
