proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification
proposed_concept.description: Empirical inventory and classification schema mapping production agentic workflows against multi-dimensional interaction categories and task activities.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification provides an empirical catalog and standardized schema for classifying, benchmarking, and reviewing production agentic workflows across industry domains. Maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this inventory deconstructs complex agent deployments into consistent structural dimensions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

# Architecture / Specification
The classification framework categorizes agent systems across multiple organizational layers:

- **Activity-Based Deconstruction**: In alignment with foundation taxonomy standards, the schema formalizes workflow units as discrete "activities" rather than "steps," providing standardized semantics for granular action boundaries and state handoffs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].
- **Autonomy and Human Intervention**: Classifies human-in-the-loop oversight patterns along a gradient from manual checkpoints like [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) to automated resolution under [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md).
- **Topology and Execution Scope**: Identifies structural patterns such as single-agent iterations, hierarchical supervisor structures, and dynamic subagent swarms.

# Lifecycle History
During schema refinement across the Critical Use Cases workstream, the working group aligned the inventory with the foundation taxonomy by replacing legacy "step" nomenclature with standardized "activity" definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining the six-step intake, review, voting, and onboarding workflow for prospective Agentic AI Foundation projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process is the operating procedure governing how open source projects are proposed, reviewed, approved, and onboarded into the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. It implements the lifecycle stages and admission criteria mandated by the [Project Lifecycle Policy](./project-lifecycle-policy.md) under the authority of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification
The procedure follows an offline-first execution model to accommodate a geographically distributed Technical Committee, prioritizing asynchronous engagement over recurring live meetings[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Rather than requiring a dedicated project champion from intake, the process guarantees a collective engagement bar where a minimum threshold of Technical Committee members must review and comment before a submission can advance to a formal vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

## Six-Step Lifecycle Workflow
1. **Initial Intake (Offline)**: Owned by the Foundation CTO and assisted by an automated intake agent. The intake agent conducts technical compliance checks publicly on the GitHub issue and generates an advisory review for the Technical Committee. The CTO executes an initial smoke test and prepares the committee brief[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
2. **TC Q&A Window (Offline)**: Technical Committee members engage on the GitHub issue. If the engagement bar is not met, TC chairs trigger an on-demand TC supporter role to champion the submission; absent a willing supporter, the proposal is rejected[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. An optional live presentation can be scheduled on demand if requested by a TC member[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Submitter contributor paperwork runs in parallel.
3. **TC Vote (Offline)**: Conducted through LFX Vote to determine formal admission and initial lifecycle tier[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
4. **Governing Board Approval (Offline)**: Validates organizational resource commitments and legal feasibility via LFX Vote[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
5. **LF Legal Formation (Offline)**: Prepares contribution agreements, technical charters, and intellectual property/trademark transfers[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
6. **Technical Onboarding (Offline)**: Linux Foundation IT and project maintainers transition repository permissions, CI/CD pipelines, and project infrastructure[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Lifecycle History
Version v0.3 became effective August 28, 2026, formalizing the intake agent automation, removing mandatory single-champion dependencies in favor of the engagement bar, and introducing on-demand supporter escalation[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

mutations.rationale: Updates the proposal/execution split pattern with architectural specifications enforcing role separation, data immutability, and attribution boundaries.

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural governance pattern separating intent generation, authorization, and workflow execution into distinct roles to enforce deterministic attribution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal/Execution Split is a workflow safety pattern that enforces authorization, attribution, and non-repudiation at protected execution boundaries when intent originates from a probabilistic AI agent[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]. Because agent reasoning is probabilistic and non-deterministic, systems cannot accept an agent's self-contained decision as an authorized execution; instead, intent, authorization, and execution must be isolated into separate architectural roles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

The pattern forms a structural prerequisite for architectures like [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md), working in tandem with the [Human Approval Gate](./human-approval-gate.md) and [Durable Wait](./durable-wait.md) patterns[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

# Architecture / Specification
The core principle requires one precept and three distinct separations: intent, authorization, and execution belong to distinct roles, and each is independently persisted in an immutable system of record[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

## Core Roles
- **Proposer (Agent)**: Generates proposed parameter data rather than executing direct effects. The payload is treated as immutable data representing proposed intent, not executable code or autonomous capability[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
- **Authorization Authority**: An accountable entity—either an authenticated human principal or an immutable, versioned policy engine—evaluating whether that exact, immutable proposal payload may proceed[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]. If denied, timed out, or unverified, the gate fails closed into a terminal or recovery path[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
- **Workflow-Controlled Executor**: A deterministic system component invoked exclusively by workflow orchestrators (and inaccessible to direct agent calls) that executes the authorized payload against downstream protected resources[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

## Invariants and Enforcement
- **Proposal Immutability**: What is authorized must match byte-for-byte what executes; downstream mutations invalidate the approval[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
- **Fail-Closed Verification**: Absence, delay, or failure of an authorization signal strictly terminates execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
- **Idempotency & Non-Replayability**: Retrying an approved proposal must never result in duplicate external side effects[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

# References
Defined by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [workstream on reference architectures](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

mutations.rationale: Incorporates standard terminology definitions from the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, standardizing on Activity rather than Workflow Step.

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Core vocabulary and execution primitives standardizing structured multi-activity work, coordination models, and state persistence in agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Workflow Primitives define the foundational vocabulary and execution semantics for agentic AI processes established by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. These definitions establish a shared operational model across workflow reference architectures, patterns, and interoperability specifications[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

# Architecture / Specification
The taxonomy replaces legacy concepts of "Workflow Step" or "Workflow Task" with the unified primitive **Activity** to prevent circular definitions between execution units and overarching workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

## Foundational Primitives
- **Activity**: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].
- **Workflow**: The primary unit of structured, multi-activity work with a defined goal and outcome. A workflow is composed of one or more activities, their relationships, and the logic required to achieve that outcome[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].
- **Workflow Execution**: A runtime instance of a workflow definition maintaining its own isolated execution state and lifecycle across concurrent executions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow State**: The data representing the current condition of a workflow execution at a specific point in time, including progress indicators and continuation data[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow Context**: The shared information available to workflow participants during execution—including inputs, metadata, execution history, configuration, and external references—that informs decision-making across activities and boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

## Execution and Control Characteristics
- **Control Flow**: The orchestration logic determining order, branching conditions, loops, parallelism, and synchronization of activities[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Trigger**: An event, signal, schedule, or request initiating or advancing a workflow execution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Durability**: The capability of a workflow execution to persist state across infrastructure failures or process interruptions so execution resumes without loss of progress[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Determinism**: The property whereby a workflow produces identical execution behavior given identical inputs, state, and history[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

# References
Maintained under `workstreams/taxonomy/terms.md` by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing measurement frameworks, failure taxonomies, evaluation protocols, and empirical surveys for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an AAIF technical body focused on defining measurement frameworks, failure taxonomies, and empirical evaluation standards for production AI agent systems [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]. Chaired by Jordan Auge (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group coordinates cross-industry efforts to capture failure modes, benchmark agent behavior, and establish common definitions across the AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

Key deliverables under development include the terminology and failure taxonomy deliverable (D1) and the gap analysis and empirical survey track (D2) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its primary technical outputs across distinct deliverables:
- **D1 (Terminology and Failure Taxonomy)**: Establishes a shared taxonomy for failure modes, hallucination classifications, and operational accuracy metrics in coordination with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].
- **D2 (Gap Analysis and Survey Support)**: Gathers empirical data through practitioner surveys targeting engineers and operators with firsthand agent-system deployment experience to uncover operational pain points, prioritization signals, and benchmarking gaps [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].
- **Phase 2 & Internal Deliverables (I1)**: Establishes cross-working-group relays and alignment to coordinate evaluation protocols with other AAIF bodies [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Conducted iterative review of the D1 terminology pull request (#8) and advanced the D2 survey specification pull request (#9) toward merge readiness, targeting practitioners across early exploration and production agent deployments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream establishing unified agentic AI terminology, classification schemas, and ecosystem landscape mappings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting AAIF initiative chartered to establish unified terminology, ontological boundaries, and landscape mappings across all agentic AI domains [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]. Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream reviews and curates vocabulary proposals submitted by individual working groups to maintain consistency across foundation deliverables [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

The group maintains both the AAIF Universal Terminology and the interactive Agentic AI Landscape, serving as the common semantic backbone for working groups including [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), and [Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates through weekly terminology-review syncs and domain editor pull request cycles:
- **Unified Terminology Curation**: Terms undergo multi-round review categorizing candidate definitions as kept, culled, or held for debate. Relational mappings are explicitly documented between adjacent concepts such as Skill and Tool, Kill Switch and Reversibility, Harness and Meta-harness, and Delegation and Handoff [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Agentic AI Landscape**: Organizes ecosystem tools, frameworks, and protocols into standard categories, including specialized categories like Agentic Vulnerability Enumeration (AVE) and Attestation & Verifiable Evidence [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].
- **Cross-Group Representation**: Dedicated liaisons from sibling working groups, such as Identity & Trust and Agentic Commerce, ensure terminology alignment across domain boundaries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Reviewed 53 candidate terms across three review syncs (keeping 37, culling 15, and holding 1 for debate); resolved `Agent` as a kept universal term; merged the `Harness` definition (PR #37); and advanced pull requests for `Human in the loop`, `Meta-harness`, Identity & Trust terms, and Workflow & Process Integration terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing a protocol-neutral capability map, trust boundaries, and settlement mechanisms for autonomous commercial transactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an AAIF technical body developing vendor-neutral capability models, state-transition frameworks, and trust boundary specifications for autonomous commerce interactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]. The group analyzes end-to-end commerce flows spanning pre-purchase inquiry, payment and settlement, and post-purchase lifecycle operations across heterogeneous agent platforms and protocols [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's charter centers on several core workstreams and deliverables:
- **Deliverable 1 (Agentic Commerce Capability Map)**: A comprehensive reference mapping of commercial agent capabilities, protocol coverage flags (e.g., UCP, ACP, AP2, and x402), and signal requirements across transaction phases [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]. Key post-purchase rows (P1–P7) specify eligibility inquiry, remedy offer and negotiation, buyer authorization and consent evidence, state-change execution signals, evidence binding, dispute and claims initiation, and adjustment ledgers [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **Deliverable 2 (Gap Analysis)**: Identifies operational and protocol coverage gaps across commercial agent interactions, particularly in post-purchase dispute and remedy workflows [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **Evidence and Auditability Contracts**: Machine-readable contracts employing an 8-field bounded verdict envelope (`verdict`, `verifier`, `verifier_signature`, `evidence_refs`, `evidence_fingerprints`, `verification_basis`, `witness_scope`, `timestamp`) to bind cross-boundary verification evidence to execution outcomes [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **Cross-Group Coordination**: Coordinates with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) via dedicated liaison representation and aligns evidence models with the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Proposed post-purchase section inputs (P1–P7) and bounded verdict envelope contracts for Deliverable 1 (PR #6) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]. Expanded participation in AAIF taxonomy curation through cross-group representation with Identity & Trust [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry specification capturing agent reasoning paths, state transitions, tool invocations, and cross-trace turn continuity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry standard developed by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to record the execution lifecycle of autonomous agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]. It defines vendor-neutral semantic conventions and context propagation mechanisms for reasoning chains, tool invocations, and multi-turn conversational sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40, ^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].

The model addresses gaps where standard distributed tracing cannot represent long-running agent interactions, asynchronous pause-and-resume operations, and cross-turn dialog states without creating impractically long session-level spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model is validated through a structured execution plan across independent agent runtimes:
- **Baseline Capture and Gap Classification**: Validates semantic models by recording reproducible baseline telemetry against reference runtimes, such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and secondary SDKs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]. Observed discrepancies are classified as unsupported behavior, instrumentation defects, specification guidance gaps, or missing semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].
- **Session and Turn Continuity**: Connects distributed traces across multi-turn interactions without relying on single, long-running session spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43]. Completed turns maintain shared conversation identifiers across process restarts, pause/resume phases, and caller-agent hierarchies using exported telemetry attributes alone [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026**: Established the nine-task execution plan defining baseline telemetry capture protocols across independent runtimes (Issue #40) and formalizing multi-turn cross-trace continuity criteria (Issue #43) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40, ^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining commerce capabilities, payment protocol boundaries, dispute accountability models, and merchant consent surfaces for delegated agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group establishes a protocol-neutral capability map, trust boundaries, dispute evidence frameworks, and payment integration models for autonomous purchasing agents[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. Co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group addresses architectural challenges spanning real-time payment execution rails and post-transaction accountability[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

Related efforts coordinate with identity verification in [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and cross-domain taxonomy alignment in [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on three core architectural domains:

- **Payment Rails and Transaction Composition:** Evaluating protocols such as x402 (a Linux Foundation project) that decouple single-payment transactions from cart-shaped checkouts across HTTP, MCP, and A2A transports[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. The model isolates scheme, network, asset, and settlement mechanisms, delegating buyer intent and policy enforcement to the agent layer while supporting pay-per-use micropayments for API, content, and context retrieval[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Dispute and Evidence Models:** Addressing post-transaction accountability when cardholders are absent and traditional web signals (click trails, device fingerprints, session behavior) disappear[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307]. The group investigates verifiable-intent records, know-your-agent identity anchors, and structured transaction metadata (agent ID, platform, model version) to substantiate authorization in payment dispute workflows[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].
- **Structured Consent Surfaces:** Defining machine-readable interfaces for capturing agent acknowledgment of merchant terms and conditions without relying on implicit human browsing conventions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026:** Completed deep dive on x402 payment protocol integration across AP2, UCP, and ACP, and formulated dispute accountability requirements; scheduled upcoming technical reviews of the Order Network eXchange (OnX) standard and Machine Payment Protocol (MPP)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-922f59c26329-125f7307].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, lower-layer syscall observability, and verifiable action tracking for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, distributed tracing protocols, and runtime execution evidence for AI agents across application and system layers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]. Its work spans high-level agent reasoning trajectories, tool invocations, and low-level kernel syscall events required to audit autonomous operations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

The group collaborates with [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) on execution boundaries and [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) on standardized event terminology.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical initiatives through specialized focus groups and validation projects:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** A multi-task specification workstream standardizing runtime agent trajectories, tool invocations, provider streaming behaviors, and execution continuity fixtures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].
- **Primitives and Protocol Observability:** A focus group addressing cross-boundary tracing across MCP, Agent Gateway, and lower infrastructure layers (below L7, down to kernel syscall tracing and provenance)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].
- **Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) Lifecycle Telemetry:** Validating end-to-end telemetry across discovery, provenance, governance, trust, and admission stages correlated with agent execution through standard OTLP pipelines using [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Agent Gateway[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].
- **Verifiable Action Capture:** Reviewing projects such as Agent Action Capsules (MeshLLM) to record dispatches, runtime occurrences, and regulatory conformance through cryptographic ledgers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Lifecycle History
- **August 2026:** Formulated nine-task execution plan for the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].
- **September 2026:** Consensus established to incorporate lower-layer (syscall and below L7) observability under the Primitives and Protocol Observability focus group led by Trace; initiated review of Agent Action Capsules and sandbox project intake policies[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing threat models, runtime security design patterns, static-analysis rules, and security guidelines for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group develops vendor-neutral threat models, runtime defense patterns, actionable hardening guidelines, and security verification rules for agentic AI architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]. It coordinates cross-cutting security reviews with other AAIF working groups, including [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) and [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Architecture / Specification
Key workstreams and deliverables maintained by the group include:

- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices:** Comprehensive operational hardening guidance covering secrets management, tool invocation boundaries, and model input validation, intentionally delegating identity and trust practices to [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Static Analysis Rules:** An automated, tool-facing deliverable translating security best practices into executable static-analysis rules benchmarked against major cloud provider agent SDKs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Design Patterns Catalog:** Standardized catalog of security patterns, including independent [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) mechanisms and agent memory isolation models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Systematic coordination framework ensuring other technical working groups integrate baseline security reviews into deliverable lifecycles[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History
- **September 2026:** Finalized reviews to freeze and merge v1 of the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md); integrated kill-switch patterns into the design pattern catalog and initiated rule extraction for static code analyzers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

mutations.rationale: Record the freezing and merging of v1, the formal scoping exclusion of identity/trust topics, and the creation of companion static-analysis rules.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security guidelines covering secrets management, isolated tool execution, human accountability boundaries, and static-analysis compliance rules.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline defines architectural and operational requirements for securing autonomous agents against prompt injection, unauthorized privilege escalation, sensitive data exfiltration, and unintended autonomous tool execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]. Developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guideline serves as the foundation's core security baseline for agent developers and platform operators[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

Identity, attestation, and credential delegation practices are formally scoped out of this document and governed separately by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline outlines defense-in-depth principles across the agent lifecycle:

- **Execution Boundary Isolation:** Enforcing isolated runtimes and least-privilege scoping for tool execution environments, preventing agents from exceeding runtime permissions.
- **Control and Interception Planes:** Implementing out-of-band controls, including [kill switches](../patterns/kill-switch.md) and deterministic policy gates, to halt runaway iterations or untrusted dispatches.
- **Actionable Static Analysis Rules:** Translating descriptive security tenets into machine-checkable static analysis rules that evaluate agent codebases against best practices established across major agent SDKs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Memory and State Protection:** Guarding persistent agent memory against malicious injection and cross-session state corruption[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History
- **September 2026:** Version 1 frozen and merged following month-long review; initiated translation into static-analysis enforcement rules and affirmed exclusion of identity and trust domains to avoid cross-group duplication[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

mutations.rationale: Detail the five-stage ARD capability lifecycle and its standard OTLP telemetry correlation across Agent Gateway and Goose.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Resource Discovery (ARD)
proposed_concept.description: Decentralized discovery, verification, and admission specification enabling agents to find, trust, and instrument capabilities across five lifecycle stages.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) is a decentralized specification and lifecycle architecture enabling AI agents to discover, verify, govern, and admit external resources, tools, and skills across system boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49]. ARD ensures that agent resource acquisition is subject to deterministic trust evaluation, governance checks, and end-to-end telemetry rather than unverified dynamic loading[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

Instrumentation and telemetry standards for ARD are reviewed in collaboration with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).

# Architecture / Specification
ARD defines a five-stage capability acquisition lifecycle, each emitting structured telemetry correlated via W3C Trace Context and exported through standard OTLP pipelines[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49]:

1. **Discovery:** The initial search, querying, and identification of prospective external resources or endpoints.
2. **Provenance:** Tracing the authoring origin, release signature, and supply chain integrity of the discovered capability.
3. **Governance:** Evaluating environmental policies, runtime constraints, and organizational permission boundaries.
4. **Trust:** Cryptographic verification, reputation scoring, and attestation checks assessing capability reliability.
5. **Decision:** Explicit admission, conditional quarantine, or rejection of the resource prior to runtime loading.

Admitted resources emit correlation spans linking the admission decision directly to subsequent activation and execution inside runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) or proxy layers such as Agent Gateway, ensuring that quarantined capabilities produce zero unauthorized execution spans[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

# Lifecycle History
- **September 2026:** PoC validation established export of all five lifecycle stages via OpenTelemetry (OTLP JSON fixtures) and correlation with skill activation in Agent Gateway and Goose[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate concrete tokens, typographic constraints, palette rules, surface models, and asset usage guidelines from DESIGN.md.

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual, typographic, palette, and asset specifications governing Agentic AI Foundation digital assets, reports, and communications.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF design system governs visual identity across foundation collateral, audit reports, documentation, and external presentations [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. All generated human-facing artifacts rely on standardized CSS tokens and strict component specifications to preserve structural consistency.

# Architecture / Specification

### Palette and Surfaces
- **Primary Accent**: Black (`--accent: var(--ink)`). Primary actions are strictly black [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve solely as internal surface accents with at most one hue leading at a time (e.g., coral is `--spec-8`, not the primary brand color) [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Surfaces**: Two first-class surfaces: white editorial ground (`--paper`) and black plate [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. There is no dark mode or `prefers-color-scheme` block. Warm off-white (`--paper-2`) provides occasional section banding, while tinted panels use `--paper-3` [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Depth and Corner Radius**: No drop shadows. Visual depth is established via 1px hairlines, surface tinting, and inset strokes. Layout boxes, cards, stats, tables, and chips remain square (`border-radius: 0`), reserving pill radii (`--radius-pill`) exclusively for interactive buttons and badge elements [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

### Typography
- **Typeface**: Instrument Sans (OFL) at weights 400, 500, 600, and 700 across display and UI layers [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Monospace stacks are reserved strictly for metadata and eyebrows, never body copy [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Headings**: Weight 500 with tracking `-0.02em` and line height 1.05–1.15. Weight 600 is restricted to level 5 and level 6 headings [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

### Asset Governance
- **Mark and Logo**: Official vector marks (`assets/aaif-mark.svg`, `assets/aaif-mark-square.svg`, `assets/aaif-logo-white.svg`) must be rendered verbatim without redrawing [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Agent Motif**: Derived from mark primitives, the agent motif is designated for empty states, loaders, event media, and section dividers. It is explicitly prohibited in governance, board, or press communications [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Lifecycle History

- Baseline token definitions and report layout constraints codified in `community-events/DESIGN.md` [^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural break between agent proposal and execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent Human Approval architecture defines an execution topology where an autonomous agent operates in a sandboxed proposal environment, requiring explicit authorization by an authenticated human before changes transition to production systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture establishes three decoupled operational boundaries:
1. **Proposal Generation**: The agent synthesizes structured changes or content updates within an isolated workspace without direct write permissions to production sinks [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].
2. **Approval Checkpoint**: A deterministic boundary evaluates proposals and surfaces immutable diffs to human reviewers using patterns documented in [../patterns/human-approval-gate.md](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md).
3. **Publication Boundary**: Once signed or approved, an out-of-band execution engine commits the payload to target datastores or systems of record [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

### Validated Use Cases
Empirical validation records verify this topology across editorial and knowledge management workloads [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]:
- FAQ and knowledge-base article updates.
- Automated release notes generation.
- Directory listing and marketplace description synchronization.

# Lifecycle History

- Merged validation scenarios covering publication and approval boundaries for content use cases [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Core vocabulary and execution primitives standardizing structured multi-activity work, coordination flows, and determinism boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Workflow Primitives provide foundational definitions for orchestrating agent activities, coordinating control flow, and classifying execution state transitions across multi-step processes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Primitives
- **Determinism**: Evaluated as a scoped property of a discrete layer—Workflow Execution, Control Flow, or an individual Activity—rather than an invariant across an entire end-to-end workflow [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. A workflow can retain deterministic control flow logic while orchestrating non-deterministic language model activities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Control Flow**: The structural ordering, branching, and joining logic governing execution sequences [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. Control flow definitions are agnostic to whether transitions are static design-time paths or dynamically determined at runtime by an agent orchestrator [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Workflow Execution**: An instantiated lifecycle execution that retains continuity across mid-execution replanning, retries, and dynamic plan alterations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Handoff**: The transfer of execution responsibility or context across agents, tools, or human boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. Handoff captures both the responsibility transition and the observable trace boundary where transfer occurs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

# References

- Layered determinism models reference factor classifications from [../resources/agentic-vulnerability-enumeration.md](../resources/agentic-vulnerability-enumeration.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, delegation, and authorization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical committee body dedicated to defining vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, authorization, discovery, consent, and auditability [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. While conventional identity frameworks address human users and microservice workloads, agentic architectures introduce complex challenges surrounding dynamic task delegation, cross-domain authority propagation, actor chain verification, and human approval evidence [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical activities into three collaborative breakout streams [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- **Use Cases**: Grounding technical requirements in enterprise and consumer agent workflows, coordinated by Wei Chen.
- **Reference Architecture**: Defining core actors, component interactions, trust boundaries, and authority delegation protocols across runtime platforms, coordinated by Brian Malone.
- **Taxonomy Coordination**: Harmonizing domain terminology with the cross-cutting [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), liaised by Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky.

The group evaluates and builds upon external foundations including [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md), SPIFFE/SPIRE workload attestation, Uber Engineering's actor chain identity architecture, the NVIDIA Secure Agent Workspace reference design, and IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization specifications (`draft-klrc-aiagent-auth`) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Lifecycle History
The Identity and Trust Working Group operates under charter from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Leadership for the March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 term was appointed by Platinum and Gold foundation members, designating Grant Miller (IBM) as Chair and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE) as Co-Chair [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. The working group maintains public meetings every Thursday alternating weekly between 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM Pacific Time, alongside an agenda tracker and running notes repository [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3][^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0].

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool Local CLI Boundary Deep Dive
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and context propagation model analyzing direct agent invocations of local CLI child processes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-to-Tool Local CLI Boundary Deep Dive establishes a telemetry reference matrix and context propagation architecture for direct agent invocations of local command-line interface (CLI) subprocesses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]. When an agent launches an operating system subprocess directly without an intermediary skill runtime, the boundary bridges both an agent-level semantic decision (`Agent → Tool`) and an operating-system process execution (`Agent Runtime → Local Process`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# Architecture / Specification
The boundary spans two interconnected execution surfaces: an agent execution surface where tool call identification, parameter serialization, and security policy checks occur, and an operating-system process surface where environment variables are constructed, child processes are spawned, and exit codes are observed [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

The causal invocation model follows:
- Upstream caller / turn
  - Tool execution span (`Agent → Tool` semantic boundary)
    - Optional CLI caller span
      - Local CLI execution span (`Agent Runtime → Local Process` boundary)
        - Downstream CLI operations

The matrix analyzes six observable telemetry dimensions across the boundary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:
- **Identity**: Binds agent, principal, turn/session, `gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, executable path, and process ID (PID). A critical remaining gap is the absence of an immutable binding between the tool call, the binary digest/version, and the delegating principal.
- **Context**: Propagates active trace context and optional baggage across the boundary using the OpenTelemetry environment-variable carrier specification (`TRACEPARENT`, `TRACESTATE`, `BAGGAGE`). Context must cross before process invocation; post-hoc transcript parsing cannot supply child-visible parent spans.
- **Relationship**: Preserves causal parent-child hierarchy from agent turn to tool span and process span. For detached, background, or fire-and-forget tasks, OpenTelemetry Span Links represent ownership to avoid misrepresenting lifecycle duration.
- **Lifecycle**: Maps the transition sequence `selected → authorized/denied → context prepared → spawn requested → process started → running → exited/errored/timed out/canceled`.
- **Outcome**: Captures process exit codes (`process.exit.code`), structured execution errors (`error.type`), partial standard output/error, and compensation results.
- **Provenance**: Records the tool schema source, invocation plugin, executable path, and observer attribution metadata.

# Lifecycle History
Authored by `@fangxiu-wf` for the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) in response to working group issue #29, this reference document incorporates real-world validation from the LoongSuite Pilot implementation and Claude Code execution models [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]. The model demonstrates that pre-execution span reservation and environment variable injection successfully preserve end-to-end distributed trace continuity prior to process execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Inventory and Schema
proposed_concept.description: Empirical inventory and multi-dimensional schema classifying production AI agent workflows across orchestration patterns, coordination mechanisms, and agent cardinality.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification is an empirical inventory and taxonomy schema developed by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to categorize production agentic workflows against architectural dimensions such as coordination models, agent cardinality, and execution patterns.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] The repository maintains both a formal schema specification (`schema-agentic-use-cases.md`) and a concrete inventory (`use-case-inventory.md`) backed by vendor documentation and empirical case studies.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48]

# Architecture / Specification
The classification framework evaluates real-world agent deployments along standardized structural axes:

- **Coordination Mechanisms**: Distinguishes deterministic, fixed or scripted coordination from dynamic AI-coordinated planning systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]
- **Execution Patterns**: Characterizes operational execution topologies, such as sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out distributions, and convergence loops bounded by deterministic acceptance criteria.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]
- **Agent Cardinality**: Assesses whether a task is single-agent sufficient or inherently multi-agent due to context size exhaustion, role separation, or privilege boundaries.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

Every classification entry requires verifiable citations to publicly accessible technical documentation that explicitly describes execution structure rather than generic capabilities.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] Where documentation does not specify execution topology (such as concurrency versus sequence), cells are tracked as unspecified pending verification.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39]

# Lifecycle History
The inventory undergoes continuous verification to eliminate broken citations and ungrounded assumptions.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] In early revisions, rows such as lead research and enrichment were tied to sequential waterfall enrichment pipelines, on-call incident triage was identified as an inherently multi-agent parallel fan-out architecture coordinated by AI planning, and contract review was categorized under AI-coordinated planning.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39] File path alignment standardizes cross-references between the inventory and `schema-agentic-use-cases.md` across the working group repository.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry specification and execution plan standardizing agent reasoning spans, execution state transitions, and upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to capture AI agent reasoning paths, state transitions, tool invocations, and multi-turn execution spans.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47] The initiative establishes a structured execution plan to generate evidence-backed contributions for runtime instrumentation, Foundation terminology, and upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

# Architecture / Specification
The specification addresses gaps in standardized distributed tracing for non-deterministic AI agent behaviors, providing crosswalks across execution domains:

- **Upstream OpenTelemetry GenAI Alignment**: Translates behavioral findings into contributions for the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, addressing telemetry gaps such as turn-entry spans, conversation identifiers, and token attributions.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]
- **Taxonomy Integration**: Coordinates trace vocabulary and semantic concepts with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to ensure consistent domain terminology across agent lifecycles.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]
- **Runtime Instrumentation**: Establishes fixes and reference implementations for agent runtime hosts that omit conversation context or fail to expose uniform entry points across execution turns.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

# Lifecycle History
The trace model is governed under a nine-task execution plan established following working group discussions in August 2026.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47] Task 9 focuses on upstream contributions, transitioning experimental agent trace extensions into standardized conventions in OpenTelemetry and core runtime codebases.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security guidelines covering secrets management, isolated tool execution, human accountability, and multi-cloud workload identity federation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes architectural security standards for AI agent systems, detailing controls for secrets lifecycle management, isolated tool sandboxing, human oversight, and cryptographic identity.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23] Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guideline defines baseline requirements for limiting agent blast radius and securing cross-boundary resource access.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

# Architecture / Specification
The guidance sets expectations for operational runtime environments across core security domains:

- **Workload Identity Baseline**: Establishes default temporary credential boundaries, specifying short-lived tokens (with a one-hour default configurable downward) constrained by strict IAM role scoping.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Multi-Cloud and Hybrid Federation**: Addresses cross-cloud and on-premises boundary crossings where agents assume roles across heterogeneous IAM providers, recommending OIDC-based federation and evaluating blast radius across multi-cloud identity chains.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Role Scoping and Least Privilege**: Recommends tight operational bounds on automated role assumption to prevent privilege escalation across federated service endpoints and multi-agent coordination boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]
- **Cross-Group Alignment**: Coordinates workload identity patterns and token lifetime guidance jointly with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

# Lifecycle History
Following community review of the single-cloud identity baseline, the working group initiated efforts to formulate cross-cloud role assumption, hybrid cloud-to-on-premises federation patterns, and federated token lifetime guidance to prevent reliance on static credentials.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation methodology validating reference architectures against empirical use cases using practitioner jobs and structural boundary alignment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The reference architecture use-case validation process determines whether a Reference Architecture (RA) is an architectural fit for a real-world workflow use case [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. Validation evaluates whether an empirical use case exhibits the primary practitioner job and defining structural boundaries specified by the candidate architecture [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. It establishes structural compatibility rather than verifying whether an existing deployment already implements every technical control or runtime guarantee defined by the RA [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

# Architecture / Specification

## Validation Purpose and Scope
Validation asks whether a target use case shares the practitioner job and core operational boundary addressed by the reference architecture [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]:
- **Fit vs. Implementation Conformance**: A `Validated` finding confirms that an RA is a good architectural fit for the use case; it does not require proof that an existing system already implements every RA control, such as retry mechanisms, storage design, hash verification, or idempotency keys [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. The RA provides these controls to enable safe implementation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Evidence Standards**: Validation relies strictly on verified facts documented in the [Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md) and its cited external sources [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. Illustrative examples or scenarios embedded within an RA cannot be used as circular evidence for validation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

## Validation Protocol
Validators execute a lightweight assessment:
1. **Boundary & Job Alignment**: Assess whether the RA solves the central job of the use case, mapping participant roles across agents, orchestration workflows, human operators, and external systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
2. **Check Formulation**: Establish two or three simple checks focusing on the primary job and defining boundary [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
3. **Result Documentation**: Structure validation findings with concise observations, limiting `What matches` and `What is unknown` summaries to no more than two bullets each [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. If a classification entry carries an undocumented rationale marker, its basis must be marked `Unknown` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

# Lifecycle History
The validation guide was formalized in the Reference Architectures workstream to support both human contributors and AI coding agents conducting rigorous, evidence-backed compatibility reviews [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64] under overarching contribution rules [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

# References
- [Job-Oriented Architecture Model](job-oriented-architecture-model.md)
- [Reference Architecture Template](reference-architecture-template.md)
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural framework distinguishing patterns, reference architectures, and scenarios around recognizable practitioner jobs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Architecture Model defines the structural taxonomy and authoring relationships separating reusable patterns, composite reference architectures, and validation scenarios within the AAIF Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. The model establishes a consistent framework ensuring that architectural components remain vendor-neutral, modular, and directly verifiable against real-world operational problems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

# Architecture / Specification

## Contribution Hierarchy
The framework partitions workflow specifications into three core tiers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]:
- **Pattern (`patterns/`)**: Solves a single recurring workflow sub-problem with an independently reusable, context-free solution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. Patterns mandate invariants that implementations must preserve and detail concrete failure modes when invariants are violated [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Reference Architecture (`architectures/`)**: Defines the reusable whole for a recognizable practitioner job (named to complete the sentence *"We are building a ___"*) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. It integrates multiple patterns, capability roles, operational boundaries, guarantees, and exit states [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. Generic architectures avoid domain-specific naming unless the practitioner job itself is inherently domain-bound [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Scenario (`Worked scenario` / `Validation record`)**: Concrete or illustrative workflow executions used to test whether an architecture fits [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. Scenarios serve as evidence and test cases rather than standalone architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

## Authoring Principles and AI Contribution Rules
All contributions must adhere to core authoring constraints [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30]:
- **Logical Vendor Neutrality**: Capabilities and required behaviors must be described in logical, vendor-neutral terms before naming specific products [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Evidence vs. Interpretation**: Documented facts from empirical use cases must be strictly distinguished from proposed working group interpretations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30]. Genuine gaps must be recorded as open questions rather than speculative certainty [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Clear Work Boundaries**: Architectures must explicitly demarcate work controlled autonomously by agents from work managed deterministically by workflow orchestrators [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# Lifecycle History
The model was adopted as an architectural decision record and contributor standard within the Reference Architectures workstream to maintain uniformity across contributed patterns and architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# References
- [Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide](reference-architecture-validation.md)
- [Reference Architecture Template](reference-architecture-template.md)
- [Workflow Architecture Principles](workflow-architecture-principles.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry specification standardizing agent reasoning spans, execution turns, proposed actions, and OTel crosswalks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model defines a vendor-neutral specification and execution plan for capturing the complete lifecycle of agent reasoning, tool execution, interaction turns, and governance approvals [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. Developed by the Observability and Traceability Working Group, the model provides standard semantic conventions and relationship models that bridge AAIF behavioral concepts with OpenTelemetry distributed tracing standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification

## Identity and Relationship Contract
The shared trace model contract establishes explicit hierarchical and causal relationships between execution artifacts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]:
- **Session & Turn Scope**: Tracks multi-turn conversations across discrete interaction turns, permitting turns to maintain distinct distributed trace IDs while preserving overall session context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Proposed Actions vs. Execution Spans**: Explicitly models intent through proposed actions prior to execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]. When human or policy approval gates evaluate an action, the approval references the proposed action regardless of whether authorization is granted; if denied, trace continuity is maintained even when no corresponding tool execution span is generated [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **Observations and Resumption**: Encodes observation relationships, handling approval waits, asynchronous dialog resumption, and incomplete observations when execution fails or targets are missing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].
- **OpenTelemetry Crosswalk**: Maps AAIF turn-entry and reasoning abstractions to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, establishing common attribute mappings without prescribing internal runtime storage [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

## Execution Plan Workstreams
The specification evolves across a nine-task execution plan, including gap baselining, identity contract definitions, fixture test suites, and cross-working-group alignment with taxonomy definitions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Lifecycle History
Following August working group sessions, Task 3 of the Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan initiated formalization of the versioned identity and relationship contract and OTel crosswalk [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

- [Approval Checkpoint Pattern](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification is an empirical inventory and taxonomy schema categorizing production AI agent workflows across architectural patterns, human oversight boundaries, and execution models [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]. Maintained by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group, it establishes standardized criteria to benchmark real-world deployments and validate workflow reference architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification

## Structural Classification Dimensions
The schema classifies agent implementations across several structural parameters, including approval mechanisms, exception escalation paths, and workflow orchestration patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

## Pattern Disambiguation: Fan-out vs. Pipeline
A prominent open classification question centers on the structural boundary between `Parallel fan-out` and `Sequential pipeline` patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]:
- **Timing Dimension**: `Parallel fan-out` has traditionally been defined by execution timing (concurrent sub-tasks) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
- **Dependency Dimension**: `Sequential pipeline` has been defined by state dependency (dependent activities feeding downstream steps) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].
- **Orthogonality and Classification Gaps**: Because concurrency and data dependency are not strict opposites, tasks may exhibit neither or both characteristics, leaving numerous inventory rows classified as `Unspecified` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]. Working group discussions evaluate whether to resolve the distinction via observed timing, subagent count, or strict causal dependency, and whether classification reflects an organization's specific runtime implementation or the intrinsic use case requirement [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

# Lifecycle History
PR#47 formally recorded the fan-out versus pipeline classification ambiguity as an open question in `schema-agentic-use-cases.md`, maintaining neutrality across interpretations while coordinating with joint reference architecture decision notes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task boundaries, deterministic acceptance checks, and reversible execution effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a workflow reference architecture for autonomously resolving bounded operational issues without requiring human approval on every iteration, provided independent acceptance evidence verifies the candidate result and the execution effect is strictly constrained[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. It stands as a contrasting counterpart to [Single-Agent Human Approval](./single-agent-human-approval.md), removing in-band human gates only when deterministic evidence gates can reliably assess outputs and non-convergence paths escalate safely[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Guarantees

The architecture enforces four runtime guarantees[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
1. **Bounded Autonomy:** The agent operates exclusively within the task contract, allowed tools, data, credentials, and budget declared for a single run.
2. **Independent Acceptance:** An independent deterministic gate, rather than the agent itself, evaluates whether candidate results satisfy declared acceptance conditions.
3. **Controlled Effect:** Only the exact, verified result is transmitted to the constrained effect executor; the agent cannot directly invoke high-impact capabilities.
4. **Safe Non-Convergence:** Exhausted budgets, missing evidence, scope violations, or repeated failures terminate in recorded outcomes and escalate to human-owned processes.

### Pattern Composition

Bounded Autonomous Remediation composes three foundational patterns[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
- [Bounded Convergence Loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Drives iterative refinement in an isolated workspace against an explicit operational budget.
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Runs automated tests, contract checks, and schema validation against candidate outputs.
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Physically decouples candidate generation from the external execution executor.

### Qualification Checklist

A workflow qualifies for this architecture if and only if all of the following criteria are met[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
- The task contract, allowed scope, and acceptance criteria are explicitly bounded before execution begins.
- An independent, deterministic gate can meaningfully assess the candidate result.
- The execution effect is constrained and low-impact or reversible (e.g., opening a pull request, creating draft records).
- The agent environment is isolated from authoritative production systems.
- A safe non-success escalation path exists for budget exhaustion or gate rejections.

### Validated Scenarios

The architecture has been validated against production maintenance scenarios, including an automated night-shift maintenance run where routine dependency and configuration fixes are generated, checked against multi-criteria test gates, and committed as draft pull requests[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Reference Architecture Validation Guide defines the standardized evaluation framework for testing AAIF workflow reference architectures against real-world use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35]. It establishes repeatable scoring categories and structured artifact formats for validation records submitted via GitHub issues and pull requests[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

# Architecture / Specification

### Architectural Fit Classifications

Validation assessments classify the architectural compatibility of a candidate use case into four standard ratings[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35]:

- **Validated:** The use case fully matches the reference architecture's structural boundaries, pattern composition, and execution guarantees without requiring architectural exceptions.
- **Partial:** The use case conforms to the core execution model but diverges in specific boundary controls, tooling requirements, or peripheral capabilities.
- **No Fit:** The use case violates core architectural assumptions (e.g., attempting bounded autonomy without independent acceptance gates, or omitting human checkpoints where required).
- **Candidate:** The use case has been proposed and documented as an illustrative scenario but lacks empirical execution data or an authoritative Use Case Inventory backing[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

### Contribution and Lifecycle

Validation records are linked directly to architecture specifications—such as [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)—and indexed in working group documentation to prevent theoretical drift[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Accuracy & Reliability Survey
proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question evaluation instrument measuring production deployment stages, failure frequencies, quality evidence, and intervention mechanisms across agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Accuracy & Reliability Survey is a platform-neutral assessment instrument developed by the [Accuracy & Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to gather firsthand operational telemetry and practitioner experiences across production AI deployments[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. The instrument benchmarks agent reliability, impact discovery timing, failure modes, and verification mechanisms across organizations[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

# Architecture / Specification

### Response Mechanics and Eligibility

The survey utilizes four input formats: single-select, multi-select, single-response Likert matrices, and conditional inline text[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

Eligibility is determined via Q1 filtering across deployment maturity over the preceding six months[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]:
- **Eligible pathways:** Serious pilots, limited deployments, broad deployments, paused/retired production systems, or indeterminate real-world use.
- **Early-exit disqualifications:** Demos, prototypes, generic research, secondhand knowledge, or absence of relevant system experience.

### Focal-System Protocol

Respondents evaluate a single qualifying "focal system" throughout the remaining 15 questions to ensure data consistency[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. The questionnaire captures data across four structured dimensions:
1. **System Attributes:** Direct respondent roles, organizational scale, and technical structure.
2. **Benefits and Challenges:** Human checking frequency, operational constraints, and realized impact.
3. **Accuracy and Reliability Factors:** Frequency of unacceptable outputs, recognition points (pre-impact vs. post-impact), severity of consequences, and quality verification methods.
4. **Future Priorities:** Industry-wide shared priorities and open-source tooling needs[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].
