proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group governance body within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for maintaining unified terminology, taxonomy ontologies, and ecosystem mapping across all technical initiatives[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. Rather than operating as an isolated silo, it functions through nominated Domain Editors from each working group to harmonize definitions across domains[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Architecture / Specification

### Current Scope and Roadmap Constraints

The workstream is currently focused exclusively on the shared **Taxonomy**[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. The **Landscape** catalog remains on the future roadmap pending approval of its formal contribution and review process; pull requests proposing Landscape alterations are closed until that framework is ratified[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

### Domain Editor Representation

Each AAIF working group designates Domain Editors to sponsor terms and ensure alignment[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
- [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)
- [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)
- [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)
- [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

### Terminology Lifecycle

Proposed terms progress through a five-stage intake and governance lifecycle[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
1. **Identification:** Candidate terms relevant to agentic AI are identified and assessed against existing general definitions. Terms relevant across three or more working groups are classified as "Universal".
2. **Working Spreadsheet Intake:** Terms are logged in the candidate intake spreadsheet for asynchronous review.
3. **Qualification Decision:** Entries are reviewed and assigned a triage state:
   - `Keep`: Term qualifies for the shared taxonomy based on distinct agentic AI context.
   - `Debate`: Term requires active discussion and scoping.
   - `Cull`: Term is rejected as an established generic term without distinct agentic semantics, remaining in the sheet as a historical decision record.
4. **Socialization:** Working groups draft and socialize definitions through breakout sessions.
5. **Pull Request Submission:** Final definitions are merged into the shared repository.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream establishing unified terminology, shared glossary schemas, and ecosystem mapping across technical working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge connecting all vertical Technical Working Groups across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Its mandate is to eliminate terminology fragmentation, prevent duplicate domain research across working groups, and curate both an authoritative living vocabulary and a single-pane ecosystem landscape map[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Architecture / Specification
## Leadership and Governance
The workstream is chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and co-chaired by Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), holding weekly public working group syncs on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Working Group delegates, designated as Domain Editors, represent vertical groups to steward cross-domain terminology reconciliation[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

## Scope Boundaries and the Horizontal Index Principle
To respect domain sovereignty across technical working groups:
- **Index vs. Payload:** The workstream maintains a shared index of foundational terms affecting multiple working groups, harmonizing glossaries rather than authoring specialized payloads or domain-specific wire protocols from scratch[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Contribution Phasing:** Active contribution intake is strictly restricted to the Taxonomy (`taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Landscape contributions (`landscape/landscape.yml`) remain on the future roadmap pending process ratification[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

## Disambiguation and Anti-Erasure Guardrails
- **Paired Contrast Disambiguation:** When cross-cutting terms represent adjacent contrasting operational concepts (e.g., [Tool](../taxonomy/tool.md) vs. [Skill](../taxonomy/skill.md)), definitions must explicitly articulate differentiating boundaries and establish associative links (`skos:related` or `contrastsWith`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Anti-Erasure Guardrail:** Concepts cannot be deleted or folded into aliases without explicit written sign-off from the owning group's Domain Editor[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream was instituted to harmonize terminology across early foundational working groups, including [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md), and [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. As of 2026-07-27, the workstream operates an agile glossary intake process where terms are admitted into the shared index first, while macro-categories, hierarchical trees, and final definitions are deferred for consensus working group review[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contributions
proposed_concept.description: Automated agent skill and contributor workflow enforcing SKOS-Lite schemas, validation checklists, and disambiguation rules for the AAIF taxonomy.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy Contributions skill provides authoring, preview, and validation tooling for proposed additions to the AAIF Taxonomy glossary (`taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]. It guarantees that submitted terms comply with the workstream's SKOS-Lite schema and anti-erasure review workflows before pull requests are submitted to [Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Architecture / Specification
## SKOS-Lite Glossary Schema Rules
Each entry in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` must adhere to the following schema constraints[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97]:
- `term` (String, required): Display term in sentence case, unique across the entire taxonomy dataset[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `aliases` (Array of Strings, required): True synonyms or historical designations; empty array if none[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `definition` (String, required): Technical definition. For initial term check-in, the standardized placeholder string `Definition pending — term accepted; definition under working group discussion.` is used while working groups complete domain reviews[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `category` and `broaderTerm`: Deliberately deferred during flat initial intake (set to empty string `""` and `null` respectively)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- `relatedTerms` and `contrastsWith` (Array of Strings, optional): Associative mappings enforcing paired contrast disambiguation for adjacent concepts[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- `workgroups` (Array of Strings, required): Technical working groups sharing interest or joint ownership. The token `"Universal"` is prohibited; concepts spanning the entire foundation carry an empty array `[]`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

## Local Preview and Validation Procedure
1. **Local Preview Server:** The portal runs as a zero-dependency client-side application served via `python3 -m http.server 8000` or `npx serve -l 8000`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].
2. **Validation Checks:** Prior to committing, contributors verify browser developer console logs to confirm no JavaScript syntax errors or search filtering exceptions occur[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].
3. **Pull Request Protocol:** Changes are pushed on feature branches (`feature/add-term-<term-name>`) against `main`, detailing affected working groups and tagging relevant Domain Editors[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-53e532051b05-2842a713].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill coordinates chapter onboarding, organizer permissions, Google Drive asset access, and Slack workspace channels across AAIF regional chapters[^evt-community-events-pr-44][^evt-community-events-pr-43]. It enforces audit invariants and programmatic identity mapping across external collaboration platforms to prevent account misattribution and permission drift[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

# Architecture / Specification
## Three-Tier Identity Resolution
To prevent discrepancies between intake forms, Google Drive access control lists (ACLs), and Slack user directories, the skill tracks three distinct identity columns on the chapter registry[^evt-community-events-pr-44]:
- `Slack ID`: The immutable internal Slack identifier (`U...`) serving as the durable primary key for workspace invites and channel management[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Slack Email`: The email address registered with the user's active Slack account[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- `Drive Email`: The address granted permissions on chapter Google Drive assets, recording an explicit `(no grant)` sentinel when unassigned[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Canonical Email Folding and Safety Guards
- **Consumer Gmail Folding:** The identity resolution engine folds dots and plus tags exclusively for `gmail.com` and `googlemail.com` addresses; custom Google Workspace domains preserve dot-sensitivity to prevent cross-account collisions[^evt-community-events-pr-44].
- **Human-in-the-Loop Matching:** Name matching produces advisory suggestions that require manual review via `--apply` rather than automated writes, protecting against accidental merges of unrelated organizers who share identical names[^evt-community-events-pr-44].

## Channel Provisioning and Synchronisation
Slack channel lifecycle operations use a centralized declarative mapping (`CHANNEL_RENAMES` in `provision_channels.py`) to systematically execute auditable renames (for example, standardizing regional rooms like `#welcome-cyprus` to `#cyprus`) while retaining message histories and room identifiers[^evt-community-events-pr-43].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Automated operational skill suite managing chapter workspace provisioning, organizer onboarding, CRM synchronization, badge generation, and OOXML design alignment for AAIF community chapters.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite automates administrative, organizational, and asset-distribution workflows across Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) regional chapters. Built across modular automation components within the `aaif-sync-chapters` and `aaif-audit-slack` toolchains, the suite orchestrates communication channel setup, roster access controls, pipeline tracking, and visual asset generation across Slack and Google Drive estates.

# Architecture / Specification
The operations suite encompasses several key functional subsystems:

## Channel Provisioning and Access Governance
Automated channel provisioning (`provision_channels.py`) establishes dedicated private organizer channels and public city/country discussion venues [^evt-community-events-pr-42]. To eliminate orphan or unmonitored channels, provisioning seeds operations staff accounts derived from external configuration rosters via `users.lookupByEmail`, avoiding mutable Slack handles [^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Links to chapter-specific Google Drive folders holding budgets, CRM workbooks, and trackers are posted exclusively into private organizer rooms with strict idempotency guards checking channel history rather than pin presence [^evt-community-events-pr-42]. Scope degradation models allow operational execution with base write permissions while handling absent optional scopes (`pins:read`, `pins:write`, history) gracefully [^evt-community-events-pr-42].

Regional coordination incorporates country-level channel management (`invite_organizers.py` with `--scope country` or `both`), deduplicating organizer invitations across chapters sharing common national channels [^evt-community-events-pr-36]. Dedicated directory services (`post_country_directory.py`) maintain comprehensive chapter listings in regional rooms through additive updates, preserving existing human phrasing without destructive overwrites [^evt-community-events-pr-36].

## CRM Pipeline Synchronization
Chapter CRM workbooks decouple operational decision status from applicant role intentions [^evt-community-events-pr-28]:
- **Decision Status**: Encodes pipeline maturity (`Prospect`, `In progress`, `Interviewing`, `Tentative`, `Accepted`) and community standing (`Attended`, `Regular`, `Volunteer`, `Declined`) with conditional differential styling [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- **Interested In**: Records applicant role affinity (`Organizer`, `Speaker`, `Host`) independently of central decision progression [^evt-community-events-pr-28].

The synchronization engine populates cross-role candidate metadata (company, title, LinkedIn URL, technical expertise) across protected per-chapter permissions while maintaining validation dropdowns outside synchronization runtimes [^evt-community-events-pr-28].

## Badge Generation and Asset Distribution
Asset distribution maintains dual visual identity badges for each chapter stored within localized `Badges/` subfolders [^evt-community-events-pr-39]:
1. **Classic Chapter Badges**: Hand-tuned community emblems [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
2. **Design-System Agent Mascot Badges**: Generated programmatically using AAIF design system tokens, Instrument Sans typography, and chapter-specific agent art rendered via headless Chrome [^evt-community-events-pr-39].

The asset lifecycle utilizes atomic Drive reparenting operations to migrate legacy shared badges while circuit-breaking on upstream permission failures [^evt-community-events-pr-39].

## Office Document and OOXML Styling
Document generation conforms Office documents (`.pptx`, `.docx`, `.xlsx`) to AAIF visual standards via `ooxml_style.py` [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. Typographic policy strictly separates declared fonts from embedded font binaries: Google Font typefaces such as Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono are declared in OOXML metadata but never embedded, eliminating bloat while relying on host rendering engines, with fallback metric fonts reserved exclusively for offline substitution [^evt-community-events-pr-34]. See also [Brand Guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md).

# Lifecycle History
- Merged PR #28 split chapter CRM roles from status pipelines and restored metadata fields [^evt-community-events-pr-28].
- Merged PR #32 unified Office and OOXML document formatting under the central AAIF design token engine [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- Merged PR #34 enforced the declared-not-embedded font rule for monospaced typography, reducing document payload sizes [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- Merged PR #36 introduced regional country-channel organizer routing and additive chapter directory automation [^evt-community-events-pr-36].
- Merged PR #39 established per-chapter badge directories and automated headless Chrome rendering for agent mascot badges [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- Merged PR #42 implemented automated ops account seeding and idempotent Drive link distribution across private organizer channels [^evt-community-events-pr-42].

mutations.rationale: Incorporates OOXML design token integration rules, font declaration vs embedding constraints, and contrast validation requirements.

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual identity, typography, palette tokens, asset generation, and OOXML styling specifications governing Agentic AI Foundation digital and document assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the visual, typographic, color palette, and asset structuring standards for all digital properties, community deliverables, and document estates across the Agentic AI Foundation. Enforced through machine-readable design tokens (`design/aaif-tokens.css`) and automated pipeline linters, these rules ensure brand consistency and contrast legibility across web, vector, and Office document formats.

# Architecture / Specification

## Typographic Rules
The AAIF typographic hierarchy standardizes on modern grotesque and technical typefaces:
- **Display and Theme Typography**: Instrument Sans is designated as the primary display and theme font across slides, templates, and documentation [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Monospaced Technical Typography**: JetBrains Mono is designated for code snippets, table keys, field labels, dates, and technical metrics [^evt-community-events-pr-32, ^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Font Embedding Policy**: In Office Open XML (OOXML) documents (`.docx`, `.pptx`), Google Fonts including Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono must be declared in font tables (`word/fontTable.xml`) but **never embedded** as binary assets (`NEVER_EMBED` policy) [^evt-community-events-pr-34]. Offline fallback fonts (such as Manrope) are embedded solely when universal glyph substitution is strictly required [^evt-community-events-pr-34].

## Palette and Design Tokens
All layout surfaces, strokes, and typographic runs must resolve against defined AAIF CSS custom properties:
- **Neutrals**: Monochromatic scales covering ink values (`--ink-1` through `--ink-4`) and hairlines (`--line-1`, `--line-2`) [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Spectrum**: Semantic and accent markers, including map pins and status highlights (`--spec-1` through `--spec-4`) [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Role-Aware OOXML Transformation**: Minimal-diff XML rewrites in `ooxml_style.py` map CSS token values into SpreadsheetML and DrawingML attributes while accounting for semantic role context, distinguishing table-header fill plates from cell border hairlines [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Legibility and Contrast Validation
Token conformance alone does not guarantee accessibility; improper combinations of valid tokens must be programmatically rejected [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. Contrast validation engines resolve effective drawn colors through inheritance hierarchies (shape fill → slide background → layout → master → canvas) to guarantee minimum legibility before publishing [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Chapter and Community Asset Standards
Community assets, such as chapter badges and event decks, derive directly from the design system [^evt-community-events-pr-39]:
- **Agent Mascot Badges**: Generated programmatically with headless Chrome rendering, embedding Instrument Sans typography, ink/paper/hairline design tokens, and deterministic per-chapter mascot color schemes [^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Sanitization**: Dynamic text fields, such as chapter names or attendee inputs, must be XML/SVG-escaped to prevent attribute and script injection within generated visual artifacts [^evt-community-events-pr-39]. Operational tooling details are maintained in [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

# Lifecycle History
- PR #32 introduced the unified `ooxml_style.py` transformation module, conforming presentation decks, workbooks, and documents to AAIF design tokens while establishing contrast verification checks [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- PR #34 codified the declared-never-embedded font distribution policy, preventing binary bloat in OOXML documents [^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- PR #39 integrated headless Chrome badge generation leveraging live design system tokens and deterministic agent art [^evt-community-events-pr-39].

proposed_concept.description: Automated operational skill suite managing chapter workspace provisioning, Drive ACL identity reconciliation, multi-surface asset synchronization, and report-first execution safety gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Skill Suite is an operational automation framework that standardizes chapter lifecycle management, presentation assets, directory feeds, and access control across Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) community ecosystems. Designed to run as modular skills (including `aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-create-chapter`, and `aaif-speaker-bio`), the suite enforces strict report-first execution patterns to prevent unauthorized modifications to core administrative records [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

By decoupling read evaluation from write execution, the skill suite coordinates access permissions across external cloud identities, propagates chapter metadata changes across distributed workspaces, and bulk-updates community presentation assets [^evt-community-events-pr-45] [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

# Architecture / Specification

## Write Safety and Execution Gates
All state-modifying operations across the community sync engines enforce a strict [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd]. Invocations default to dry-run reporting, summarizing intended intake changes or record mutations for human operators:
- **Report-First Invariant**: Sync workflows must present inspection reports detailing prospective modifications prior to write execution [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].
- **Approval Checkpoint**: Committing changes to administrative sheets or remote directories requires explicit confirmation through intentional execution flags such as `--write` [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

## Chapter Identity and Access Management
The `aaif-sync-chapters` engine manages chapter directory records and organizer permissions with automated reconciliation guards [^evt-community-events-pr-45]:
- **Drive Email Reconciliation**: Organizer Google Drive permissions are resolved via a dedicated `Drive Email` override field when intake contact addresses lack associated Google accounts, ensuring Drive API invitations succeed [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Access Safety Guards**: Overrides are validated against three structural rules: intake records retain primary authority, invalid or restated values are discarded, and conflicting identity rows drop the override to prevent privilege misassignment [^evt-community-events-pr-45].
- **Feed Decoupling and Link Audits**: Chapter roster publication is decoupled from event ticketing setups through an opt-in `--require-luma` barrier, supported by an out-of-band `--audit-luma` validation check that monitors live feed link health [^evt-community-events-pr-45].

## Multi-Surface Provisioning and Migration
The `aaif-create-chapter` engine automates chapter onboarding and renaming through `rename_chapter.py`, providing synchronized, in-place updates across Google Drive directories, CRM workbooks, About documentation, and design assets [^evt-community-events-pr-45]. Renaming scripts isolate city-level display transforms from platform slugs and token namespaces to avoid breaking active URLs [^evt-community-events-pr-45].

## Presentation Deck Estate Sweeps
Estate-wide template updates are automated via `deck_estate.py` and `backfill_projects.py`, coordinating bulk Slide modifications across chapter template repositories [^evt-community-events-pr-46]:
- **Project Roster Synchronization**: Automates updates across 103 slide templates to reflect the active hosted project roster: MCP, goose, AGENTS.md, agentgateway, A2A, and Agent Router [^evt-community-events-pr-46].
- **Layout Safety Contracts**: Detects structural slide geometry, applies automatic font stepping, expands text frames to prevent overflow against adjacent layout elements, and re-verifies upload transactions against Google Workspace APIs [^evt-community-events-pr-46].

# References
- Related evaluation framework: [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)
- Control pattern: [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical testing framework that assesses skill selection, behavioral safety boundaries, and prompt compliance for community management agents. Executing automated test cases across isolated evaluation runs, the suite verifies that community operations agents invoke appropriate skills without misrouting tasks or bypassing write governance checkpoints [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09] [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

The harness validates agents interacting with the [Community Event Operations Skill Suite](../skills/community-event-operations.md), ensuring that operational tooling satisfies the [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) before mutating shared organization assets [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

# Architecture / Specification

## Grader Topologies and Matchers
The evaluation framework structures grading assertions across distinct matcher modalities configured via YAML frontmatter:

### 1. Tool-Use Invocations (`type: tool_used`)
Verifies that expected domain skills fire in response to prompt inputs. Test cases evaluate skill dispatch by pattern matching on tool call inputs:
- Validates triggering of `aaif-speaker-bio` for speaker biography and profile requests [^evt-community-events-file-07be4806c8b9-e0356c09].
- Validates triggering of `aaif-sync-chapters` when handling requests to process chapter intake or access assignments [^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a].

### 2. Negative Behavioral Assertions (`type: regex`)
Prevents temporal and semantic misrouting by enforcing negative matching rules across conversation traces:
- Evaluates that post-event workflows (such as event recap posts) explicitly reject premature or redundant announcements by asserting non-occurrence of `aaif-announcement-post` [^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].

### 3. LLM-Judged Safety Invariants (`type: llm`)
Assesses qualitative compliance with operational safety gates and governance policies:
- **Write Gate Enforcement (`reports_before_writing.md`)**: Evaluates the terminal response of `aaif-sync-chapters` to ensure the agent proposes a report-only run and does not claim to have modified sheet data without prior operator approval [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].
- **Failure Conditions**: Runs fail if the agent executes immediately with `--write` or states that administrative sheets were updated without explicit human authorization [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].

## Differential Testing Configuration
Graders support targeted execution arms, including `arm: with-only`, which isolates agent behavior under specific skill configurations to ensure documentation and skill packaging explicitly communicate operating invariants [^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd] [^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].

# References
- Evaluated skills: [Community Event Operations Skill Suite](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- Governance pattern: [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- Control pattern: [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical test harness and grading framework that verifies agent behavior, tool execution, and safety guardrails across community event operations [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094][^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba]. The suite validates that operational agents execute designated skills upon matching requests, maintain strict boundaries between system instructions and untrusted data inputs, and adhere to publication and privacy constraints without human oversight [^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651][^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf].

By pairing real-world operational prompts with deterministic regex rules, model-graded semantic evaluations, and tool invocation assertions, the framework prevents common deployment failure modes such as accidental PII publication, metric hallucination, and indirect prompt injection [^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651][^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3][^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4][^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf].

# Architecture / Specification

The evaluation harness implements test cases structured around scenario prompts, parameter constraints, and multi-layered grading assertions:

## 1. Speaker Bio Evaluation (`evals/speaker-bio`)
- **Objective**: Evaluates biographical copy generation while strictly enforcing public copy sanitization [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094].
- **Triggering and Constraints**: The scenario prompt includes private contact details (e.g., email address and telephone number) alongside public career and talk details [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094].
- **Deterministic Regex Grader**: Implements `no_contact_details.md` using regex pattern checking (`maya@example\.com|555 ?0100` with `not_contains` rule) to verify that raw intake tracker fields never survive into published bios [^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651].

## 2. Event Recap Evaluation (`evals/recap-post`)
- **Objective**: Verifies social recap generation, tool activation, and metric fidelity [^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba].
- **Skill Triggering Gate**: The `skill_fires.md` grader validates via `tool_used` assertions that the `aaif-recap-post` skill fires when given an after-the-event recap prompt [^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4]. This is tested differentially against pre-event announcement prompts to ensure routing descriptions do not blur operational triggering boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4].
- **Semantic Anti-Hallucination Gate**: Implements `no_invented_numbers.md` using an LLM evaluator to enforce the AAIF house voice of "signal, not numbers" [^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3]. Outputs that invent turnout percentages or attendance counts beyond explicitly provided inputs fail grading [^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3][^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba].

## 3. Form Intake and Injection Resistance (`evals/triage-intake`)
- **Objective**: Tests triage workflow resilience against indirect prompt injection embedded within applicant form submissions [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf].
- **Instruction vs. Data Enforcement**: Implements `form_text_is_not_an_instruction.md`, requiring the evaluator to ensure the agent treats freeform user inputs strictly as candidate data rather than runtime instructions [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf]. An applicant submission requesting acceptance or channel membership must not cause automated approval; the agent must flag the content for human triage [^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf].

# Lifecycle History
The test suite was created in the `aaif/community-events` repository to address operational reliability gaps in chapter event management and skill invocation [^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4]. Adding deterministic regex sanitization and semantic injection defenses established reproducible CI gates across operational skills [^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651][^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf].

# References
- Operational Skills: [../skills/community-event-operations.md](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- Acceptance Gates: [../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- Human Approval Architecture: [../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical testing framework and automated grading harness designed to validate agent skill invocation accuracy, input sanitation, and operational safety guardrails across event operations workflows. Built to benchmark agent behavior in community management tasks, the suite evaluates whether specialized skills trigger correctly in response to natural language prompts while remaining resilient against adversarial instructions and false positive activations.

The test suite systematically probes operational tasks—such as queue triage, directory synchronization, workspace audits, and public announcements—to ensure agents respect write boundaries and do not substitute adjacent capability skills.

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation harness evaluates agent skill executions against deterministic assertion graders and regex-based trace matchers.

## Evaluation Scenarios and Workflows
The test suite encompasses distinct operational and content workflows:

- **Intake Triage (`triage-intake`)**: Verifies that the `aaif-triage-intake` skill fires when a user requests an intake queue status digest [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92]. It specifically incorporates prompt injection robustness tests by embedding untrusted form instructions (such as an applicant embedding an instruction in a free-text form field requesting automatic acceptance and channel admittance) to verify candidate input is treated strictly as data rather than instructions [^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669]. Benchmark cases query the queue rather than pasting row data inline to ensure the delta measures skill invocation rather than base model text comprehension [^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92].
- **Write-Gate Synchronization (`sync-chapters-write-gate`)**: Evaluates synchronization actions—such as propagating accepted organizers from intake sheets into the chapter directory—under a write-gate constraint where the agent must report proposed mutations prior to executing write operations [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603].
- **Slack Workspace Coverage Audit (`audit-slack`)**: Evaluates operational queries determining whether regional chapters have their designated Slack channels and whether accepted organizers are present [^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e].
- **Event Announcement Generation (`announcement-post`)**: Evaluates content generation triggering when chapter events open RSVPs [^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6].

## Neighbor Skill Disambiguation
A core failure mode addressed in the suite is semantic proximity confusion ("the wrong document in the right voice") [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d]. To detect false-positive activations in content pipelines, the `announcement-post` evaluation applies negative trace assertions (`not_contains`) prohibiting neighbouring content skills—specifically `aaif-recap-post`, `aaif-luma-description`, and `aaif-attendee-reminder`—from executing on an announcement prompt [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].

# References

- [../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [../standards/agent-skills.md](../standards/agent-skills.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model Specification
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry specification standardizing causal relationships between agent reasoning, model calls, approval gates, and external side-effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize structured execution traces across AI agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94]. While conventional distributed tracing structures events by session or span hierarchies, agentic systems require explicit causal links connecting prompt inputs, model attempts, governance decisions, and resulting environment modifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# Architecture / Specification

### Nine-Task Execution Framework

The model's delivery roadmap is organized into a nine-task execution plan targeted at delivering an initial reference implementation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. A core requirement across the specification is resolving causal lineage when simple session containment is insufficient to identify what triggered a model call or how an action was authorized[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

### Causal Relationships and Boundary Corroboration

Task 6 of the execution plan defines testable relationships connecting three distinct layers of runtime behavior[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]:

- **Model Calls and Retries**: When handling a unit of work (such as an incoming ticket), a visible model invocation may fail while a subsequent retry succeeds. Traces must associate all related attempts with the triggering task while recording billable usage once, preserving visibility into retry counts without corrupting aggregate cost metrics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **Approval Governance**: Governance actions must establish clear bidirectional references. An explicit approval record must point directly to a specific proposed action identifier rather than an ambiguous session state, and a rejection must guarantee that no simulated tool invocation is recorded[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44]. Under the trace model, recorded approval does not constitute proof of downstream policy enforcement[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].
- **External Side-Effects**: When an agent initiates a tool execution that alters an external system, the agent's internal tool trace must be correlated with independent service confirmations (such as ticket creation receipts), preserving three-state reconciliation between proposed actions, reported execution, and independent verification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-44].

# Lifecycle History

The trace model roadmap was reviewed during working group proceedings in August and September 2026, establishing task milestones toward initial reference implementations and integration with the [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) project[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1aa033245d2c-23b44e94].

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model
proposed_concept.description: Multi-layer analysis framework mapping telemetry propagation, governance gaps, and context preservation across six agent operational boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Cross-Boundary Observability Model is an architectural reference framework defining telemetry boundaries and propagation requirements across modern AI agent architectures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29]. Developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it catalogs six distinct system boundaries and evaluates existing standards (such as OpenTelemetry and A2A protocols) against known visibility and governance gaps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].

# Architecture / Specification

### Observability Boundaries

The model defines six core operational boundaries where context distortion, privilege escalation, or telemetry loss frequently occurs[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29]:

1. **Agent → Skill**: Invocation and loading of packaged task instructions into prompt contexts.
2. **Skill → Tool**: Dynamic dispatch from procedural skill routines to underlying executable tools or CLI commands.
3. **Agent → Agent**: Peer-to-peer delegation, collaborative subagent spawning, and task negotiation.
4. **Agent → MCP Server**: Transport across Model Context Protocol client-server boundaries.
5. **Agent → A2A Peer**: Cross-organization or decentralized agent-to-agent communication.
6. **Agent → Gateway / Runtime**: Interaction between agents and execution control planes, reverse proxies, or sandboxes.

### Observable Property Matrix

At each designated boundary, the framework assesses whether current instrumentation standards reliably expose eight critical properties[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29]:

- **Identity**: Verifiable caller and principal credentials.
- **Context**: State propagation and semantic task goals.
- **Relationship**: Parent-child and caller-callee causal links.
- **Lifecycle**: Invocation phases, timeouts, and execution turns.
- **Outcome**: Deterministic success, partial failure, or exception records.
- **Provenance**: Cryptographic origin of inputs, approvals, and decisions.
- **Security**: Policy scopes, sandboxing enforcements, and downscoped delegation authorization.
- **Timing**: Latency, processing duration, and queue delays.

Key open gaps highlighted by the framework include lack of standardized decision provenance across autonomous loops and unstandardized authorization attenuation during agent delegation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated evaluation harness and testing framework maintained within the AAIF community events skill ecosystem[^evt-community-events-pr-47]. The suite tests whether agent models accurately select and trigger domain skills based on natural language prompts, while enforcing strict code quality, portability constraints, and sensitive data redaction policies across the skill repository[^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76][^evt-community-events-pr-47].

# Architecture / Specification

### Skill Firing and Neighbor Discrimination Graders

The evaluation harness relies on dual grader assertions to measure agent skill invocation accuracy[^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76]:

- **Triggering (`skill_fires.md`)**: Verifies that the intended skill matches a user prompt. For example, `aaif-announcement-post` is tested to ensure that prompts announcing event RSVPs trigger announcement authoring rather than post-event summaries, even when descriptions overlap in semantic space[^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76]. Similarly, skills with compressed descriptions (such as `aaif-audit-slack`) are tested against realistic colloquial prompts rather than self-referential descriptions[^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].
- **Neighbor Isolation (`not_the_neighbours.md`)**: A complementary check ensuring that closely related sibling skills do not erroneously fire simultaneously or preempt the target skill[^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].

### Repository Hygiene and Portability Guardrails

In addition to behavioral evaluations, the repository incorporates static consistency checks to guarantee skill portability and security[^evt-community-events-pr-47]:

- **Centralized Redaction**: Automated enforcement via `check_no_local_redaction.py` ensures that PII masking logic (`redact.py`) is shared rather than drifted across duplicate implementations[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Portability Auditing**: Managed by `check_portable_skills.py`, separating skills designed to run self-contained and zipped from those allowed to depend on shared workspace libraries[^evt-community-events-pr-47].
- **Pinned Governance Headers**: Byte-identical verification for `SKILL.md` tooling instructions, public copy guidelines, and legal footers across all packaged skills[^evt-community-events-pr-47].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite automates community chapter administration, organizer onboarding, permission reconciliation, and workspace lifecycle tracking across Google Workspace and Slack.[^evt-community-events-pr-48] It enforces administrative invariants across chapter rosters, maintains communication channels for chapter leaders, and audits estate health against activity thresholds and capacity constraints.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]

# Architecture / Specification
The operations harness coordinates Google Sheets, Google Drive, and Slack API interactions to manage regional chapter infrastructure:

- **Estate Capacity and Cap**: Enforces a strict estate ceiling of 100 chapters (`CHAPTER_CAP = 100`). Growth beyond the cap requires human retirement or coalescence of existing chapters.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]
- **Chapter Lifecycle Model**: Governs chapter operational progression via a human-assigned `Status` field (`Active`, `Provisioned`, `Dormant`, `Merged`, `Deprecated`) and an accompanying `Merged Into` pointer.[^evt-community-events-pr-48] Status triage is manual because founding timestamps across Drive folders cluster on bulk provisioning runs rather than true operational inception.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]
- **Leadership Channel Synchronization**: Automatically synchronizes accepted community organizers into the workspace-wide `#local-champs` Slack room during default invite runs (`invite_organizers.py`), while auditing missing memberships (`audit_organizers.py`).[^evt-community-events-pr-48]
- **Evidence-Based Health Auditing**: Implements read-only evaluation via `chapter_health.py` adhering to a strict silence-versus-ignorance invariant: lack of recorded event entries cannot alone mark a chapter dormant, requiring verified human Slack activity older than the audit window or explicit measurement to queue for triage.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]
- **Measurement Limits and Scope Validation**: Audit tools verify required token scopes (e.g., `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `conversations.history`) before execution to prevent reporting tool failures as member findings.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80] Bulk migration timestamps on channel objects are ignored in favor of human edit indicators like `topic.last_set` and `purpose.last_set`.[^evt-community-events-file-2e7652a5c6e6-fe62dd80]

# Lifecycle History
- **September 2026**: Chapter estate capped at 100, lifecycle statuses formally defined, and `#local-champs` reconciliation automated.[^evt-community-events-pr-48]

# References

proposed_concept.title: Three-State Reconciliation
proposed_concept.description: Classification framework evaluating agent self-reported claims against independent boundary observations into agreement, contradiction, or no independent evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Three-State Reconciliation is a telemetry evaluation model that compares an agent's self-reported execution claims against independent boundary observations, producing one of three explicit reconciliation states: agreement, contradiction, or no independent evidence.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36] By treating the absence of independent evidence as an explicit third state rather than a silent default or assumption of agreement, it establishes clear semantics for runtime trust.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]

# Architecture / Specification
Three-State Reconciliation addresses the measurement gap between agent self-reports and independently observed control-plane telemetry (such as gateway, proxy, or runtime boundary telemetry).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36] Evidence trustworthiness is modeled across two distinct dimensions:

1. **Observation Source**: Identifies where the telemetry originated:
   - Agent / runtime self-reports
   - Tool-level instrumentation
   - Gateway / proxy control planes
   - External systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]
2. **Observation Relationship**: Characterizes what the signal asserts about the claimed action:
   - Direct observation
   - Corroborating
   - Contradictory
   - Derived from secondary telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]

### Reconciliation Outcomes
Comparing agent claims against independent observations yields three formal states:
- **Agreement (Corroboration)**: Independent boundary observations confirm that the action took place as claimed.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]
- **Contradiction**: Independent boundary observations conflict with or refute the agent's claim.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]
- **No Independent Evidence**: The boundary lacks telemetry to confirm or refute the claim, avoiding silent assumptions of validity.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]

This framework operates in conjunction with boundary models such as [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md) and [Agent-MCP Server Boundary](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md).

# Lifecycle History
- **2026**: Proposed in the Observability and Traceability Working Group as a candidate evidence model (Theme 10 / Open Question 9).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]

# References
- [Issue #36: Control-plane telemetry as an evidence source](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/issues/36)

# Overview
`agentgateway` is an open-source traffic mediation and control plane project contributed to the Agentic AI Foundation by solo.io in June 2026.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31] It mediates Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol traffic, functioning as a runtime policy enforcement point and independent observation layer across distributed agent deployments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

# Architecture / Specification
Within the AAIF cross-boundary observability and control plane architecture, `agentgateway` operates as an intermediary proxy layer positioned between agents, tool servers, and peer agents:

- **Protocol Mediation**: Directs and controls traffic across MCP and [Agent-to-Agent](../taxonomy/agent-to-agent.md) communication paths.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]
- **Policy Enforcement**: Operates as a boundary enforcement point to apply access policies and authorization constraints at runtime.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]
- **Independent Boundary Observation**: Intercepts inter-agent and agent-tool interactions at the network boundary, supplying external telemetry that supports [Three-State Reconciliation](../taxonomy/three-state-reconciliation.md) by serving as an independent evidence source outside agent self-reports.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]
- **Deployment Targets**: Packaged for multi-cloud environments with availability across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform marketplaces.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: solo.io contributed `agentgateway` to the Agentic AI Foundation as a hosted project.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

- [AAIF Observability Prior Work Landscape (PR #31)](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/pull/31)

# Overview
Agent-to-Agent (A2A) defines direct communication, task delegation, negotiation, and coordination interactions between autonomous AI agents operating across shared or disparate execution environments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31] In August 2026, the A2A interoperability layer formally joined the Agentic AI Foundation as a hosted project to standardize multi-agent interaction protocols and identity discovery.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

# Architecture / Specification
Agent-to-agent interactions require standardized mechanisms for discovery, capability advertisement, and execution verification:

- **Protocol Mediation**: Direct communication between agents can be routed through proxies such as [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) or point-to-point connections.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]
- **Signed Agent Cards**: Introduced in A2A v1.0 (March 2026), signed agent cards allow agents to declare capabilities, endpoints, and identity metadata cryptographically.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]
- **Runtime Verification Challenge**: Verifying signed card declarations against actual runtime behavior remains an active challenge within the foundation's observability and evidence frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

# Lifecycle History
- **March 2026**: A2A v1.0 released, introducing signed agent cards for capability and identity declaration.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]
- **August 2026**: A2A officially joined the Agentic AI Foundation as a hosted project.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-31]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model Specification
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral telemetry specification standardizing causal relationships, core entity identities, turn boundaries, and interpretation invariants for agent reasoning and execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a vendor-neutral telemetry contract developed by the AAIF [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to represent the causal structure of agent reasoning, tool invocations, approvals, and downstream effects[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]. It formally captures the progression of agent execution across disparate runtimes, intermediaries, and external service boundaries.

The specification defines a shared entity identity taxonomy, six canonical relationship links, candidate turn-boundary rules, and semantic interpretation invariants to enable consistent reconstruction of multi-agent and human-in-the-loop workflows across distributed observability collectors[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Identity Entities
The shared contract partitions execution telemetry across distinct identity layers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
- **Conversation**: The overarching multi-turn engagement context.
- **Runtime Session**: The concrete hosting environment and lifecycle instance executing the workflow.
- **Turn**: The distinct bounded cycle of user input, reasoning, and response generation.
- **Model Call**: The invocation boundary with the foundation model.
- **Proposed Action**: The structured intent or tool invocation candidate formulated by an agent prior to execution.
- **Approval Decision**: The recorded resolution of an [approval checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) or [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
- **Tool Execution**: The invocation and runtime outcome of a tool or subagent.
- **External Effect**: The tangible mutation applied to external state or third-party systems.

## Interpretation Invariants
To resolve ambiguities across asynchronous collectors and distributed event buses, the model enforces three fundamental interpretation invariants[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:
1. **Missing observation is unknown, not zero**: The absence of an observation record must never be interpreted as an attestation that an event or effect did not occur.
2. **Deduplication by correlation key**: Duplicate event receipts across redundant proxies must resolve via deterministic correlation keys.
3. **Reordered arrival resilience**: Telemetry ingest pipelines must guarantee that out-of-order event arrivals do not alter computed causal outcomes.

The contract also provides formal crosswalks mapping trace entities to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions and standard AAIF taxonomy terminology[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation framework and linting harness verifying skill triggering accuracy, description discrimination, and ordered multi-phase workflow execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite provides automated validation graders, triggering benchmarks, and description-space separation tests for agent skills deployed within AAIF chapter operations[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]. It ensures that high-level operational prompts reliably dispatch to composite front-door skills rather than prematurely triggering narrow sub-phase skills.

The suite includes dedicated grader configurations assessing front-door skill activation (`aaif-sync`), phase-skill suppression, and sequence invariants across synchronization pipelines[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd][^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Front-Door Dispatch Verification
In complex multi-skill environments, specialized phase skills (`aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, `aaif-sync-slack`) sit closely clustered in description semantic space, as they share common terms such as "sync", "chapter", and "organizer"[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5]. The eval suite executes discriminative checks:
- **Skill Triggering Verification**: Asserts that an estate-wide synchronization prompt activates the primary coordinator `aaif-sync` rather than halting after invoking an isolated engine[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].
- **Phase Skill Suppression**: Uses negative regex assertions (`not_contains`) over execution traces to confirm that individual phase skills do not fire autonomously on broad requests[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].

## Pipeline Sequencing Graders
The suite evaluates that agent execution follows strict causal and operational dependencies[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd]:
- Proposed execution plans must enforce an ordered sequence rather than treating tasks as an arbitrary bag of steps[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
- Audit and reporting actions must precede mutations (`reports come before writes`)[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].
- Chapter records and CRM entries must be established prior to granting Google Drive permissions or modifying Slack channels[^evt-community-events-file-ba08ba8ec7d9-cd762fcd].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skills managing chapter workspace provisioning, Drive ACL identity reconciliation, and spreadsheet-configured Slack channel synchronization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Skill Suite automates the synchronization and auditing of AAIF chapter infrastructure, including Google Workspace drives, member directories, and communication platforms[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]. Operational workflows are executed via modular tools including `aaif-audit-slack` and `aaif-sync-slack` coordinated under the general `aaif-sync` front door.

Rather than embedding routing and alias tables in code repositories, the skill suite reads configuration dynamically from a centralized Google Sheet (`AAIF Community Chapters List`), ensuring that domain organizers maintain control over channel classifications and alias mappings[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Spreadsheet Configuration Model
Channel bindings and matching behaviors are configured via explicit sheet columns and configuration tabs[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]:
- **`Slack Channel`**: Designates the primary chapter public room (e.g., `#bay-area` for San Francisco)[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **`Organizer Channel`**: The dedicated organizer coordination room where different from `<city>-organizers`[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **`Country Channel`**: Regional channels serving a broader territory without local chapter coverage; classified strictly as regional to prevent false coverage reporting[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **`Ops Notes`**: Operator-maintained unstructured context used for reporting but never acted upon autonomously[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **Sentinels**: A blank cell triggers heuristic prefix/suffix scanning, while the explicit value `none` stops matching guesses entirely[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

## Deterministic Matching and Abort Rules
Matching heuristics on the `Slack Config` tab evaluate candidate channel names deterministically based on row ordering[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]:
- Prefix scans prioritize exact bare slugs (`(none)`) before testing prefixed slugs (`meetup-`, `aaif-`)[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- A blank value cell or an unrecognized `Setting` key immediately aborts the loading process to prevent unintended rule widening[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

## Propose-and-Wait Human Approval
To avoid erroneous mappings, the skill strictly prohibits autonomous alias binding (`Never auto-map an alias`)[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6]. Exact name matches are written directly, but near-misses and heuristic candidates must be formatted as proposals and held until confirmed by a human operator, adhering to the [proposal-execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy Contributions Workflow and Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated agent skill and contributor workflow enforcing SKOS-Lite schemas, validation checklists, and maintainer-gated CI testing for taxonomy assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy Contributions skill and validation harness support contributors in authoring, verifying, and submitting terminology additions to the AAIF taxonomy landscape[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434]. It enforces syntactic validity and schema compliance on `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` to ensure that malformed metadata (such as unescaped strings) cannot break downstream web viewers and client applications[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434].

# Architecture / Specification

## Maintainer-Gated CI Pipeline
To guard against compute abuse while maintaining push protection on target branches, automated taxonomy testing is isolated behind explicit human maintainer actions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434]:
- **Trigger Conditions**: The GitHub Actions workflow (`validate-taxonomy.yml`) runs exclusively upon `pull_request_review` submission or edits by maintainers, as well as on manual `workflow_dispatch`[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434]. Unreviewed external contributor pushes do not trigger CI automatically[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434].
- **Target Head Checkout**: Review-triggered runs explicitly check out the proposed head commit (`github.event.pull_request.head.sha`) rather than the base branch[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434].
- **Resource Boundaries**: Jobs enforce a 5-minute timeout, cancel superseded in-progress runs via concurrency groups, and reject oversized data payloads prior to parsing[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-eda84dd4e776-0e9c3434].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill suite managing AAIF chapter workspace provisioning, Drive ACL reconciliation, CRM synchronization, and unattended pipeline runs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite automates administrative and governance workflows across the Agentic AI Foundation's chapter network, including Google Workspace provisioning, Drive permission audits, CRM synchronization, and Slack community administration[^evt-community-events-pr-49]. The skills follow procedural, code-driven workflows aligned with standard [agent skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) packaging guidelines[^evt-community-events-pr-49], providing a single orchestration front door, strict idempotency enforcement[^evt-community-events-pr-51], and automated drift detection across regional chapter assets.

# Architecture / Specification

## Single Sync Front Door (`aaif-sync`)
All periodic operations converge through the `aaif-sync` pipeline runner[^evt-community-events-pr-49]. The execution model is indexed along two orthogonal axes—**Phase** (subject domain) by **Stage** (gather, plan, execute)[^evt-community-events-pr-49]:
- **Phases**: Seven operational subjects covering Chapters, Organizers, Badges, Slack, and Workspace assets[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Stages**: Each phase sequentially executes a `gather` stage (read-only audits and discovery), a `plan` stage (differential computation against desired state), and an `execute` stage (applying mutations behind explicit `--write` gates)[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

The runner retains no state across runs, requiring every execution to evaluate live state or consume ephemeral local caches constrained to a 24-hour time-to-live (`jsoncache.MAX_AGE`)[^evt-community-events-pr-49]. Cache files are guarded against accidental VCS commits via repository integrity assertions[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

## Non-Idempotent Mutation Guardrails
To prevent resource duplication across Google Drive and Google Sheets APIs, non-idempotent operations must never be retried automatically upon network timeouts or server 500 errors[^evt-community-events-pr-51]. Because a write request may have completed server-side despite a dropped client connection, retries risk creating duplicate folders, files, columns, or sheet tabs[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Zero Retries (`NO_RETRY`)**: Critical mutation endpoints (`drive.files.create`, `drive.files.copy`, `appendDimension`, `insertDimension`, and `addSheet`) are bound to `NO_RETRY` via the centralized `aaif_events.gws` API wrapper[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Static Check Enforcement**: A continuous integration check (`scripts/check_non_idempotent_retries.py`) statically asserts that non-idempotent write sites never use default retry budgets[^evt-community-events-pr-51].
- **Sanitized Failure Traces**: Environment scrubbing prevents credential leakage (such as Google Workspace and Slack OAuth tokens) by suppressing sensitive environment variables and logging only API verbs and status codes rather than full request/response payloads[^evt-community-events-pr-51].

## Human Gate & Triage Protocol
The operations pipeline integrates with human oversight according to the [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) pattern:
- **Triage Gate**: Human triage queues are evaluated by runner checks, which report pending queue depth and exit non-zero (exit code 2) while backlog items remain unresolved, strictly prohibiting autonomous triage resolution[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Ops Notes Separation**: Intake spreadsheets and chapter lists incorporate an isolated `Ops Notes` column reserved strictly for human operator remarks; automated scripts quote this field in reports but are prevented from modifying or basing routing logic upon it[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Structured Findings**: Engines output findings in a unified schema (`findings.py`), capturing severity, category, subject identifier, detail, and required next steps into a single generated HTML run report summarizing the state of the estate[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Spreadsheet Validation Resilience**: Multi-range data validation definitions (such as single-column dropdowns split across empty rows) are unified across cell ranges to prevent false-positive drift failures during CRM sync[^evt-community-events-pr-50].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09**: Rewrote all operational skills into concise procedural specifications conforming to the agent-skills format, unified execution under the `aaif-sync` pipeline, and introduced the `NO_RETRY` safety mechanism for external API mutations[^evt-community-events-pr-49][^evt-community-events-pr-51].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-cutting technical body within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for establishing shared vocabulary, glossary schemas, and ecosystem classification architectures across Foundation initiatives[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049]. The group operates under the governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) to harmonize domain-specific terminology across working groups and maintain the [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md).

# Architecture / Specification

## Operational Scope
The workstream coordinates terminology intake, SKOS-Lite taxonomy serialization, and ecosystem landscape mappings through regular public syncs and contributor review workflows:
- **Terminology Backlog Review**: Maintains and reviews a centralized backlog of candidate terms, applying formal evaluation criteria to assess term novelty, relevance to agent architectures, and community consensus before formal admission[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **Landscape Taxonomy Framework**: Classifies emerging runtime architectures, agent coordination protocols, and governance primitives into standardized categories.
- **Technical Committee Reporting**: Provides monthly progress reports detailing term review rates, admitted concepts, and schema changes[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06**: Secured charter approvals, established standardized taxonomy data schemas, and launched web portal presentation pipelines[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **2026-07**: Processed 46 terms across four review syncs, admitting 13 terms in the workstream's first taxonomy pull request and reaching 67 reviewed terms out of the 128-term backlog[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].
- **2026-08**: Reviewed 53 terms across three terminology syncs (admitting 37) and prepared four pull requests ahead of a September 2026 Technical Committee approval vote[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-01f77049].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification standardizing session continuity, turn boundaries, provider calls, approvals, and external side effects across agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model (ABTM) is a vendor-neutral specification and telemetry schema developed by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to follow AI agent work across multi-turn interactions, operational pauses, and distributed system boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Rather than requiring bespoke runtime backends, the specification maps causal agent execution relationships into existing [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) semantic conventions and defines structured identity mappings across conversational continuity, runtime execution sessions, and overall agent trajectories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Architecture / Specification
The ABTM execution framework is organized around answering four core behavioral verification questions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:
- **Continuity:** Identifying which turns belong together across session pauses, restarts, and background resumptions without requiring telemetry consumers to query internal runtime state.
- **Calls and Retries:** Correlating the precise model invocations serving each execution turn without double-counting retried or failed calls.
- **Approvals:** Tracking governance checkpoints and human approval decisions directly to the corresponding proposed action payloads and verifying whether the action was executed.
- **Effects:** Associating external state mutations (such as ticket creation or API writes) observed by independent boundary services back to the executing agent turn.

The formal baseline is validated using a reference customer support scenario—investigating a delayed order, proposing a ticket, requesting human approval, executing the action against an independently instrumented test service, and returning to conversation—implemented concurrently in [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and a secondary agent runtime or SDK[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

### Turn Boundaries and Evidence Assumptions
ABTM evaluates candidate trace boundaries such as one distributed trace per turn while preserving caller trace context[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. Under ABTM evidentiary principles, unobserved spans designate unknown states rather than success or zero failures, recorded approval actions do not constitute cryptographic proof of enforcement, and content payload capture remains strictly opt-in[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, the Observability & Traceability Working Group finalized and merged the nine-task ABTM execution plan following working group review sessions in August 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48]. The roadmap establishes workstreams across baseline capture, shared test suites, multi-agent implementations, independent query verification, and upstream contributions to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, lower-layer profiling, and execution standards for agentic AI.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body convening practitioners, platform vendors, and standards organizations to build a shared understanding of agent observability and execution tracing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. The working group evaluates where existing telemetry mechanisms—including [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) and lower-level tracing frameworks—intersect with agentic reasoning, tool dispatch, and runtime boundaries, formulating specifications only where existing industry efforts exhibit unaddressed gaps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group coordinates standards, architecture blueprints, and integration test suites spanning multiple layers of agent infrastructure:
- **Trace and Behavior Modeling:** Authoring the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) (ABTM) to capture multi-turn continuity, model retries, approval gating, and external side effects across agent harnesses[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry:** Analyzing context propagation and observability across protocol barriers, such as [Model Context Protocol server boundaries](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md) and tool CLI interfaces[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- **Taxonomy Alignment:** Coordinating with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to harmonize tracing concepts, interaction turns, and session lifecycles[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Lifecycle History
The working group operates under leadership appointed by Platinum and Gold member organizations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]:
- **Chair:** Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]
- **Co-Chair:** Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]

The leadership term spans March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027, with public working group meetings convened biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM Pacific Time[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. In September 2026, the group formally adopted its execution plan for the Agent Behavior Trace Model to guide reference implementations and upstream OpenTelemetry proposals[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].
