proposed_concept.title: Workflows & Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing shared workflow execution models, state persistence patterns, human-in-the-loop gates, and enterprise process integration standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows & Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to define shared execution models, interaction primitives, and runtime architectures for complex agentic workflows[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. The group establishes reference patterns governing multi-activity coordination, state persistence, approval mechanisms, and enterprise integration boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group carries out its technical mandate across three primary workstreams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]:
- **Reference Architectures:** Scoping and evaluating formal workflow blueprints, such as [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md) and [Single-Agent Human Approval](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md).
- **Critical Use Cases:** Cataloging and voting on representative enterprise workflow scenarios to anchor pattern requirements.
- **Workflow Taxonomy:** Developing structured definitions for workflow primitives and execution concepts, coordinating directly with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to prevent fragmented or overlapping vocabulary definitions across AAIF working groups[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

# Lifecycle History
The working group is chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea]. In June 2026, the working group initiated active workstreams across reference architectures, taxonomy, and critical use cases, while submitting governance feedback to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) recommending stronger global taxonomy empowerment to unify vocabulary across working groups[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a17a580f85c2-46ce20ea].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill suite managing AAIF chapter workspace provisioning, Drive ACL reconciliation, and idempotent multi-step directory synchronization.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Skill Suite (`aaif-sync`) is an operational toolset and automation harness used by the Agentic AI Foundation to manage chapter records, attendee intake, Slack directory membership, and Google Workspace permissions[^evt-community-events-pr-52][^evt-community-events-pr-53]. It coordinates multi-source synchronization across external SaaS providers to maintain consistent, idempotent operational state for local community chapters and organizers[^evt-community-events-pr-52].

# Architecture / Specification
The suite executes as an 18-step sequential synchronization pipeline ensuring end-to-end reconciliation across chapter spreadsheets, organizer records, and messaging directories[^evt-community-events-pr-52][^evt-community-events-pr-53]:
- **Run-Level Memoization:** To prevent redundant network calls across pipeline steps, synchronization runs utilize transient append-only run memos (`AAIF_SLACK_RUN_MEMO` and `AAIF_GWS_RUN_MEMO`) locked for concurrent thread access and restricted to POSIX permissions `0600`[^evt-community-events-pr-52]. Read memoization is restricted exclusively to report runs to ensure `--write` runs always observe live state, and all memo files are purged immediately upon run termination[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Concurrent Drive Operations:** Chapter CRM synchronization (`sync_crm`) reads chapter workbooks concurrently through a thread pool of six workers with folder-scoped download paths to prevent collisions[^evt-community-events-pr-52].
- **Execution Keep-Awake Protection:** Under macOS environments, the runner automatically spawns a `caffeinate` supervisor process tied to the runner process ID (`caffeinate -i -w <runner pid>`), preventing OS sleep interruptions during long-running 18-step synchronization runs[^evt-community-events-pr-53].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026, performance optimizations and execution hardening were introduced across the suite[^evt-community-events-pr-52][^evt-community-events-pr-53]. Read memoization and CRM thread pooling reduced report execution runtimes from 50 minutes to approximately 11 minutes[^evt-community-events-pr-52], and process-bound sleep suppression was integrated into the runner to prevent session expiration across external SaaS connectors[^evt-community-events-pr-53].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Architectural framework structuring agent workflows across reusable patterns, job-oriented reference architectures, and scenario evaluations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Job-Oriented Architecture Model establishes a three-tier framework structuring agentic workflow knowledge into reusable patterns, practitioner job-oriented reference architectures, and empirical scenario validations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]. It provides an architectural foundation for composing granular workflow primitives into reviewable, verifiable operational designs.

# Architecture / Specification
The framework coordinates workflow system design across three structural levels [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]:
- **Reusable Patterns**: Modular building blocks addressing isolated workflow execution problems, such as [durable wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) and [human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
- **Job-Oriented Reference Architectures**: Composite frameworks uniting patterns, capability roles, boundary controls, guarantees, and exit states to execute recognizable practitioner jobs.
- **Real-World Scenarios**: Concrete operational use cases (such as invoice processing or autonomous remediation) used to test and validate reference architecture suitability.

Under active workstream consideration, the model evaluates expanding beyond human-readable guidance to produce a formal, machine-readable Workflow Design Specification (WDS) serialized in schema-valid YAML [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]. If adopted, this model treats the specification as an authoritative design artifact from which architecture diagrams, human review materials, and implementation handoffs are automatically derived [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28].

# References
- Reference Architectures Workstream Issue #28 [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-28]
- [Workflow Architecture Principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md)
- [Reference Architecture Template](../guidelines/reference-architecture-template.md)

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and trust models for agent identity, attestation, and delegated authority.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral specifications, reference architectures, and trust models for AI agent identity, cryptographic attestation, and delegated authority across organizational boundaries. The group addresses foundational mechanisms for establishing provenance, operational accountability, and verifiable authentication across autonomous agent workflows.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group investigates security, identity delegation, and compliance alignment across multi-agent environments [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]:
- **Attestation vs Regulatory Attribute Credentials**: Distinguishing low-level hardware attestation (such as RATS evidence) from legal electronic attestations under eIDAS 2 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Terminology and Legal Regime Alignment**: Resolving ambiguities where engineering terms conflict with statutory definitions, including 'operator' under the EU AI Act, 'relying party' under eIDAS, 'consent' across GDPR and PSD2, and contractual 'mandate' versus authorization objects [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].
- **Custody and Evidence Chains**: Mapping statutory roles (provider, deployer, controller, processor) across multi-hop agent delegation chains and tool calls to satisfy mandatory logging and evidence retention obligations [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10].

# References
- Identity & Trust Working Group Issue #10 [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-10]
- [Governance, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)
- [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md)

# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem catalog and structured data registry mapping agent runtimes, protocol standards, security frameworks, and global governance regimes. It provides an empirical overview of the technologies, open-source projects, and statutory baselines shaping autonomous AI deployment.

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape organizes entries across standardized ecosystem domains, maintaining strict data schemas and upstream authoritative citations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67]:
- **Global Governance and Enacted Legislation**: Catalogs statutory mandates governing autonomous and automated systems, incorporating Colorado SB 26-189 (the Automated Decision-Making Technology Act, repealing and reenacting SB 24-205) and the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation 2024/1689) linked to authoritative EUR-Lex registries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].
- **Standards and Risk Frameworks**: Groups voluntary guidance and risk governance models, including Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].
- **Runtime, Gateways, and Protocols**: Documents emerging agent communication protocols, execution sandboxes, and mediation proxies across industry implementations.

# References
- Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream Issue #67 [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67]
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group bridging global AI regulatory policies and agentic AI architectures through standardized risk themes and comparative gap analyses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG GRR) serves as a bridge between international AI regulatory frameworks and technical agentic architectures within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]. Co-chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group assesses jurisdictional compliance mandates, risk tiering models, and technical governance controls required for autonomous systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its comparative analysis and regulatory gap mapping across 16 baseline themes [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]:

1. **Governance & accountability**: System ownership, sign-offs, RACI mappings, and explicit risk acceptance.
2. **Use-case classification & risk tiering**: Permitted versus prohibited deployments and tiered control requirements.
3. **Architecture**: Reference patterns, trust boundary definition, and control placement.
4. **Agent identity & delegation**: Authentication, authorization, acting-on-behalf-of delegation semantics, and agent registries.
5. **Guardrails & policy constraints**: Declarative business rules, policy-as-code engines, and execution limits.
6. **Data protection & privacy**: PII handling, data minimization, retention schedules, and geographical residency.
7. **Security & access controls**: Least privilege, secrets isolation, process segmentation, and granular tool permissions.
8. **Model/agent risk management**: Model validation, robustness benchmarks, behavioral drift tracking, and change control procedures.
9. **Human oversight**: Human-in-the-loop (HITL), human-on-the-loop (HOTL), escalation pathways, override controls, and out-of-band kill switches (such as [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md)).
10. **Action management**: Pre-execution verification gates, dual control verification, and reversibility mechanisms.
11. **Monitoring & logging**: Tamper-evident audit trails, prompt/tool execution logs, and decision rationale records.
12. **Testing & red teaming**: Adversarial prompt injection defense, tool abuse mitigations, and autonomy boundary failures.
13. **Third-party & supply chain**: Vendor due diligence, model and tool provenance tracking, and dependency validation.
14. **Incident response**: Real-time detection, automated containment routines, and mandatory regulatory reporting.
15. **Transparency & user disclosure**: End-user notices, technical explainability mechanisms, and user expectation alignments.
16. **Recordkeeping & auditability**: Deterministic reproducibility and legally mandated retention horizons.

To conduct phase-two comparative gap analyses across diverse geographic policy instruments, the group developed a standardized "golden source" prompt to ensure consistent baseline extraction across regional regulations [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08 / 2026-09**: Finalized 16-theme evaluation baseline and standardized the golden-source AI prompt for cross-regional policy gap analyses [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Empirical catalog and multi-dimensional schema classifying production AI agent workflows across orchestration patterns, boundary enforcement, and human oversight tiers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification inventory provides an empirical catalog of production agent deployments evaluated across key operational dimensions, including trigger type, human-in-the-loop (HITL) pattern, agent topology, orchestration style, and boundary enforcement mechanisms [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]. It serves as a benchmarking reference for workflow architects mapping real-world tasks to formal foundation patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Architecture / Specification
The classification schema categorizes agent workflows across structured operational dimensions:
- **Trigger**: Invocations such as manual dispatch, event-driven webhooks, or scheduled cron routines.
- **HITL Pattern**: Oversight mechanisms ranging from blocking approval gates to asynchronous review or complete absence of runtime human intervention (`None`).
- **Agent Count**: Single-agent sufficient configurations versus multi-agent cooperative topologies.
- **Coordination**: Orchestrated pipelines versus emergent multi-agent swarms.
- **Workflow Pattern**: Sequential pipelines, iterative bounded loops, or fan-out dispatch.

### Upstream SDK Release Impact Analysis
Sourced from MCP Inspector's automated maintenance workflow (`sdk-watch.yml`), this software development lifecycle (SDLC) use case demonstrates analytical autonomy with structural boundary enforcement [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]:
- **Trigger**: `Scheduled` (nightly cron execution).
- **HITL Pattern**: `None`; the agent posts an informational comment to a GitHub issue, and adoption decisions sit outside the workflow.
- **Agent Count**: `Single-agent sufficient`.
- **Coordination**: `Single-agent, orchestrated` by surrounding deterministic scripts.
- **Workflow Pattern**: `Sequential pipeline` (sweep, fetch, analyze, scan, post).
- **Boundary Enforcement**: Realizes the [proposal-execution-split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) through job-level operating permissions rather than a runtime approval gate. The agent runs with a read-only token and restricted inspection tools (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`) without shell, network, or write access, isolating untrusted upstream release text. Analysis output is scanned for verbatim credentials before being uploaded to an isolated write-scoped job [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09**: Added upstream SDK release impact analysis case study documenting job-level permission isolation without runtime HITL requirements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification standardizing session continuity, turn boundaries, provider calls, tool delegations, and relationship verification in agent execution traces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open observability and telemetry specification defining how multi-turn agent sessions, subagent delegations, tool calls, and human approvals are captured, linked, and verified [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]. Extending standard distributed tracing paradigms, it ensures agent traces maintain verifiable causal relationships even under transport failure, out-of-order delivery, or message duplication [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model standardizes session structure, context propagation, and event causal graphs across runtime boundaries.

### Relationship Test Kit and Conformance Verification
As part of the trace model execution roadmap (Task 4), the specification establishes automated test suites and contribution templates to validate exported telemetry integrity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]:
- **Relationship Invariant Checks**: Telemetry verifiers test causal integrity across edges, ensuring traces remain logically sound when records are delayed, dropped, or reordered [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **Idempotency and Receipt Handling**: Verifies that duplicate delivery of execution receipts (e.g., ticket creation records) resolves to a single confirmed state, whereas missing receipts transition state to "unconfirmed" rather than asserting non-execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].
- **Test Harness Architecture**: Integrates with OpenTelemetry conformance tooling, providing language-neutral synthetic data fixtures, opt-in sensitive payload capture, and isolated deterministic and live integration suites [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-08 / 2026-09**: Established 9-task execution plan; specified Task 4 requirements for causal relationship testing kits and OTel-compatible conformance harnesses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42].

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model
proposed_concept.description: Multi-layer observability framework mapping telemetry propagation, governance gaps, and context preservation across agent, runtime, tool, and human approval boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Cross-Boundary Observability Model analyzes telemetry continuity, identity preservation, and security enforcement across agent operational interfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]. Maintained by the Observability and Traceability Working Group, the model categorizes observation capabilities and governance gaps across distinct interaction planes: Agent to Gateway/Runtime, Agent to Tool, and Agent to Human (HITL) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].

# Architecture / Specification
The framework maps interactions across layers, protocol boundaries, and enforcement points.

### Boundary Definitions
- **Agent → Gateway / Runtime**: Intercepts tool dispatches, mediation policies, and isolation parameters. In kernel-enforced runtimes (e.g., the SAF-M-74 reference class exemplified by the `nono` sandbox), enforcement occurs below L7 at the OS boundary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52]. Observed implementations reveal critical telemetry constraints, such as sandbox runtimes failing to propagate standard W3C trace context (`traceparent`, `tracestate`, `baggage`) across isolation barriers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].
- **Agent → Human (HITL)**: Captures human interaction records, decision rationale, approval metadata, and delegation authority, linking human actions to machine execution chains [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].
- **Agent → Tool**: Tracks invocation parameters, authorization context, and provenance values.

### Enforcement Classification
Working group proposals analyze whether `enforcement_layer` (categorized as `kernel`, `broker`, or `proxy`) should be structured as an explicit architectural boundary column or as an evaluated provenance attribute within audit schemas [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09**: Incorporated lower-layer runtime and HITL boundary rows into the Primitives and Protocol Observability focus group living documents, establishing benchmark fixtures from kernel-enforced execution environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-52].

proposed_concept.title: PostHog AI Agent Analytics Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Product analytics and telemetry reference architecture capturing pseudonymous agent behavioral funnels, feature adoption, and longitudinal usage tracking.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The PostHog reference architecture provides design patterns and architectural specifications for integrating product analytics into AI agent harnesses and developer tools [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55]. It establishes telemetry capture for agent user journeys, feature discovery, and session completion metrics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

# Architecture / Specification
The integration architecture standardizes client event dispatch, property capture, and funnel reporting.

### Identity and Privacy Classification
Telemetry implementations commonly generate persistent per-installation identifiers (`installation_id`, typically formatted as a random UUID) to measure cohort behavior and longitudinal usage without directly linking human identity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

However, architectural review within the Observability and Traceability Working Group emphasizes that data privacy classifications depend on jurisdictional definitions rather than implementer labels [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55]:
- **Pseudonymity vs. Anonymity**: Under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR, Recitals 26 and 30) and the UK GDPR, persistent identifiers used for longitudinal user tracking constitute pseudonymous personal data, rather than anonymous data [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].
- **Cross-Border Transfers**: Hardcoded telemetry endpoints directed to US ingest nodes (e.g., `us.i.posthog.com`) trigger international data transfer compliance duties when transmitting pseudonymous personal data originating from EU/UK jurisdictions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].
- **Template Schema Recommendations**: The working group proposes keying reference architecture privacy attributes (`personal data`, `personal information`, `PII`, `none`) directly to governing regulatory regimes rather than asserting absolute "privacy by design" claims [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-09**: Regulatory review identified that persistent installation UUIDs constitute pseudonymous personal data under GDPR/UK GDPR, initiating revisions to architectural classification standards [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-55].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, runtime security design patterns, static-analysis best practice guides, and cross-working group security checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with developing architectural threat models, runtime security patterns, and practitioner best practices for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]. Co-chaired by Alex Frazer and Junjie Bu, the group coordinates security initiatives, static analysis rules, and cross-working group governance reviews [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical agenda across several core workstreams and deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]:
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: An operational guide detailing code smells, secret handling, sandboxing, and runtime guardrails, spearheaded by Fernando Lucktemberg and Erin Farr [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
- **Threat Modeling Framework**: Gap analysis and threat modeling methodologies benchmarking agent architectures against standard threat models, led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architecture patterns addressing security-sensitive agent operations, including isolated runtimes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, this initiative establishes security verification checklists across intersecting AAIF working groups including [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md), and [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **External Liaisons and Standard Alignment**: Engaging with external bodies such as ETSI TC SAI (cybersecurity requirements for AI systems and agents) and OWASP [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Lifecycle History
The working group established recurring biweekly meetings, expanded its meeting times to accommodate APAC participants, and adopted formal pull request review windows in `CONTRIBUTING.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076]. In August and September 2026, the group addressed protocol consolidation around A2A and [Agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md), reviewed sandbox security isolations such as Eclipse Enclave microVMs, and initiated cross-WG review procedures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, prior work landscapes, and agent observability use case catalogs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group tasked with surveying, coordinating, and standardizing observability across agent architectures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra, the group produces canonical landscape surveys, multi-layer observability models, and use case frameworks guiding agent telemetry instrumentation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

# Architecture / Specification
The group's technical foundation rests upon several foundational working documents and models:
- **Agent Observability Landscape Survey (`PRIOR-WORK.md`)**: A continuous evaluation benchmarking external and open specifications, including OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions, OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS), OCSF 1.9, Monocle, AGNTCY Observe SDK, and Cursor Agent Trace [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Use Cases for Agent Observability (`USE-CASES.md`)**: A structured catalog categorizing observability needs across nine operational domains: Debugging and Root Cause Analysis, Cost Management, Code Attribution, Evaluation and Quality Assurance, Safety and Compliance, Multi-Agent Systems, Operational Monitoring, Research, and Identity Resolution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3] [^evt-wg-observability-pr-53].
- **Cross-Cutting Telemetry Principles**: Telemetry standards mandating clear provenance attribution between self-reported and boundary-attested events, privacy classification, sampling declarations, causal correlation, and explicit schema versioning [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **Cross-Boundary Framework**: Telemetry models addressing context propagation across agent, harness, tool, and host boundaries in coordination with other working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

# Lifecycle History
Initial landscape and use case inventories were established in March 2026 and refreshed through August 2026 to incorporate dedicated OpenTelemetry GenAI repository developments, OCSF 1.9 agent identity profiles, and emerging tamper-evident audit requirements [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853] [^evt-wg-observability-pr-53].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Comprehensive AAIF catalog and taxonomy defining nine functional categories and cross-cutting requirements for agentic observability and tracing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog (`USE-CASES.md`) is a living specification published by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) establishing structured operational requirements for observing AI agent behaviors, state transitions, tool invocations, and multi-agent interactions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]. It catalogs cross-cutting telemetry criteria and standardizes operational use cases across nine distinct functional categories [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3] [^evt-wg-observability-pr-53].

# Architecture / Specification
## Cross-Cutting Telemetry Requirements
The catalog defines five fundamental requirements governing all agent telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]:
1. **Source and Trust**: Telemetry must identify its producer and observation point, distinguishing between an agent's [self-reported](../taxonomy/self-reported.md) data and boundary-observed evidence from frameworks, gateways, sandboxes, or host operating systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
2. **Privacy and Governance**: Event correlation and data payload fields must carry policy metadata supporting redaction, data minimization, consent tracking, and regulatory retention without logging raw credentials [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
3. **Completeness and Sampling**: Telemetry streams must distinguish audit-required records from sampleable debugging data and declare dropped-event counts [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
4. **Schema Evolution**: Telemetry artifacts must specify schema versions, semantic convention revisions, and agent configuration versions to ensure long-term interpretability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
5. **Correlation and Causality**: Traces must maintain stable causal identifiers across sessions, delegated tasks, and queued asynchronous operations beyond simple wall-clock ordering or single-parent span trees [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

## Use Case Categories
The document details nine operational domains [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3] [^evt-wg-observability-pr-53]:
- **A. Debugging and Root Cause Analysis**: Diagnosing why an agent took a wrong path (A1), detecting retry bottlenecks and loops (A2), and deterministic session reproduction (A3).
- **B. Cost Management and Optimization**: Turn-level and session-level spend tracking (B1), outcome-adjusted cost analysis (B2), and token waste mitigation (B3).
- **C. Code Attribution and Provenance**: Tracking AI-authored code attribution (C1) and conducting security reviews on generated code (C2).
- **D. Evaluation and Quality Assurance**: Benchmarking task performance (D1), regression testing (D2), and cross-model comparative scoring (D3).
- **E. Safety and Compliance**: Monitoring real-world tool execution (E1), detecting scope/privilege violations (E2), maintaining regulatory audit trails (E3), and generating tamper-evident evidence for dispute resolution (E4).
- **F. Multi-Agent Systems**: Tracing causal flows across agent boundaries (F1) and logging inter-agent communication (F2).
- **G. Operational Monitoring**: Real-time agent health indicators (G1) and fleet capacity planning (G2).
- **H. Research and Improvement**: Discovering novel behavioral failure modes (H1), fine-tuning dataset generation (H2), and benchmarking implementations (H3).
- **I. Identity and Ownership**: Resolving cross-surface agent identity and authorization mapping (I1).

# Lifecycle History
The use cases document was drafted in March 2026 by the Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3]. In August 2026, additional use cases covering tamper-evident audit records (E4) and cross-surface identity resolution (I1) were formally incorporated [^evt-wg-observability-pr-53].

mutations.rationale: Document the prior work and industry landscape survey maintained by the Observability and Traceability Working Group.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Prior Work Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Comparative landscape survey and evaluation of external standards, specifications, and platforms across agent observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Prior Work Landscape (`PRIOR-WORK.md`) is a comprehensive survey maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) assessing existing industry specifications, instrumentation frameworks, and telemetry platforms for agentic systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. First compiled in March 2026 and refreshed through August 2026, the survey analyzes gaps, specification maturity, and opportunities for alignment across open and proprietary observability initiatives [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape benchmarks efforts across several functional sectors [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]:
- **OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions**: Dedicated repository (`open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai`) defining spans, events, and metrics for LLM calls, agent creation/invocation, workflow execution, tool runs, and planning [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Security and Compliance Frameworks**: OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS) separating instrument, trace, and inspect tiers with AgBOM integrations, and the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) Schema 1.9 incorporating AI Operation, AI Agent identity, and delegation records [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Multi-Agent and Protocol Tracing**: AGNTCY Observe SDK for cross-agent context propagation, [Agent-to-Agent (A2A)](../taxonomy/agent-to-agent.md) protocol tracing extensions, and [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) eBPF runtime instrumentation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Application and Evaluation Frameworks**: OpenInference, MLflow Tracing, [Langfuse](../resources/langfuse.md), LF AI & Data Monocle auto-instrumentation, and Cursor [Agent Trace](../standards/agent-trace.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

# Lifecycle History
Originally drafted on 2026-03-15, the survey underwent a major refresh between June and August 2026 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853]. Key updates included tracking OpenTelemetry's migration of GenAI specifications into a dedicated repository, the release of OCSF 1.9 agent profiles, AGNTCY Observe SDK v1.0.43, and the shifting focus of academic research toward observability as an active security monitoring substrate [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].

mutations.rationale: Incorporate the August 2026 execution roadmap, portable telemetry context specifications, causal linkage constraints, and independent reader interoperability testing criteria.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification standardizing session continuity, portable context propagation, causal decision-to-execution linkage, and multi-agent trace verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) that standardizes execution session continuity, turn boundaries, and causal relationships across agents, SDKs, gateways, and observability backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Rather than acting as a replacement for OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, the specification defines portable telemetry context to correlate plans, decisions, and outcomes without requiring raw chain-of-thought capture [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Portable Telemetry Context & Scope

The model relies on portable telemetry context to preserve execution context across heterogeneous agent harnesses, gateways like [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md), and telemetry collectors [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. The standard covers canonical agent identifiers, long-running multi-turn execution tasks, cross-agent context reuse, user privacy boundaries, and verifiable evidence generation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

## Causal Linkage Without Chain-of-Thought

A core design constraint of the specification is binding high-level planning and decision records to observed tool executions and concrete outcomes while avoiding exposure or retention of internal model chain-of-thought [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. This separation enables auditability, tamper-evident verification, and dispute resolution across untrusted enterprise boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

## Independent Interpretation Conformance

To prove interoperability beyond a single producer's proprietary tooling, the specification requires independent interpretation verification under Task 7 of its execution plan [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. Two or more decoupled reader implementations or query paths must interpret identical telemetry exports [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]:

- Readers may not rely on private runtime state, hidden fixture mappings, or shared reconstruction code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- Implementations must correctly categorize approved plans, observed tool calls, and independently reported effects regardless of event arrival order [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- In the absence of corroborating receipts or boundary observations, readers must mark effects as unconfirmed, demonstrating resilience against incomplete or conflicting records [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

## Trust Pipeline Integration

The trace model integrates with [Agent Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD) to observe discovery lifecycles, enterprise identity verification, and admission decisions through standardized span attributes prior to skill execution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group established an initial scope and nine-task execution plan for the trace model led by Matthew Lee, initiating work on reference libraries, synthetic examples, and conformance tests [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. Workflows developed by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) were identified as candidate evaluation workloads for cross-system correlation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, context propagation models, and agent behavior trace standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (WG O&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. The working group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry models, cross-boundary distributed tracing specifications, and portable context propagation mechanisms for single- and multi-agent AI architectures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Workstreams

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model:** Standardizes execution telemetry, turn boundaries, and causal links between plans, decisions, and side effects across multi-agent systems via portable telemetry context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. The workstream enforces conformance through multi-reader independent interpretation checks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability:** Defines metadata mappings and context propagation rules across agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and agent-to-MCP boundaries, addressing observability gaps at local CLI boundaries and [Model Context Protocol](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md) interfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **ARD Trust-Pipeline Observability:** Develops tracing proofs-of-concept for the [Agent Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) lifecycle through [Agent Gateway](../resources/agentgateway.md), exposing discovery, identity verification, and policy decisions via dedicated span attributes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Taxonomy Contributions:** Coordinates with the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) on core definitions including Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Memory Access, Context Assembly, Retrieval, and Traceability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

## Focus Group Structure

- *LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability* (led by Zayne Turner): Focuses on ARD trust verification tracing, MCP server instrumentation, and protocol boundary mappings [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- *Agentic State, Context & Reasoning* (led by Govindaraj): Focuses on memory access patterns, context lifecycle tracking, and reasoning telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- *Multi-Agentic Observability - Orchestration & Coordination*: Led by Ty Smith during early prototyping of context intelligence graph runtimes; consolidated into the general WG in August 2026 to unify broad multi-agent participation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group merged its Working Methods and contributor checklist, finalized landscape surveys covering full-stack tracing, and approved the initial scope and nine-task execution roadmap for the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body responsible for formulating threat modeling frameworks, security design patterns, best practice guides, and cross-cutting security review procedures across agentic architectures.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f] Co-chaired by Alexander Frazer and Junjie Bu, the group coordinates runtime security controls and risk assessments with related AAIF efforts.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical deliverables across several primary workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Benchmarking OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI RMF against agentic AI requirements, evaluating STRIDE and PASTA methodologies, and incorporating Model Context Protocol (MCP) and UI/Human-to-Agent interaction factors.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Security Best Practices**: Developing baseline configuration and implementation guidelines covering secrets management, execution isolation, and authorization boundaries in collaboration with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Documenting reference patterns for runtime isolation, policy enforcement, and defense-in-depth mitigations for autonomous workflows.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Formulating an inter-group checklist and scope alignment matrix to surface security and privacy gaps across AAIF workstreams.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Coordinating agent-specific security terminology in collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group instituted a policy making meeting recordings public by default.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22] During the same period, the group flagged jurisdictional and operational risks concerning overlapping working group boundaries—notably regarding protocol-level security following the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol donation—and requested scoping guidance from the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22]

mutations.rationale: Update with August 2026 report activities, liaison tracking across external and internal bodies, and trace model planning milestones.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing unified telemetry specifications, execution trace models, and cross-boundary context propagation mechanisms for AI agents.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38] The group coordinates vendor-neutral observability requirements across external standards organizations and internal AAIF initiatives.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18]

# Architecture / Specification
The group's technical initiatives and governance artifacts include:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A core telemetry and execution trace model developed under a structured recommendation plan comparing existing industry specifications against an adopt, extend, or new-artifact path.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]
- **Cross-Boundary Telemetry & Use Cases**: Reference boundary analyses and functional catalog definitions addressing runtime telemetry between agents, tool CLIs, and protocol servers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]
- **Liaison Management**: A structured liaison tracker managing technical interchange with external groups—including OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, W3C Trace Context, Agent Trace, Monocle, and AGNTCY—and internal AAIF working groups.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18]

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group delivered its monthly progress report to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), outlining the trace model scope, September implementation plan, and terminology submissions developed with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification standardizing session continuity, portable context propagation, and causal behavioral tracing across agent execution lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification authored by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to capture causal relationships, agent step lifecycles, and cross-boundary session context across disparate AI runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38] It provides a vendor-neutral schema for recording agent inputs, tool interactions, and decision lineage.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]

# Architecture / Specification
Development of the specification follows a decision-neutral recommendation plan designed to establish consensus before formalizing wire schemas:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]

- **Comparative Evaluation**: Synthesizing existing distributed tracing standards and domain models (including OpenTelemetry GenAI semantics and prior art) against agentic behavioral requirements.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]
- **Input Synthesis**: Incorporating empirical use cases, threat models, taxonomy primitives, and boundary gap analyses across tools and protocol gateways.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]
- **Standardization Path**: Evaluating candidate specifications under an adopt, extend, or new-artifact decision framework prior to publication.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]

# Lifecycle History
The trace model recommendation framework was structured under working group issue #12 in mid-2026, establishing criteria and review gates ahead of an implementation roadmap presented to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in August 2026.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]

mutations.rationale: Clarify evidence-grade ladder terminology and incorporate normative requirements distinguishing technical integrity mechanisms from legal weight.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Comprehensive AAIF catalog and taxonomy defining functional observability requirements, evidence-grade distinctions, and cross-cutting regulatory constraints for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Observability Use Cases Catalog is an empirical reference compiled by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to define operational categories, failure modes, and forensic telemetry requirements for production agent deployments.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38] It establishes baseline expectations for evidence durability, debugging, and auditability.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]

# Architecture / Specification
The catalog categorizes telemetry scenarios across distinct operational tiers and normative cross-cutting requirements:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]

- **Evidence-Grade Ladder**: A stepped grading framework categorizing artifact tamper-resistance and verification strength; the ladder explicitly differentiates evidence quality grades from specific use case identifiers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]
- **Jurisdiction and Legal Weight**: A cross-cutting telemetry requirement specifying that a record's technical integrity mechanism (such as RFC 3161 timestamps) remains structurally distinct from its legal effect, which is determined by the legal regime and role of the relying party.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]
- **Cross-Boundary Correlation**: Tracing context preservation requirements spanning agent runtimes, tool invocation boundaries, and external APIs.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38]

# Lifecycle History
In late 2026, the catalog underwent revisions to qualify evidence-grade terminology against collision with section use-case identifiers and to mandate explicit jurisdiction recording where compliance obligations are keyed to statutory laws.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56]

mutations.rationale: Update the working group specification with July 2026 status, leadership, workstream structure, execution profiles, and use case cataloging progress.

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow execution models, state persistence patterns, human intervention boundaries, and reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG Workflows & Process Integration) develops standard execution models, state persistence patterns, human intervention boundaries, and reference architectures for agentic workflows across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. Co-chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato), the working group coordinates cross-vendor alignment on orchestrating AI agents across deterministic and autonomous business processes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical deliverables into three collaborative workstreams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]:

- **Reference Architectures**: Led by Mario and Zayne, this stream defines seven execution profiles ranging from Profile 1 (fully deterministic) to Profile 7 (fully agentic), applying a proposed "least agentic default" principle[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. It formulates six charter-derived archetypes (including bounded automation and gated operation) and maintains a specification-driven design flow that transforms structured YAML use-case definitions into documentation and diagrams[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Led by Kevin Ng (Telus) and Jodee Varney (Cisco), with contributions from Rocky Zhang (SAP), this stream categorized 89 production use cases against execution primitives including triggers, human-in-the-loop patterns, agent count, coordination models, and workflow patterns[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The workflows align against a consolidated catalog of under 10 reusable patterns, including the [bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Taxonomy**: Led by Gala, this stream aligns workflow terminology with the Foundation-wide glossary in collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), preventing cross-working-group vocabulary divergence and reconciling execution profile parameters against common terms[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Lifecycle History

In July 2026, the working group submitted its monthly status report to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-24][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The group reported bi-weekly plenary meetings averaging 25 members alongside active workstream syncs. Target publication schedules for taxonomy and reference architecture deliverables shifted to August 2026 to permit thorough cross-validation of execution profiles, archetypes, and primitives prior to formal TC votes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

mutations.rationale: Document working group reporting automation and monthly metrics workflow implemented for Technical Committee accountability.

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, and context-propagation standards for agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) establishes vendor-neutral telemetry schemas, cross-boundary tracing protocols, and context propagation standards for AI agent runtimes across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59]. The group defines data models and trace collection methodologies across agent-to-tool, agent-to-model, and agent-to-agent boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group produces open specifications including the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md) and [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md), providing reference implementations for distributed trace collection, boundary mediation, and causal sequence reconstruction across heterogenous execution fabrics.

# Lifecycle History

The working group delivers periodic progress reports and operational KPIs to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59]. In response to Technical Committee reporting requirements, the working group automated its monthly issue and pull request metrics gathering via a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow using `issue-metrics`, generating monthly activity, response latency, and close-rate reports labeled `monthly-report` for TC oversight[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9373ed8bd5e2-54fdeb4c][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-59].

mutations.rationale: Update working group details with appointed leadership, operational meeting schedules, workstream structures, and repository governance policies.

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, runtime security design patterns, and cross-cutting privacy protections for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes security and privacy as shared engineering disciplines across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. It produces open threat models, domain-specific security taxonomies, and architectural design patterns that agent providers, consumers, and peer working groups adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

The working group operates under the Technical Committee and collaborates with peer workstreams including [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), and [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Architecture / Specification

### Governance and Leadership

The working group is co-chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), serving a term from March 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027 following appointment by Platinum and Gold members [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. Primary working group meetings take place biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT, complemented by trial alternate-week APAC meetings scheduled at 10:00 PM ET to bridge Asia-Pacific time zones [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

### Core Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group divides its mandate into dedicated workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157]:
- **[Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md)**: Comprehensive guidelines and feature requirements covering secrets management, protocol defense, and isolated execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **[Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md)**: Benchmarking existing security frameworks against unique multi-agent and tool-invocation vectors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Structural specifications defining runtime security solutions such as [Kill Switches](../patterns/kill-switch.md) and [Attested Isolated Runtimes](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Security and privacy evaluation criteria harmonized across peer AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

### Contribution and Merge Governance

Deliverables adhere to formal review controls: pull requests targeting the `deliverables/` directory cannot be self-merged by authors and require independent maintainer review, while individual workstream directories allow leads greater autonomy during draft iterations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

- **2026-09-29**: Established merge constraints for deliverables, initiated APAC meeting trials, and approved initial merge of the Security Best Practices guide [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security guidelines covering secrets management, MCP protocol security, skill supply-chain verification, sandboxing, and runtime guardrails.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide defines foundational operational controls, feature requirements, and architectural defenses for deploying autonomous AI agents in production environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]. Authored under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the deliverable outlines technical mechanisms and process validations designed to prevent privilege escalation, data poisoning, and unauthorized tool invocation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Architecture / Specification

### 1. Secrets Management
Agents must not execute with static, long-lived credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:
- Workload identities (e.g., AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) provide short-lived credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- Dynamic secrets engines issue per-request, narrowly scoped credentials with automated TTL cleanup [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- Network proxies and sidecars inject secrets for legacy systems outside agent context [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- Enclave-attested key release (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) protects high-sensitivity environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

### 2. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Security
Tool connections via MCP require boundary validation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:
- **Evaluation**: Static and runtime scanning (e.g., Cisco MCP Scanner, Invariant `mcp-scan`) and repository health checks (≥90-day activity) before server registration [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Transport**: Authenticated, encrypted transport using OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, TLS enforcement, and RFC 8707 token audience binding for HTTP connections [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Stdio Isolation**: Stdio MCP transports are classified as untrusted binaries requiring mandatory sandbox isolation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Gateway Mediation**: In multi-server architectures, traffic routes through an intermediary policy gateway, such as [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md), enforcing per-tool authorization and full payload audit captures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Runtime Invariants**: Comparing tool description hashes at every session start to block rug-pull mutations and unauthorized schema alteration [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

### 3. Supply Chain and Skill Verification
Third-party skills follow multi-tier verification before contextual inclusion [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:
- **Tier 1 (Automated)**: Static pattern matching and behavioral dataflow scanning blocking on high/critical vulnerabilities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Tier 2 (Elevated Permission Review)**: Manual inspection of requested permissions against stated purpose, flagging `eval()` invocations, undeclared domain endpoints, and base64-encoded strings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-18**: Initial best practices draft PR opened in the Security and Privacy Working Group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-09-29**: First edition finalized and merged via PR #9 under workstream leads Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, establishing the guide as a living document [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design is an ongoing workstream deliverable produced by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]. Its purpose is to evaluate existing artificial intelligence threat modeling frameworks—such as CSA MAESTRO, the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs/Generative AI, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)—to determine whether they sufficiently address agentic-specific threat surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].

# Architecture / Specification

### Scope and Target Threat Vectors

The analysis identifies and measures vulnerability coverage across several agentic threat classes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]:
- **Multi-Agent Persuasion and Collusion**: Subversion of subagent reasoning via adversarial prompts transmitted during agent-to-agent collaboration [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].
- **Tool Invocation Risks**: Dynamic generation of unvalidated external tool calls and unauthorized parameter injections [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].
- **Delegated Authorization Boundaries**: Privilege escalation across multi-hop credential forwarding and ambient authority propagation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].
- **Supply-Chain Integrity**: Tampering with system prompts, model provenance degradation, and lack of tools manifest signature verification [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].

### Downstream Integration

The conclusions of the gap analysis directly inform downstream specifications within the foundation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]:
1. Input for the working group's Design Patterns Catalog, including patterns like [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) and [Proposal Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].
2. Requirements and feature matrix validation for the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-23**: Initial threat modeling and best practices survey presented to the working group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-08-04**: Draft deliverable skeleton submitted for working group review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
- **2026-09-29**: Dedicated weekly threat modeling sessions established under workstream leads Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Operational security engineering guidelines addressing ephemeral secrets management, MCP protocol transport hardening, tool supply chain verification, and incident forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is an operational engineering deliverable produced by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to provide implementable controls for builders deploying agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Authored under the leadership of Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson), the guide bridges high-level threat models with practical architecture, focusing on secrets elimination, Model Context Protocol (MCP) transport and content security, tool supply chains, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

The guide explicitly scopes out baseline agent identity and delegated authorization architecture—such as SPIFFE/SVID workload attestation, RFC 8693 delegation-chain mechanics, and UCAN capability tokens—which are deferred to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and evaluated via a cross-working-group checklist[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Architecture / Specification

## Secrets Management
Static, long-lived credentials stored in environment variables, image layers, or configuration files represent persistent failure modes in agentic environments, vulnerable to prompt injection, serialization leaks, and CVE-2025-68664 ("LangGrinch") deserialization attacks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. The guide mandates shifting from credentials as stored assets to ephemeral attestations through a prioritized pattern hierarchy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:
1. **Workload Identity:** Native platform attestation (e.g., AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) exchanging cluster OIDC claims for short-lived cloud credentials automatically without storing secrets in agent runtime memory.
2. **Dynamic Secrets:** On-demand secret leasing (e.g., HashiCorp Vault) issuing narrowly scoped credentials with automatic cleanup upon short expiration windows (15 to 60 minutes).
3. **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecar proxy mediation attaching credentials out-of-band for legacy systems where agents cannot natively integrate workload identity.
4. **Confidential Computing:** Hardware-isolated enclaves (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) protecting memory states and cryptographic keys for regulated multi-tenant deployments or hostile infrastructure threat models.
5. **OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693):** Narrowing authorization scopes at each delegation hop to enforce blast radius containment.

## Secure Tool Invocation and MCP Hardening
Addressing security gaps in the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—notably optional OAuth 2.1 requirements and the lack of authentication on local stdio transports—the guide establishes strict pre-deployment and transport controls[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:
- **Verification Gates:** Mandatory static scanning of MCP servers (such as Cisco MCP Scanner) and public vulnerability database auditing prior to production connection.
- **Transport Security:** Treating third-party stdio servers as untrusted local binary execution; mandating OAuth 2.1 across all remote HTTP transports.
- **Remote Authorization Models:** Differentiating between user-direct authorization (PKCE code grant with RFC 8707 resource indicators), agent authorization under a shared IdP (RFC 8707 audience-bound Bearer tokens), and autonomous machine-to-machine execution using the OAuth 2.1 `client_credentials` grant[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Threat Mitigations:** Explicit controls targeting tool poisoning (such as hidden Unicode tag characters in descriptions), rug pulls (unannounced tool definition mutations), cross-server shadowing, and conversation hijacking[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Lifecycle History
The guide represents Deliverable 4 of the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) deliverable roadmap[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. Merged into the working group repository as Draft v0.1, it operates as a living document subject to mandatory review by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam per working group decisions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design
proposed_concept.description: Comparative threat modeling report evaluating OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, and CSA MAESTRO frameworks across eight agentic risk areas to establish foundational security baselines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design report is an authoritative technical analysis produced by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to determine whether existing security frameworks adequately address agentic AI threats[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. Led by Fernando Lucktemberg with co-lead Alon Mazor, the deliverable evaluates established frameworks against agent-specific behaviors to establish where existing taxonomies suffice and where new foundation-led engineering work is required[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

The report concludes that existing industry frameworks provide adequate classification and technique taxonomies for standard vulnerabilities, recommending that the Foundation adopt them as a baseline rather than inventing a competing taxonomy, while targeting new WG efforts exclusively at verified architectural gaps[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification

## Tri-Framework Evaluation Methodology
The analysis evaluates security frameworks in combination across three complementary operational perspectives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:
1. **Developer Controls (OWASP):** Combines the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications with the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI01–ASI10) to define application-level vulnerability requirements.
2. **SOC and Detection (MITRE ATLAS):** Leverages the adversarial technique taxonomy (`AML.T####` codes, baseline v4.6.0 through v5.4.0) to model multi-stage adversary tactics, red-team techniques, and SIEM detection rules.
3. **Architectural Hardening (CSA MAESTRO):** Uses the seven-layer reference stack (L1 Foundation Models through L7 Agent Ecosystem, intersected by vertical L6 Security and Compliance) to identify layer-specific hardening targets.
4. **Governance Scaffolding:** Evaluates NIST AI RMF 1.0, NIST IR 8596, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, and the CSA AI Controls Matrix v1.0 (243 controls across 18 domains) to provide compliance and governance frameworks.

## Evaluated Threat Domains
The deliverable expands the working group's initial mandate from four to eight distinct agentic risk domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:
- **Memory and context poisoning:** Tampering with persistent agent memory stores or conversational context windows.
- **Multi-agent persuasion:** Adversarial subversion, manipulation, or consensus corruption across autonomous agent networks.
- **Agent sabotage, derailment, and rogue agents:** Behavioral deviation, infinite execution cycles, and unconstrained action execution.
- **Tool invocation risk:** Exploitation of protocol boundaries, command injection, and untrusted execution via tool calling.
- **Excessive agency and blast radius containment:** Inadequate boundary enforcement resulting in disproportionate privilege and unconfined damage.
- **Delegated authorization boundaries:** Vulnerabilities in cross-boundary credential exchange, deferred to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).
- **Supply chain integrity:** Compromised models, malicious agent skills, and unverified tool package registries.
- **Commerce and payment-agent risk:** Financial transaction manipulation and autonomous authorization risks, interfacing with the [Agentic Commerce Working Group](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md).

# Lifecycle History
The report forms Deliverable 2 of the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) five-part roadmap[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]. Its findings serve as a mandatory precondition and baseline for Deliverable 3 (Design Patterns Catalog) and Deliverable 4 ([Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md))[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
