proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for establishing threat modeling methodologies, architectural defense patterns, operational security guidelines, and privacy-preserving frameworks for autonomous AI agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

The working group operates across five structured deliverables, coordinating closely with related Foundation initiatives including the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification

## Deliverables Roadmap
The working group organizes its formal output into a sequential series of five core deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:
1. **D1: Taxonomy of Terms:** Standardized vocabulary and shared definitions for agentic-specific threats, failure modes, and vulnerabilities.
2. **D2: Threat Modeling Gap Analysis:** Systematic evaluation of external frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) determining coverage sufficiency across eight agentic risk areas; co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
3. **D3: Design Patterns Catalog:** Architectural security specifications providing concrete implementation patterns for newly identified threat gaps.
4. **D4: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Practical operational guidance for engineering teams covering secrets management, MCP transport hardening, tool supply chain checks, guardrails, and forensics; led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].
5. **D5: Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Formal handoff and review criteria routing out-of-scope concerns (such as SPIFFE/SVID workload identities, RFC 8693 delegation, and payment boundaries) to counterpart working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Lifecycle History
The working group maintains its deliverables as living documents inside its GitHub repository, accepting community contributions through regular pull requests and issues under the technical oversight of designated workstream leads[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open telemetry specification standardizing session continuity, portable context propagation, and causal behavioral tracing across agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to define standardized trace schemas, causal propagation semantics, and session continuity conventions for autonomous AI agents[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

The model addresses pervasive inconsistencies in OpenTelemetry adoption and GenAI semantic conventions across agent frameworks by grounding specification milestones in direct behavioral evidence captured from production agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Architecture / Specification

## Execution Phases
The specification rollout follows an evidence-first, four-phase plan designed to replace uncoordinated parallel task tracks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]:
1. **Agree:** Aligning working group consensus on core dimension coverage, deferrals, and milestone boundaries.
2. **Evidence:** Capturing and cataloging actual runtime emissions from production agent implementations into a central gap register.
3. **Interpret:** Evaluating divergence between observed telemetry streams and existing OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions.
4. **Contribute:** Submitting concrete semantic proposals to upstream OpenTelemetry working groups backed by empirical capture data.

## Reference Implementations
The initial reference implementation anchors on Goose, an open-source agent runtime hosted within the AAIF ecosystem with pre-existing OpenTelemetry integration, to provide the baseline capture dataset for milestone 1 evaluations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Lifecycle History
Originally structured around nine parallel execution tasks, the plan was restructured under PR #60 into a phased evidence-driven delivery roadmap aiming for draft publication in late 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability and Execution Boundaries
proposed_concept.description: Architectural specification for cross-client portable agent plugins, abstract capability declarations, token resolution, and human mutation gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability specification governs cross-client compatibility and boundary enforcement across agent environments including Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. It mandates a root `plugin.json` as the canonical manifest for shared identity and versioning metadata under the Agent Plugins specification, while accommodating client-specific structures such as `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and marketplace catalogs without requiring diverging functional overlays[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

# Architecture / Specification
Portable agent plugins decouple skill specifications from platform-specific invocation syntax and tool bindings[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. All internal references in a skill bundle resolve relative to the `<skill-root>` directory housing the corresponding `SKILL.md` file, which is resolved dynamically by the agent runtime rather than passed as a shell environment variable or literal string[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

Agent instructions declare functional capabilities instead of proprietary runtime tool names[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- **Read bundled files**: Load workflows, references, and static assets, aborting execution if assets are missing.
- **Run Python and subprocesses**: Execute deterministic helper scripts and workspace utilities rather than ad-hoc shell reimplementations.
- **Read web pages**: Access public endpoints and operational dashboards.
- **Show local files**: Expose rendered HTML, slide decks, or diffs for user inspection.
- **Request user approval**: Enforce transitions across write, notify, or publish boundaries.

Frontmatter conforms strictly to portable [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) schemas; client-specific autocomplete cues (such as `argument-hint`) are preserved only as namespaced metadata to avoid duplicating skills[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Automated pre-commit hooks enforce manifest schema validity, relative path syntax, and the total omission of client-specific tool directives[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].

# Authorization and Mutation Controls
Skill loading or invocation never confers implicit authorization to mutate downstream environments[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Operating workflows enforce strict boundary controls aligning with [Human Approval Gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md):
- Operations are read-only and plan-generating by default.
- Mutating flags (`--write`, `--apply`, `--create`) are executed only after explicit human approval of generated proposals[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- Attestation tokens such as `--i-have-approval` record authenticated human consent and must never be passed autonomously by agents[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].
- Secrets, OAuth tokens, and API credentials must be sourced from environment variables, secure keychains, or `.env` files; they must never traverse command-line arguments (`argv`), tracked repositories, or workflow logs[^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill suite managing chapter slide deck synthesis, Gall Stereographic map projection calibration, Drive estate backfills, and Slack workspace audits.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite automates chapter lifecycle management, asset generation, and governance reconciliation across AAIF regional chapters[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49][^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]. It executes deterministic slide deck rebranding, geodetic map marker positioning, batch estate backfills, and cross-system membership and access audits between Google Drive, Google Sheets, and Slack[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49][^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

# Operational Mechanics
Chapter provisioning and asset synthesis are handled through specialized deterministic Python engines:
- **Chapter Rebrand Engine (`create_chapter.py`)**: Executes paragraph-level text transformation across OOXML PresentationML structures, concatenating text runs before transformation to withstand run-splitting artifacts[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].
- **Map Marker Projection**: Positions chapter markers on slide templates using a Gall Stereographic cylindrical projection (`lon2x` linear in longitude; `lat2y` linear in `(1 + √2/2)·tan(lat/2)`), fitted against Natural Earth 110m coastline models using Nelder-Mead distance-transform optimization[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]. Local runs enforce explicit latitude/longitude arguments to guarantee offline determinism[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49].
- **Estate Backfills (`backfill_map_dots.py`, `backfill_host_footer.py`, `backfill_projects.py`)**: Performs mass updates across Drive chapter estates following projection or footer updates[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]. Backfills execute in plan mode by default, evaluating drift against a tolerance threshold (default 1 px) and skipping compliant decks to maintain idempotency[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]. Applying writes requires explicit `--write` approval due to irreversible in-place modification[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
- **Workspace Auditing (`audit_organizers.py`)**: Reconciles accepted chapter organizers from intake sheets against Slack workspace channels via exact-string status matches and email identities[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]. Supports `--planned-ok` flags to account for pre-provisioned or private staging channels without aborting runs[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]. High-severity anomalies—such as public organizer channels—are prioritized to protect administrative privacy[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb].

# Security and Integration Boundaries
The skill enforces strict isolation governed by [Agent Plugin Portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md) and [Human Approval Gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md). All mutating operations require explicit human confirmation flags, and credential isolation prevents token leakage into command arguments or output logs[^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62][^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]. Verification routines and test suites are tracked in the [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md).

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Evaluation and Validation Suite
proposed_concept.description: CI test harness, pre-commit validation pipeline, and credential-isolated verification framework for AAIF community event plugins and skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation and Validation Suite provides continuous integration testing, linting, and structural verification for AAIF community event skills and plugin manifests[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6]. It establishes a strict security boundary by ensuring pull request validation workflows operate entirely credential-free on synthetic test fixtures, preventing credential exfiltration from forks or untrusted code[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation suite integrates multi-stage automated checks executed locally via pre-commit and enforced in GitHub Actions workflows[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6]:
- **Manifest Conformance**: Validates root `plugin.json` against the Agent Plugins v1 specification, verifies skill definitions against the [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) standard, and runs Claude Code CLI validation (`claude plugin validate .`) against marketplace and compatibility metadata[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210][^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].
- **Portability and Boundary Linting**: Inspects all `SKILL.md` files to ensure paths use relative `<skill-root>` notation and contain no client-specific tool names or command invocations[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210]. Verifies synchronization of tooling-rule banners across skill copies and checks `.gitignore` integrity to prevent local cache leakage[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
- **Static Security and Hygiene**: Executes Ruff for bug-focused Python syntax checks, Codespell for spelling validation, and Gitleaks for secret scanning[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210]. Enforces policies prohibiting secrets in command-line arguments and requires a centralized redaction surface (`--redact`) across reporting modules to prevent PII exposure in public logs[^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].
- **Deterministic Subprocess Testing**: Runs Pytest suites with synthetic fixtures in an isolated environment (`PYTHONPATH=lib`) with full clone history to guarantee end-to-end OOXML font-embed stripping and projection verification without live Google, Slack, or Luma API network calls[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

# Operational Boundaries
Live operational workflows requiring external API credentials run exclusively in gated, human-authorized GitHub Environments (`run-skill.yml`) triggered by `workflow_dispatch`, completely separated from read-only validation jobs[^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6]. This separation enforces the operational governance defined in [Agent Plugin Portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md) and implemented in [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Schema
proposed_concept.description: Twelve-column classification schema defining five structural dimensions and seven supporting fields for comparing production agentic workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification Schema is an analytical framework developed by the AAIF Workflows & Process Integration Working Group's Critical Use Cases workstream to consistently describe, categorize, and compare agent workflows across real-world deployments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]. It separates structural design choices into five discrete classification dimensions while capturing descriptive attributes, execution measurements, and operational evidence across seven supporting fields [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

The schema operates on the principle that workflows are classified against specific cited implementations rather than generalized use case titles, ensuring that architectural variations between implementations of similar business tasks remain visible [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

# Architecture / Specification
The schema defines twelve columns organized into five classification dimensions and seven supporting fields [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

### Classification Dimensions
Each classification dimension marks a structural architectural fork chosen during system design rather than an incidental runtime observation:
- **Trigger**: The event initiating execution, categorized into external system events, recurring scheduled intervals, or direct human invocation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **HITL Pattern**: The placement and necessity of human participation, defining where human input or sign-off is structurally required before execution continues (such as [../patterns/human-approval-gate.md](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Agent Count**: The number of distinct reasoning agents involved and the rationale for segregation, such as model differentiation, compartmentalized tool access, or task complexity [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Coordination**: The mechanism dictating sequencing across activities or agents, separating deterministic code following a script from dynamic LLM runtime reasoning [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Workflow Pattern**: The execution topology taken by the workflow, including linear sequences, concurrent branching and merging, or iterative evaluation loops [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

### Supporting Fields
Seven supporting fields record contextual and empirical data:
- **Duration**: Empirically measured agent runtime execution, excluding human queue latencies or downstream external processing [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Use Case**: Descriptive name of the business or technical workflow [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Description**: Unstructured narrative outlining workflow objectives and behavior [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Tools & Systems**: Enumeration of integrated APIs, platforms, and services invoked during execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Key Failure Mode**: Primary operational failure condition observed or defended against [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Preconditions**: Technical or data prerequisites required prior to invocation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].
- **Notes**: Evidentiary citations and contextual implementation rationales [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

# Lifecycle History
The classification schema was merged as an initial baseline draft within the `workstreams/critical-use-cases/` directory of the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group repository [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]. It awaits formal alignment with the Reference Architecture Workstream deliverables [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Specification
proposed_concept.description: Packaging and portability guidelines standardizing dual-manifest layout, namespaced metadata, placeholder paths, and capability checks for cross-client agent plugins.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability Specification provides packaging conventions, manifest requirements, and path normalization rules ensuring AI agent plugins and skills operate across diverse host clients and CLI harnesses without proprietary lock-in [^evt-community-events-pr-54]. Validated through the `aaif/community-events` repository, the standard aligns root-level Agent Plugins v1 manifests alongside proprietary client files, abstracting path bindings and isolating client-specific configuration into namespaced metadata [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

# Architecture / Specification

### Dual-Manifest Packaging
Portable plugin directories maintain a root Agent Plugins v1 `plugin.json` alongside platform-specific manifests [^evt-community-events-pr-54]. This dual-homing enables standard package discovery while preserving client-native enhancements. A dedicated `PORTABILITY.md` document specifies host runtime capabilities, execution boundaries, and authorization gates [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

### Skill Contract and Procedure Separation
To minimize host-specific context consumption and clarify interface boundaries, skills partition execution instructions into two distinct files [^evt-community-events-pr-54]:
- `SKILL.md`: Declares the minimal contract, input/output interfaces, and compatibility requirements [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- `WORKFLOW.md`: Houses the extended step-by-step procedural logic referenced on demand by the agent [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

### Path and Argument Abstractions
To avoid coupling to specific client path variables or interface conventions [^evt-community-events-pr-54]:
- Local filesystem roots replace engine-specific variables (such as `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`) with the standardized `<skill-root>` placeholder [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- Client-specific argument hints (e.g., `argument-hint`) are migrated out of core definitions into namespaced `metadata` blocks [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- All individual skill manifests declare explicit `compatibility` constraints [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

### Validation Suite
Conformity is verified in CI and pre-commit hooks via automated validators [^evt-community-events-pr-54]:
- `check_manifests.py`: Validates manifest syntax and structural integrity against standard schemas [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- `check_skill_portability.py`: Ensures skills avoid hardcoded environment paths and preserve portable placeholders [^evt-community-events-pr-54].
- `check_frontmatter.py`: Validates metadata consistency across all packaged skills [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

# Lifecycle History
The portability conventions were ratified in PR #54 of `aaif/community-events`, migrating 23 operational skills into standard portable packaging with dedicated automated validation [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Operational skill suite managing AAIF chapter operations, slide deck synthesis, multi-surface chapter renaming, and sync validation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations Skill Suite automates operational workflows for AAIF local community chapters, including chapter provisioning, asset rebranding, presentation deck synthesis, and data synchronization across Google Drive and CRM feeds [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3][^evt-community-events-pr-54]. The skill suite enforces strict validation and backup invariants to ensure chapter metadata, document relationships, and public URLs remain consistent across all distribution channels [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

# Architecture / Specification

### Multi-Surface Chapter Renaming
Renaming an existing chapter is implemented as an atomic, four-surface transformation executed by `rename_chapter.py` [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]:
1. **Directory Tree**: Renaming the root chapter folder on storage systems [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
2. **File and Subfolder Names**: Updating all containing filenames, CRM sheets, and media assets [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
3. **OOXML Text**: Mutating document body strings across `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` artifacts [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
4. **Document Metadata**: Updating `docProps` metadata properties and chapter labels [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

### Operational Safety Invariants
The renaming workflow enforces several deterministic safety invariants [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]:
- **Luma Slug Decoupling**: Chapter names and public Luma slugs represent distinct identities; slugs are never mutated automatically without explicit `--slug-from` and `--slug-to` arguments, preventing dead links when an event page remains at its legacy URL [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
- **OOXML Relationship Protection**: City-name string replacement is strictly barred from relationship files (`.rels`). Relationship targets only accept explicit slug substitutions to prevent broken internal XML target references [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
- **Pre-execution Backups**: All target files are copied into a timestamped `backups/rename-<UTC>/` archive prior to any remote upload [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
- **Dry-run Transparency**: Every candidate string change is echoed to standard output for human inspection prior to writing [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].
- **Post-run Verification**: The runner re-reads all artifacts from storage post-write and exits non-zero if residual old-name references remain [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

### Portable Skill Architecture
Operations adhere to [../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md), dividing operational workflows across lightweight `SKILL.md` contracts and detailed `WORKFLOW.md` step procedures validated by CI tests [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

# Lifecycle History
The four-surface rename workflow was codified following a 2026-08 migration that revealed sync discrepancies when folder names drifted from chapter feed listings [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3]. In PR #54, the entire skill suite was migrated to the portable Agent Plugins v1 layout [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Catalog of production agentic workflows classified by orchestration structure, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, failure modes, and evidentiary verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Inventory is an empirical reference catalog maintained by the Critical Use Cases Workstream within the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) that documents working, production-grade agent workflows across diverse industries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae]. Rather than presenting an exhaustive or speculative list of AI applications, the inventory captures concrete structural implementations—cataloging triggers, human-in-the-loop (HITL) gates, coordination mechanisms, agent counts, workflow shapes, failure modes, and operational preconditions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

The catalog aligns directly with the dimensional schema established in the [Agentic Use Case Classification](../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md) specification, prioritizing pattern breadth across operational contexts over volume within any single vertical [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

# Architecture / Specification

## Domain Coverage
The inventory categorizes agent workflows across three primary operational domains [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae]:
1. **Cross-Industry / Horizontal**: Workflows common across corporate functions, including Sales, Marketing, Customer Support, Finance & Operations, Human Resources & Recruiting, and Research & Intelligence.
2. **Technology & Engineering**: Systems-focused implementations spanning Engineering, IT / Network Operations, Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC), and Platform Engineering.
3. **Industry-Specific**: Highly regulated or specialized operational pipelines across Healthcare, Supply Chain, Legal, Education, and Real Estate.

## Workflow Invariants and Classification Dimensions
Each cataloged row captures structural fields defined in the AAIF schema [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae]:
- **Trigger**: The specific stimulus initializing agent activity, such as incoming messages, scheduled timers, webhooks, or system alerts.
- **HITL Pattern and Approval Gate**: Human oversight mechanisms, distinguishing between pre-execution authorization gates, asynchronous review queues, and post-execution escalations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Agent Count and Rationale**: Identifies single-agent versus multi-agent execution, mandating explicit rationales for workflows classified as "Better as multi-agent" or "Inherently multi-agent" [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Coordination Mechanism**: Communication and state-passing protocols coordinating participating agents.
- **Workflow Shape and Failure Modes**: Operational topology and primary runtime risks, such as context exhaustion or boundary drift.

## Evidentiary Standards and Verification
To maintain rigor and eliminate speculative vendor claims, the inventory enforces strict citation standards [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]:
- **Preferred Evidence**: Primary vendor announcements or product documentation referencing verified, named customer production deployments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Acceptable Evidence**: Vendor documentation showing robust feature capabilities operating in production at scale when customer names are proprietary [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Prohibited Sources**: Secondary blog posts, analyst market forecasts, academic preprints, and non-authoritative implementer write-ups are excluded [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Citation Density and Link Health**: Entries target three independent verifiable citations per row, with systematic auditing to prune link rot, acquisitions, and deprecated tooling [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification
proposed_concept.description: Twelve-column classification schema defining structural dimensions, coordination mechanisms, and evidentiary criteria for agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification schema is a standardized taxonomy and structural rubric maintained by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to systematically categorize, compare, and validate production agentic implementations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]. The framework establishes precise metadata definitions across triggers, human-in-the-loop (HITL) gates, multi-agent coordination architectures, and operational constraints [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

This classification schema serves as the formal foundation for the companion [Agentic Use Case Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-inventory.md), ensuring that real-world agent deployments are evaluated against uniform architectural criteria rather than informal marketing claims [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

# Architecture / Specification

## Structural Dimensions
The schema standardizes twelve core attributes across agentic systems:
1. **Functional Domain**: Horizontal business functions or industry verticals.
2. **Trigger Mechanism**: Event-driven, schedule-based, or manual agent initiation.
3. **Workflow Shape**: Sequence topology, including iterative convergence loops, directed graphs, or parallel swarms.
4. **HITL Pattern**: Enforcement points for human intervention, including patterns like [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) or [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md).
5. **Approval Gate Sub-Type**: Explicit taxonomy for runtime approval requirements and oversight mechanics [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
6. **Agent Count & Architecture**: Single-agent versus distributed multi-agent systems.
7. **Multi-Agent Rationale**: Mandatory documented justification when classifying workflows as "Better as multi-agent" or "Inherently multi-agent" [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
8. **Coordination Mechanism**: State machines, message passing, or shared persistent stores.
9. **Failure Modes**: Characteristic vulnerabilities, such as [Context Exhaustion](../taxonomy/context-exhaustion.md) or unconstrained tool recursion.
10. **Preconditions**: Environmental prerequisites, identity assertions, and system dependencies.
11. **Runtime Durations**: Execution envelopes and timeout budgets.
12. **Source Evidence & Citations**: Verifiable references documenting real-world operation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

## Evidentiary Standards and Citation Quality
To ensure schema integrity, entries classified under this framework must comply with rigorous verification thresholds [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]:
- **Tier 1 (Preferred)**: Direct vendor product pages or official press releases detailing named, verifiable enterprise customer deployments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Tier 2 (Acceptable)**: Vendor product documentation exhibiting documented production-scale features without public customer identification [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Excluded Sources**: Secondary analyst summaries, academic preprints, unverified third-party blogs, and commercial marketing forecasts are disallowed as primary evidence [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Citation Health**: Working groups conduct active link-rot mitigation, retiring stale URLs and updating records following corporate rebranding or software acquisitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

mutations.rationale: Integrate the People-Process-Technology capability classification matrix into operational security guidelines.

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Operational security guidelines structuring controls across people, process, and technology pillars for agent runtime defense.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices document provides operational engineering recommendations and risk mitigation strategies developed by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]. The guidelines establish comprehensive safeguards against common agent vulnerabilities, addressing dynamic prompt injection, credential exposure, privilege escalation across tools, and unbounded execution loops [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

Security controls are systematized using a three-pillar feature matrix—classifying implementations across people, process, and technology requirements to provide an enforceable defense-in-depth posture [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

# Architecture / Specification

## People, Process, and Technology Matrix
To translate high-level security objectives into actionable organizational controls, best practices map onto three operational dimensions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]:
- **People**: Capabilities focusing on personnel skills, security awareness, developer education, operational training, and human oversight vigilance required to safely design and operate autonomous agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].
- **Process**: Formal administrative procedures, documented governance policies, compliance workflows, auditing protocols, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) governing agent lifecycle stages [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].
- **Technology**: Technical safeguards, physical hardware mechanisms, digital security tools, policy-as-code proxies, isolation primitives like [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and automated policy engines enforcing boundary controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20].

## Core Security Controls
The guideline aligns operational security practices with foundational architectural patterns:
- **Least Privilege and Ephemeral Credentials**: Agents must operate under short-lived, narrowly scoped identity tokens rather than broad ambient credentials.
- **Enforced Execution Gates**: Sensitive actions requiring irreversible changes or crossing security boundaries require explicit [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) or [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) validation.
- **Fail-Safe Containment**: Runtime engines must provide out-of-band intervention mechanisms, incorporating patterns like [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) to instantly neutralize compromised agent instances.

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Operational skill suite managing AAIF chapter synchronization, roster audits, retirement candidate reporting, and slide generation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill is an automated operational tooling suite that manages AAIF regional chapter data, speaker registries, slide deck synthesis, and roster synchronization [^evt-community-events-pr-55]. The skill automates continuous synchronization between event databases, chapter roster sheets, and external community surfaces [^evt-community-events-pr-55].

To maintain data provenance and historical record fidelity, the synchronization engine enforces non-destructive chapter lifecycle invariants, ensuring active chapter records are never wiped automatically [^evt-community-events-pr-55].

# Operational Procedures

## Non-Destructive Chapter Synchronization
The chapter synchronization pipeline (`sync-chapters`) adheres to an immutable record policy:
- **No Direct Deletions**: Rows representing community chapters are never automatically erased from the Chapters List, preserving critical historical artifacts including local summaries, images, and operator notes [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
- **Retirement Candidates**: Chapters lacking qualifying active organizers are classified as retirement candidates via `retirement_candidates()` rather than being pruned [^evt-community-events-pr-55]. Candidates are surfaced in human-in-the-loop audit dashboards (such as the Drift tab) for operator assessment [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
- **Explicit Human Lifecycle Actions**: Deprecation requires explicit operator review:
  - Transitioning status to `Status=Deprecated` [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
  - Transitioning status to `Status=Merged` accompanied by a designated `Merged Into` target chapter [^evt-community-events-pr-55].
- **Validation and Disambiguation Holds**: The engine halts modification when city metadata is malformed, unrecognized, or ambiguous (such as capital-city renames or designated rosterless shadow chapters), preventing unintended drift [^evt-community-events-pr-55].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate and structural break between agent proposal generation and protected system execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Process with Human Approval reference architecture governs workflows where an autonomous agent prepares an action, a designated human approves or rejects it, and an independent workflow-controlled executor applies the protected effect only upon recorded approval[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]. It establishes a strict structural separation between reasoning and execution, preventing generative models from directly invoking irreversible or high-consequence system capabilities[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].

The architecture addresses common enterprise operations—such as issuing financial refunds, modifying production configurations, or dispatching external communications—where audit compliance mandates non-repudiation of authorization or where error reversal costs are high[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]. Core architectural guarantees require that no protected effect occurs without prior approval, the exact approved payload cannot be modified prior to dispatch, execution state survives long-duration waits, and complete provenance records link the proposer, approver, and executor[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].

# Architecture / Specification

## Pattern Composition
The reference architecture is composed of three core runtime patterns:
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Isolates the agent's exploratory and reasoning activities from the execution interface, restricting the agent to emitting structured action proposals[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md): Mandates explicit, non-bypassable sign-off from an authenticated human reviewer on the immutable candidate proposal[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].
- [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md): Converts human review delays into persisted, queryable suspension states, ensuring process runs survive restarts, infrastructure deployments, or multi-day wait times without dropping state or re-executing completed steps[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].

## Required Capabilities
Executing this architecture requires seven coordinated capabilities across the runtime environment[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]:
1. **Execution Engine**: Orchestrates step sequencing, state transitions, timers, and durable pauses.
2. **Agent Runtime**: Hosts the reasoning model, manages context windows, and synthesizes candidate plans.
3. **Tool Access Layer**: Restricts agent tools to read-only or sandbox queries, strictly excluding protected mutation endpoints.
4. **State and Context Store**: Persists run progress, agent inputs, intermediate evidence, and serialized proposals.
5. **Human Interaction Surface**: Presents the candidate proposal, context, and decision controls to authorized approvers.
6. **Workflow-Controlled Executor**: Executes approved actions against target systems strictly based on recorded authorization.
7. **Audit Log**: Immutably records the proposer identity, proposed payload, approver identity, approval verdict, and dispatch status.

## Task and Activity Boundaries
The architecture distinguishes between overarching business tasks and execution activities:
- **Business Task**: The end-to-end operational problem or request managed by the workflow (for example, a disputed transaction resolution)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-50].
- **Activities**: The discrete, scheduled units of work executed by either deterministic logic or model-driven agents to resolve that business task[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-50].

## Execution Separation and Review Feedback
Working group feedback highlights operational trade-offs concerning whether the executor must be isolated as an independent process or can run within an existing harness[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45]. An independent executor avoids stale in-memory context and security vulnerabilities following multi-day durable waits, while requiring fresh context loading at execution time[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45]. Reviewers also noted that decision criteria for introducing multi-agent configurations—such as separating reasoning sessions for independent critique—are illustrative design patterns rather than an exhaustive boundary[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History
- **Draft Reference Architecture**: Initial drafting codified pattern invariants, refund walkthroughs, and crash-recovery procedures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].
- **Clarification of Task and Activity Terminology**: PR #50 updated terminology to explicitly distinguish business tasks from [workflow primitives](../taxonomy/workflow-primitives.md) and activities[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-50].
- **Runtime Discussion**: Issue #45 introduced community feedback on executor isolation trade-offs and multi-agent routing criteria[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture governing iterative, autonomous problem resolution within predefined task boundaries, safety convergence loops, and deterministic acceptance gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a reference architecture governing agentic systems that autonomously diagnose, synthesize solutions for, and remediate technical or operational issues within constrained execution boundaries. The architecture relies on bounded iteration cycles, constrained effect scopes, and strict deterministic evaluation criteria to resolve failures without human intervention while guarding against diverging loops or collateral system damage.

To maintain safety without requiring manual human approval for every action, the architecture pairs autonomous exploration with a [deterministic acceptance gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) and [bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md). Proposed remediation candidates are evaluated against objective verification suites before deployment, ensuring that autonomous action remains bounded by policy and predictable exit criteria.

# Architecture / Specification

## Deterministic Gate Minimum Evidence Bar
Working group proposals establish that the required rigor of a deterministic acceptance gate scales directly with two fundamental properties of the permitted remediation effect[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]:
1. **Blast Radius**: The maximum scope, infrastructure surface area, or customer population affected if the remediation candidate fails or behaves incorrectly[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].
2. **Reversal Cost**: The operational, financial, or temporal difficulty required to roll back or undo the applied change[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].

As blast radius and reversal cost expand, gate validation must escalate from local functional assertions to comprehensive pre-flight verification, canary evaluations, or cross-system integration checks[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].

## Universal Acceptance Record Invariants
Independent of the specific gate strength required for a given remediation effect, every generated acceptance record must satisfy three invariant properties[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43]:
- **Verdict Determinism**: The evaluation verdict must be strictly reproducible given the identical candidate artifact and evaluation inputs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].
- **Candidate Binding**: The verdict record must cryptographically or structurally bind to the exact hash or immutable specification of the evaluated candidate, preventing post-evaluation tampering or payload substitution[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].
- **Execution Evidence Preservation**: The acceptance record, evaluation telemetry, and test outputs must be preserved as non-ephemeral execution evidence within the audit trail[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].

# Lifecycle History
- **Draft Architecture Intake**: Initial formulation establishing bounded iteration loops, resource ceilings, and acceptance gate checks.
- **Evidence Bar Calibration (PR #43)**: Open proposal resolving criteria for deterministic gate strength by mapping evidence requirements to blast radius and reversal cost while defining universal acceptance record invariants[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Operational security guidelines structuring controls across secret management, in-loop hooks, approval fatigue mitigation, confidential computing, and threat model mappings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes operational, runtime, and architectural controls across people, process, and technology pillars to secure autonomous agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations. Developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the deliverable defines prescriptive requirements spanning credential leakage prevention, tool invocation policy enforcement, human oversight validation, runtime observation baselines, and external threat matrix mapping.

# Architecture / Specification

## Secret Auditing and Credential Lifecycle
Security audits require comprehensive discovery across all local configuration files, tool communication transcripts, and host credential stores[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]:
- **Agent Configuration Files and Skills:** Automated scanners must audit MCP client configurations (such as `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, and `claude_desktop_config.json`) and portable [agent skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) for hardcoded environment keys and tokens[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Context and Memory Sanitization:** Tool outputs must be sanitized before re-entering conversation context or persistence layers to prevent credentials from entering transcripts, distributed traces, and long-term memory, mitigating OWASP ASI03 memory-based privilege retention[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Host Credential Isolation:** Execution environments must enforce explicit deny policies at agent hooks on sensitive host filesystem paths (including `~/.ssh` and cloud provider credential stores) to prevent local sandbox escapes from hijacking host sessions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Confidential Computing Limits:** Revisions clarify that hardware-isolated environments (such as confidential VMs) protect guest memory against host compromise but do not shorten token validity; guest software remains in the trusted computing base, meaning leaked bearer tokens retain full blast radius and lifespan regardless of hardware isolation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

## Tool Invocation and Policy Enforcement Points
Working group discussions differentiate network mediation from execution-layer enforcement[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30]:
- **In-Loop Hooks:** Authoritative policy enforcement belongs inside the agent execution loop, where every tool call can be intercepted regardless of transport layer (stdio, network sockets, shell commands, or SDK connectors) while retaining full prompt context[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].
- **Network Gateway Checkpoints:** External gateways like [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) provide payload capture, network discovery, and protocol mediation for remote MCP servers, but function as checkpoints feeding policy hooks rather than serving as single points of security failure[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].

## Human Oversight and Approval Fatigue Mitigation
Governance controls in the guide address the demonstrated failure modes of uncalibrated human-in-the-loop gates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35]:
- **Empirical Fatigue Baselines:** Proposals replace unverified incident examples with empirical research showing that flat approval prompts induce rubber-stamping; in tested coding agent deployments, human reviewers approved 97% of permission prompts and intercepted dangerous commands in only 13.6% of cases (dropping to roughly 5% after 50 prompts), while automated checks intercepted 89%[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- **Pre-Gate Validation:** Mandates pairing human approval prompts with automated acceptance checks and velocity monitoring to counter cognitive fatigue[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

## External Threat Framework Mappings
The guide's defense-in-depth principles align with recognized security standards[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32]:
- **MITRE ATLAS (v5.6.0):** Inline mappings trace mitigations to specific techniques including AI Agent Tool Poisoning (AML.T0110), Indirect Prompt Injection (AML.T0051.001), AI Supply Chain Compromise (AML.T0010.005), AI Agent Tool Credential Harvesting (AML.T0098), and Agentic Resource Consumption (AML.T0034.002)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].
- **OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026):** Mappings correlate operational controls with core vulnerability categories, including Memory-Based Privilege Retention (ASI03), Tool Poisoning and Shadowing (ASI02), Insecure Execution (ASI04), and Human In the Loop Failures (ASI08, ASI09)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained as an active deliverable by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md). Ongoing review issues focus on refining credential leakage threat boundaries, clarifying gateway versus in-loop enforcement scopes, integrating empirical approval fatigue statistics, and aligning taxonomy tags across the specification[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-32][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow governance pattern requiring authorized human review before executing sensitive agent actions, mitigated against approval fatigue via automated acceptance checks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Human Approval Gate pattern establishes an explicit execution pause in an autonomous agent workflow, requiring an authorized human operator to inspect and approve a structured proposal before any irreversible or high-impact tool can execute. Designed to maintain human accountability over autonomous systems, the pattern combines cryptographic approval binding with fatigue-reduction mechanisms to prevent superficial review and rubber-stamping.

# Architecture / Specification

## Workflow Execution and Proposal Split
Operating alongside the [proposal-execution split](./proposal-execution-split.md), the agent transitions into a [durable wait](./durable-wait.md) state upon assembling a critical action. The system creates an [approval checkpoint](./approval-checkpoint.md) record containing:
- The exact serialized command and target resource.
- Contextual justifications, tool provenance, and safety classifications.
- An immutable cryptographic hash binding the reviewer's signature directly to the payload.

Execution remains blocked until an authenticated operator signs an approval token or issues a structured rejection.

## Reviewer Fatigue and Vulnerability Profiles
Working group reviews highlight that flat, high-frequency approval gates suffer severe human reliability degradation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35]:
- **Rubber-Stamping Baselines:** In empirical studies of interactive coding agents, operators approved 97% of permission prompts indiscriminately[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- **Interception Degradation:** Humans intercepted dangerous commands in only 13.6% of presentations, with interception success dropping to approximately 5% after 50 consecutive prompts[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
- **Automated Gate Comparison:** By comparison, deterministic automated checks successfully intercepted 89% of the same hazardous operations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

## Fatigue Mitigation and Gate Calibration
To preserve defensive validity, implementations must not rely on unassisted manual review:
1. **Automated Pre-Filtering:** Precede human gates with [deterministic acceptance gates](./deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) that automatically intercept out-of-policy invocations before alerting human reviewers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].
2. **Approval Velocity Limits:** Monitor prompt repetition velocity and reviewer dwell times, flagging rapid sequential approvals for secondary review.
3. **Differential Impact Highlighting:** Visually distinguish destructive, network-exfiltrating, or credential-accessing arguments from routine read operations.

# Lifecycle History
Documented as an architectural governance pattern by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md). Empirical failure data and rubber-stamping defenses incorporated following technical reviews with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Architectural security pattern isolating policy enforcement and evidence signing inside hardware-attested enclaves while bounding guest software bearer token lifecycles.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Attested Isolated Runtime pattern executes agent policy engines, cryptographic signing keys, and privileged tool execution environments within hardware-enforced trusted execution environments (TEEs) or confidential virtual machines. By decoupling runtime trust from the underlying host and hypervisor, the pattern provides remote attestation of software integrity and protects sensitive memory state against infrastructure operators and adjacent tenants.

# Architecture / Specification

## Enclave Isolation and Remote Attestation
The runtime leverages hardware TEE mechanisms (such as AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, or ARM CCA) to guarantee memory encryption and state isolation:
- **Cryptographic Measurement:** Emits hardware-signed measurement quotes verifying the firmware, kernel, and agent runtime layers before cluster admission.
- **Report Payload Claims:** Attestation report payloads (such as Azure confidential VM REPORT_DATA) bind a cryptographic hash of runtime claims, including the virtual TPM key, guest configuration, and caller-supplied data[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].
- **Evidence Signing:** Signs [action records](../taxonomy/action-record.md) and telemetry directly within the protected boundary using hardware-derived keys.

## Threat Model Scope and Credential Exposure Boundaries
Security Working Group analysis defines the precise boundaries of hardware isolation models[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37]:
- **Guest Software within TCB:** Hardware attestation defends guest memory against unauthorized hypervisor and host access, but guest application software remains inside the trusted computing base[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].
- **Bearer Token Lifespans:** Hardware enclaves do not compress or limit token lifetimes; if a guest component or agent tool leaks a bearer token, the exposure window is determined by token validity and revocation mechanisms, while the blast radius is governed by token permissions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].
- **Layered Controls:** Enclave isolation must operate in tandem with short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials and internal compartmentalization restricting which guest components may access sensitive tokens[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

# Lifecycle History
Established by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) as a foundational hardware-attested trust pattern. Enclave threat model boundaries and bearer token lifetime specifications clarified during post-merge review discussions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-37].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry schemas, OpenTelemetry semantic conformance, cross-boundary execution tracing, and attestation protocols.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body developing vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, cross-boundary tracing frameworks, and execution attestation standards for autonomous and agentic systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]. The working group focuses on capturing causal execution chains, resolving telemetry gaps across tool boundaries, and standardizing agent behavioral records.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's scope and active deliverables encompass:
- **Semantic Conformance for OpenTelemetry**: Rather than maintaining a distinct, competing trace specification, current efforts focus on identifying semantic inconsistencies across agent SDK implementations of OpenTelemetry and defining a standardized semantic conformance framework[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Agentic Observability White Paper**: A living deliverable outlining practical organizational guidelines for observability, debugging, failure isolation, and cost control, coordinated alongside potential RFC submissions to standards venues such as IETF 127[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Cross-Workstream Attestation**: A joint initiative formed across working groups to formalize execution attestation and verifiable logging protocols[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **External Liaisons**: Active coordination and liaison outreach to standards bodies and industry consortiums, including FINOS for compliance testing, and platform maintainers across cloud providers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Observability Taxonomy Integration**: Collaborating with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define foundational observability vocabulary directly through GitHub tracking issues[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# Lifecycle History
In September 2026 meeting proceedings, the working group initiated efforts to align AI contribution standards requiring human review checkpoints, reframed the behavior trace model towards OpenTelemetry semantic convergence, chartered an attestation joint workstream, and began development of an organizational observability white paper[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Telemetry specification and OpenTelemetry semantic conformance framework standardizing session continuity, causal tool lineage, and agent execution spans.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open telemetry framework maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize execution spans, causal context propagation, and agent session tracking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]. The specification addresses semantic inconsistencies in how agent SDKs instrument reasoning loops, tool interactions, and delegation boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
While early work explored an independent telemetry serialization model, the technical direction focuses on an OpenTelemetry semantic conformance framework[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]. Because most production agent frameworks and software development kits already integrate with OpenTelemetry but apply inconsistent semantic attributes and span hierarchies, the specification focuses on:
- **Semantic Gap Remediation**: Documenting discrepancies and omissions across agent runtimes when emitting OpenTelemetry standard GenAI and span attributes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Conformance Test Suite**: Providing automated validation tools within the foundation's repositories to test whether SDK telemetry streams conform to standardized agent lifecycle and boundary semantics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].
- **Upstream Standardization**: Contributing refined semantic conventions and schema improvements directly to upstream OpenTelemetry working groups rather than creating an isolated standalone protocol[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

# Lifecycle History
The project was reframed during the September 2026 Observability and Traceability Working Group discussions to pivot from developing a disparate trace format toward establishing an OpenTelemetry semantic conformance suite and upstream contribution track[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Operational security guidelines structuring runtime sandbox boundaries, tool egress controls, approval gates, and prompt injection defenses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes operational and architectural baselines for securing autonomous AI agents operating across sensitive environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]. The guidelines address credential isolation, policy enforcement hooks, approval gate configurations, and execution confinement models.

# Architecture / Specification
The guidelines categorize security controls into distinct defensive layers:
- **Sandbox Confinement and Blast-Radius Constraints**: Evaluates the defensive limitations of containerized and directory-level agent execution environments. Review discussions within the working group emphasize that while sandbox modes effectively narrow the local filesystem blast radius to working directories, they do not inherently prevent network egress or unsandboxed execution handoffs to host tools[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34].
- **Network Egress and Exfiltration Defense**: Agents equipped with scripting runtimes (such as Python's standard `urllib`) can circumvent shell-level network restrictions (such as blocking `curl`), necessitating strict network namespace isolation or egress proxy filtering to prevent unauthorized data upload[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34].
- **Host Tool Handoff Risks**: Files emitted by an agent inside a restricted sandbox may subsequently be invoked or parsed by unconfined host processes, presenting an escape vector where malicious scripts or configurations bypass workspace barriers[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34].
- **Independent Approval Checkpoints**: Requiring external, policy-enforced approval checkpoints ([patterns/approval-checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md)) before actions cross trust boundaries or execute irreversible operations.

# Lifecycle History
The guide's sandbox confinement definitions underwent scrutiny in Issue #34, where reviewers highlighted production sandbox escapes and network exfiltration via standard runtime libraries to refine sandbox blast-radius claims from absolute containment to directory-scoped containment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-cutting AAIF workstream establishing unified agentic terminology, schema-validated taxonomies, and ecosystem catalogs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is an Agentic AI Foundation cross-cutting initiative standardizing terminology, definitions, and ecosystem classifications across autonomous agent technologies[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]. The workstream provides foundational vocabularies for other AAIF technical working groups and maintains interactive ecosystem landscape registries.

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream maintains the following schemas and intake pipelines:
- **JSON and Zod Validation**: The central taxonomy representation transitioned from a JavaScript file (`taxonomy-data.js`) to a declarative JSON format (`taxonomy/taxonomy.json`) validated in continuous integration via Zod schemas, eliminating custom syntax parsers and preventing malformed string submissions[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79].
- **Cross-Group Term Ingestion**: Domain working groups—such as [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and Agentic Commerce—submit emerging terms (including three-state reconciliation, witness scopes, and agent-completed or agent-in-the-loop transactions) for reconciliation into the foundational vocabulary[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-70][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-71].
- **Landscape Intake Criteria**: The ecosystem landscape registry accepts open-source agent projects and runtimes subject to established qualification thresholds, such as star minimums or explicit governance exceptions evaluated via tracking issues[^evt-aaif-landscape-issue-22].

# Lifecycle History
In late 2026, the workstream refactored its repository structure to use JSON with Zod validation to secure and streamline CI checks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-79], while coordinating web publication via GitHub Pages and receiving terminology contributions from domain working groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Operational skill suite and automation pipeline managing AAIF chapter lifecycle synchronization, country-level chapter resolution, and CRM membership audits.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite automates administrative synchronization across AAIF regional chapters, intake pipelines, CRM records, shared Drive repositories, and communication channels.[^evt-community-events-pr-57] It enforces standardized naming and hierarchy constraints, reconciles attendee and organizer roles, and maps local city representations into authorized regional and country chapters.

# Architecture / Specification

## Country Chapter Folding
The operational pipeline supports country-wide chapter structures where multiple municipal event locations fold into a single national chapter, permitting local organizers to host events in any city under one unified administrative umbrella.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]
- **Resolution Layer (`lib/aaif_events/cities.py`)**: A centralized `chapter_for()` resolver evaluates city inputs during intake and dynamically maps municipalities to their designated country chapters (e.g., Tokyo folds into `AAIF Japan`; Wellington and Auckland fold into `AAIF New Zealand`).[^evt-community-events-pr-57]
- **Ingestion Consistency**: The centralized resolver intercepts every subsystem reading intake city values, including chapter metadata synchronization (`sync_chapters.resolve_city`), document generation (`sync_about`), CRM integration (`sync_crm`), permission grants (`sync_access`), and Slack workspace audits.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]

## Clean Script Precedence
Because retired chapter records are retained for auditing purposes in master chapter lists, the maintenance script (`clean.py`) enforces that explicit country chapter fold dictionaries (`COUNTRY_CHAPTER_FOLDS`) override legacy sheet records to prevent retired municipal entries from reclaiming active cities.[^evt-community-events-pr-57] The fold rules are mirrored across standalone skills via synchronized mappings (`CITY_FOLDS`).[^evt-community-events-pr-57]

## Migration Sequencing Invariant
To preserve relational integrity between external assets and intake state, structural migrations from municipal to country chapters require an explicit ordering protocol:[^evt-community-events-pr-57]
1. Primary Google Sheet chapter rows, Google Drive directories, chapter About documentation, CRM listings, and icon assets must be renamed prior to merging codebase changes.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]
2. Automated sync routines evaluate the renamed entities at runtime. Executing runtime synchronization prior to asset renaming risks generating duplicate chapter entries and overwriting existing organizer metadata.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]

# Lifecycle History
- Merged support for national country chapter folding (folding Tokyo to Japan, Wellington/Auckland to New Zealand) and formalized asset pre-rename invariants.[^evt-community-events-pr-57]

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Meeting Notes Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill converting working group audio transcripts and AI summaries into standardized AAIF meeting notes documenting discussions, decisions, and action items.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Meeting Notes skill (`aaif-wg-meeting-notes`) is an explicit-load agent skill designed to assist working group chairs in compiling authoritative meeting records from conversational artifacts.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2] It parses meeting transcripts and preliminary AI-generated summaries to output structured notes adhering to the standard AAIF documentation format.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]

# Architecture / Specification

## Skill Structure
The skill package is organized into two primary files adhering to the modular skill packaging format:[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
- `SKILL.md`: Runtime instructions and contextual constraints directing the agent on parsing transcripts, filtering extraneous dialogue, and extracting factual outcomes.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
- `template.md`: Standardized AAIF working group meeting template defining the schema and section layout of the target markdown document.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]

## Processing Pipeline and Content Schema
When invoked explicitly by an operator, the skill extracts and formats key meeting elements into fixed structural sections:[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
- **Topics Discussed**: High-level narrative summaries of substantive technical or organizational discussions.
- **Decisions**: Explicit consensus points and formal working group resolutions reached during the session.
- **Deliverables**: In-progress and completed work products, specifications, or reference architecture assessments.
- **Action Items**: Assigned follow-up tasks linked to designated owners.
- **Artifact Links**: Direct hyperlinks to third-party AI summaries, full raw transcripts, and audio/video session recordings.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]

## Operational Invocations
The skill utilizes an explicit activation model and does not inject background context automatically; users load the directory into their agent environment (e.g., Cursor or Claude environments) and invoke it explicitly with target meeting identifiers.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2] The resulting document is stored in the respective working group's repository prior to human review and commit.

# Lifecycle History
- Proposed in the Working Group Chairs repository (`PR#2`), adapting prompts originally piloted in the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) for foundation-wide reuse.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Monthly Report skill (`aaif-wg-monthly-report`) is an explicit-load agent skill assisting working group chairs in drafting regular progress reports for the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md).[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2] It synthesizes the preceding month's meeting records, repository pull requests and commits, and prior status reports into a unified markdown report draft.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]

# Architecture / Specification

## Skill Structure
The skill package is partitioned into an operational prompt and output schema:[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
- `SKILL.md`: Procedural instructions guiding the agent to query the working group repository's GitHub activity, evaluate previous monthly reports, and aggregate recent meeting minutes.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
- `template.md`: Formal monthly reporting template defining standard reporting sections, including active workstreams, key achievements, and external ecosystem highlights.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]

## Workflow and Execution Cycle
The drafting cycle operates as an assisted human-in-the-loop workflow:[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
1. **Context Aggregation**: The skill ingests all meeting notes published during the target calendar month, inspects merged and open PRs across the working group repository, and ingests the previous month's report to track recurring deliverables.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
2. **Draft Synthesis**: The agent generates a candidate report placed at `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md`.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
3. **Human Review & PR**: The working group chair reviews the generated draft, tailors ecosystem highlights or cross-working-group items, and submits the finalized draft to the repository via pull request for Technical Committee review.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]

# Lifecycle History
- Proposed in the Working Group Chairs repository (`PR#2`) to provide a foundation-wide generic reporting framework based on earlier [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) templates.[^evt-working-group-chairs-pr-2]
