proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group standardizing telemetry schemas, OpenTelemetry semantic conformance, and cross-layer tracing reference architectures from kernel to AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical body chartered to establish vendor-neutral telemetry specifications, tracing frameworks, and evidence-grade observability models for agentic AI systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721] The group's work covers end-to-end tracing methodologies spanning low-level operating system mechanisms, hardware accelerators, network protocols, and high-level agent runtime behaviors.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]

# Architecture / Specification

## Five-Layer Reference Architecture Framework
The working group organizes its technology assessments and reference architectures along a bottom-up narrative stack structured into five discrete architectural layers:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]

1. **Layer 01 — Foundations**: Focuses on trace encoding, binary formats, and comparative frameworks, including the [Common Trace Format](../resources/common-trace-format.md) (CTF) for zero-copy nanosecond recording and [Trace Compass](../resources/trace-compass.md) for cross-domain trace visualization.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]
2. **Layer 02 — Kernel Tracing**: Analyzes operating system observability facilities, including [FTrace](../resources/ftrace.md), [Linux perf](../resources/linux-perf.md), [LTTng Kernel](../resources/lttng-kernel.md), [LTTng-UST](../resources/lttng-ust.md), kernel driver tracing, container scheduling and CFS throttling ([Container Orchestration Tracing](../resources/container-orchestration-tracing.md)), hypervisor stolen-time distortion ([Virtualization Tracing](../resources/virtualization-tracing.md)), [Tracy](../resources/tracy.md), [sysdig](../resources/sysdig.md), and [Falco](../resources/falco.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]
3. **Layer 03 — Hardware Accelerators**: Evaluates hardware profiling mechanisms, GPU kernel dispatches, tensor core utilization, and correlation across frameworks and accelerators (e.g., [NVIDIA Nsight](../resources/nvidia-nsight.md), [AMD ROCprofiler](../resources/amd-rocprofiler.md), and [PyTorch Profiler](../resources/pytorch-profiler.md)).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]
4. **Layer 04 — Network**: Analyzes on-the-wire communication, protocol verification, and packet capture using tools such as [Wireshark](../resources/wireshark.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]
5. **Layer 05 — AI Agent Observability**: Governs agent runtimes, LLM distributed tracing backends, product analytics, and semantic conventions mapping agent decisions to underlying system events.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]

## Core Initiatives and Specifications
- Telemetry specifications including the [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md).
- Cross-boundary observability mapping telemetry propagation across agent harnesses, tool calls, and host environments via the [Cross-Boundary Observability Model](../resources/cross-boundary-observability-model.md).
- Telemetry ingestion through vendor-neutral standards such as [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md).

# Lifecycle History
- Authoritative reference architecture assessments established covering foundational encoding through AI agent observability layers.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-cc8ae721]

# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the visual identity, typography, color palettes, and digital asset usage standards for the Agentic AI Foundation. These specifications ensure consistent visual presentation across documentation, slide decks, event collateral, and community web properties [^evt-community-events-pr-41].

# Architecture / Specification

## Canonical Logo Assets
Official vector assets reside in the central repository `assets/` directory and must be consumed directly by authors and automated generation agents [^evt-community-events-pr-41]:
- `aaif-mark.svg`: Serves as the primary full lockup, containing both the brand symbol and typographic mark despite its shortened filename.
- `aaif-icon.svg`: The standalone brand glyph intended for chapter badges, square icons, and avatars.
- `aaif-wordmark.svg`: Typographic wordmark without the standalone icon.

## Rendering Invariants
- **Never Redraw the Mark**: Agents and human contributors are strictly prohibited from redrawing, vectorizing from screenshots, or approximating the AAIF logo mark; the canonical SVGs must always be sourced directly [^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- **Palette and Typography**: Brand typography and color token tables in `DESIGN.md` establish authoritative values for digital, print, and presentation media [^evt-community-events-pr-41].

# References
- Automated brand tooling: [../skills/aaif-brand-guidelines.md](../skills/aaif-brand-guidelines.md)

# Overview
The Community Event Operations Skill provides automation pipelines and verification scripts supporting AAIF community chapters, event scheduling, speaker intake, and tabular data hygiene. It ensures consistent tracking of speaker submissions and operational status across localized chapters [^evt-community-events-pr-58].

# Architecture / Specification

## Data Hygiene and Inactive Filtering
The data sanitation script (`clean.py`) and live spreadsheet formulas audit submission rows across role sheets. To prevent noisy false positives, triage rules suppress issue flagging for inactive records under specific conditions [^evt-community-events-pr-58]:
- **Suppression Criteria**: A submission is excluded from error flagging when every role tab where it is registered records a status of `Denied`, `Inactive`, or `Duplicate` [^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Multi-Role Handling**: If an applicant has active or prospective status on any single role tab (e.g., organizer Denied, but speaker still Prospect), flags remain active to ensure pending reviews receive attention [^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Status Column Dependency**: If a sheet lacks explicit `Status`, `Timestamp`, or `Email` columns, suppression is bypassed to avoid hiding actionable errors [^evt-community-events-pr-58].
- **Formula Generation**: Dynamic sheet formulas (`issues_formula()`) evaluate matching `DECIDED_NO` statuses, displaying a blank state rather than highlighting inactive entries [^evt-community-events-pr-58].

# References
- Community test suite: [../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Technical working group defining commerce capabilities, payment protocol boundaries, dispute accountability, and transaction evidence architecture across autonomous agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, capability maps, and protocol boundaries governing autonomous financial transactions, checkout handoffs, and post-purchase accountability. The group defines how agent identity, user delegation, and transaction execution are bound and audited across merchant and payment domains [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

# Architecture / Specification

## Capability Map and Post-Purchase Accountability
The working group organizes agentic commerce workflows across lifecycle phases, standardizing cross-boundary evidence requirements for dispute resolution and auditability [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]:
- **Evidence Binding**: Tamper-evident receipts and audit trails binding delegation identifiers, transaction IDs, agent credentials, shopper identities, and signed claims [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Signal Provenance**: Clear attribution distinguishing self-reported agent assertions from independently observed markers across platforms, merchants, and payment providers [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Authorization Strength for State Changes**: Verified evidence requirements separating order observation from state-changing post-purchase remedies such as returns, cancellations, or refunds [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
- **Auditability**: Post-purchase retention bundles enabling relying parties to independently verify authorizations and replay dispute trails [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

## Bounded Verification Verdict Envelope
To standardize verification results across merchant and payment platforms without renegotiating transaction state, the group evaluates an eight-field machine-readable contract [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5]:
1. `verdict`: Three-state classification (`supported`, `contradicted`, or `unresolvable`) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
2. `verifier`: Identity of the computing verification entity, distinct from the claim producer [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
3. `verifier_signature`: Cryptographic signature over the verdict and canonical hashes [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
4. `evidence_refs`: Explicit delegation, transaction, and consent identifiers [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
5. `evidence_fingerprints`: Canonical hashes (RFC 8785) supporting deterministic verification replay [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
6. `verification_basis`: Specification of rule sets and checks evaluated [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
7. `witness_scope`: Explicit boundary coverage of what the verdict attests [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].
8. `timestamp`: Freshness timestamp of verdict evaluation [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-issue-5].

## Terminology Alignment
The group collaborates with the taxonomy workstream to standardize terms including Agentic commerce protocols across payment layers [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-75].

# References
- Reconciliation model: [../taxonomy/three-state-reconciliation.md](../taxonomy/three-state-reconciliation.md)
- Observability and trace coordination: [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Identity delegation: [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group bridging global AI policy developments and technical agentic AI architectures through governance frameworks, risk classifications, and reversible execution standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (GRRA WG) serves as the primary bridge between international AI regulatory frameworks and technical specifications across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]. Approved on June 1, 2026, the working group identifies policy developments, analyzes operational governance for agentic communication protocols, and establishes interoperable risk mitigation strategies for enterprise and open-source agent deployments[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

The working group is led by Chair Deborah Eng (JPMorgan) and Co-chair Sriram Natarajan (Google)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

# Scope and Responsibilities
The GRRA WG operates under explicit boundaries to support open-source agent governance without providing legal advice or formal compliance certification[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

## In Scope
- **Regulatory Monitoring:** Tracking, identifying, and evaluating existing and emerging global regulations, standards, and AI policy frameworks influencing the deployment of agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Protocol Governance:** Examining how protocols—including the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—are operationalized within enterprise policy controls and organizational governance structures[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Open Source Advocacy:** Developing policy recommendations and transparent insights that advance the adoption of open-source agentic AI projects[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

## Out of Scope
- Providing legal counsel, definitive compliance solutions, or formal regulatory legal opinions[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

# Future Workstreams and Roadmap
The charter outlines several target technical areas and potential standards initiatives under active consideration[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf]:
- **Reversibility and Undo Infrastructure:** Researching formal methods, protocols, and interchange formats for action reversibility characterization and broadening the scope of reversible agent actions[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **AI Agent Bill of Materials:** Defining standard machine-readable provenance schemas ([`AI Agent Bill of Materials`](../taxonomy/ai-agent-bill-of-materials.md)) covering foundation models, scaffolding harnesses, tools, APIs, and external components[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Autonomy & Human-in-the-Loop:** Specifying risk tiers, autonomy definitions, and operational controls such as [`Human Approval Gates`](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [`Hard-Constraint Gates`](../patterns/hard-constraint-gate.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Incident Reporting and Discovery:** Formulating transparent policies governing agent discovery frameworks and post-incident disclosure workflows[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **Industry Vertical Alignment:** Evaluating and adopting vertical governance specifications, including integration with the FINOS AI Governance Framework[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-01:** Charter officially approved by the AAIF [`Technical Committee`](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].
- **2026-10-09:** Charter updated with expanded scope covering reversibility protocols, vertical frameworks, and AI Agent Bill of Materials specifications[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-13ea07bf].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical body chartered to establish comprehensive threat models, runtime security design patterns, and cross-cutting defense guidelines for autonomous agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group produces foundational baseline guidance, design pattern catalogs, and threat landscape gap analyses.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group operates across five active workstreams stood up in June 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]:
- **Threat Modeling**: Produced the [Threat Modeling Gap Analysis](../resources/agentic-ai-threat-modeling-gap-analysis.md), evaluating existing industry frameworks against agentic vulnerabilities and merged as a draft deliverable [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **Best Practices**: Authoring the [Agentic AI Security Best Practices](../guidelines/agentic-ai-security-best-practices.md) guide and the Security Best Practices Feature Matrix [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-36].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Establishing structured architecture patterns including [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md), landing its initial pattern drafts in late 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinating domain-specific security and privacy terms for review and integration into the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) unified taxonomy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **Review and Protocols**: Driving review checklists and cross-working group protocol coordination [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06**: Stood up five workstreams with confirmed leads; transitioned initial taxonomy work into the cross-WG effort [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **2026-07**: Published initial pull requests for the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Best Practices Guide; finalized the structural outline of the Design Patterns Catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **2026-08**: Released past meeting recordings publicly, established internal review and PR merge policies, and expanded cross-WG collaboration on shared review checklists [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **2026-09**: Formally merged the Best Practices Guide and Threat Modeling Gap Analysis into `deliverables/`, landed initial four design pattern drafts, merged the Feature Matrix, and introduced alternate-week APAC meetings [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].

# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill governs automated tooling, Google Sheets scripts, and CRM pipelines supporting AAIF regional chapters, intake pipelines, and event coordination [^evt-community-events-pr-59]. It maintains data consistency across participant applications, chapter lead directories, speaker queues, and collaborator engagements.

# Architecture / Specification

The intake subsystem processes contributor applications submitted through public forms into centralized operational spreadsheets and chapter CRMs [^evt-community-events-pr-59]:
- **Multi-Role Intake Routing**: Form submissions evaluate discrete Yes/No questions per operational role (organizer, speaker, host/venue, collaborator) rather than a single choice, permitting single applicants to apply for multiple roles concurrently [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **Role Tabs and Guard Formulas**: Applications are split into filtered views (`Organizers`, `Hosts`, `Speakers`, `Organizers by City`, and `Collaborators`). Formulas include column guards that emit explicit warning banners (`MISSING FORM COLUMN: <question>`) instead of failing silently via blanking filters [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **Migration Tooling**: The `migrations/migrate_intake_role_gates.py` script applies idempotent updates across spreadsheet formulas, verifying expected row counts and column references prior to production write commits [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **CRM Synchronization**: The `sync_crm` pipeline reconstructs composite legacy interest fields (`GATE_INTEREST`) from multi-role selections to preserve backwards compatibility with chapter CRMs while keeping the un-synced `Collaborators` queue isolated in Intake Ops [^evt-community-events-pr-59].
- **Deduplication and Validation**: Tools such as `clean.py scan` validate required question columns and enforce organizer duplicate prevention rules across live form submissions [^evt-community-events-pr-59].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-10**: Merged PR #59 establishing per-role intake questions, idempotent migration scripts for spreadsheet gate formulas, and a dedicated `Collaborators` role tab [^evt-community-events-pr-59].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Operational security guidelines structuring runtime sandbox boundaries, tool egress controls, approval checkpoints, and credential isolation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline provides defensive specifications and runtime security recommendations for deploying autonomous agents in enterprise environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]. Developed by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the deliverable defines control requirements across execution sandboxing, tool egress, authorization checkpoints, and credential segregation.

# Architecture / Specification

The guideline establishes concrete implementation criteria for securing agent execution boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e]:
- **Sandbox Isolation**: Agents must run within isolated environments that restrict host system access, utilizing patterns such as [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).
- **Tool Egress Filtering**: Outbound network and tool calls must be mediated through policy gateways to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration and prompt injection escalation.
- **Approval Checkpoints**: High-impact or irreversible actions mandate policy-bound checkpoints, incorporating [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) mechanics.
- **Emergency Termination**: Systems must implement out-of-band termination capabilities modeled on the [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) pattern.
- **Deliverable Feature Matrix**: The guideline links with the Security Best Practices Feature Matrix, providing comparative scoring and conformance checklists across deployment architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-36].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07**: Initial draft submitted as a pull request within the Security and Privacy Working Group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e].
- **2026-09**: Officially merged and registered as a draft deliverable in `deliverables/` alongside the Security Best Practices Feature Matrix [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-440eb159591a-c575359e] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-36].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Operational security guidelines structuring runtime sandbox boundaries, tool egress controls, pre-execution hooks, and tiered authorization oversight.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes operational and architectural security baselines for autonomous agents, delineating execution sandbox boundaries, outbound tool egress restrictions, and action authorization frameworks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]. Maintained by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guideline defines defense-in-depth enforcement mechanisms to prevent untrusted agent actions from bypassing organizational policy.

# Architecture / Specification

## Multi-Tier Authorization and Pre-Execution Hooks
Section 4 of the guidelines defines authorization controls governing tool invocations and sensitive actions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]:
- **Classification Boundaries**: Tier assignment must be enforced outside the agent boundary by an orchestration-layer classifier or policy engine, strictly prohibiting self-reported authorization tiers by the model [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Pre-Execution Interception**: Tool actions are subject to interceptor hooks evaluated prior to execution, supporting programmatic responses including `allow`, `deny`, `modify`, or `ask` (escalation to human approval) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31]. Automated rules and deterministic policies execute first, followed by optional model judges, reserving human checkpoints specifically for ambiguous or elevated-risk escalations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Call-Site Parameter Context**: Authorization decisions evaluate full invocation payloads—including tool identity, runtime arguments, and task context—rather than relying solely on static operation types [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Approval Fatigue Mitigation**: Reliance on unassisted [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) introduces severe operational risk due to approval fatigue, where empirical testing demonstrates habitual pass-through (e.g., 97% human approval rates with catch rates dropping to ~5% over prolonged sessions), necessitating automated rule-based filtering prior to human review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

## Runtime Controls and Egress Policies
- **Sandbox Isolation**: Agents executing external commands or shell scripts must be restricted to hardened container or microVM boundaries, isolated from internal control planes.
- **Egress Filtering**: Tool-level network communication requires deterministic allowlists at the code and transport layers to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration or unsanctioned tool calls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].
- **Emergency Termination**: Systems must integrate an external [kill switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) mechanism capable of halting agent sessions immediately upon policy violation.

# Lifecycle History
- Originating in the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), the guide established baseline runtime isolation and authorization tiers.
- Issue #31 initiated technical review of Section 4 to resolve ambiguities between static design-time classification and runtime action inspection, incorporating pre-execution hook architectures aligned with external specifications such as the OWASP Agent Control Standard [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-31].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and evaluation frameworks for AI agent identity, cryptographic attestation, and delegated authority verification [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17]. Operating under the technical governance of the AAIF [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group produces specifications for credential lifecycle management and verifiable dispatch authorization.

# Architecture / Specification

## Workstreams and Deliverables
- **Authority-at-Dispatch Catalogue**: A structured comparison catalogue and automated testing workflow benchmarking delegated authority mechanisms [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17]. Traces in the comparison require versioned contract identifiers, evidence age tracking, and deployed freshness limits, validated using automated tooling such as [agent-evidence-observer](https://github.com/probityai/agent-evidence-observer) across test runs including MintID, Proofable, and Alakris [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].
- **Credential Verification**: Exploration and evaluation of human-backed agent credentials and verifiable delegation chains, formalizing how human authority is securely bound and attested to autonomous subagents [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-16].
- **Evidence Verification Standards**: Development and maintenance of schema specifications such as the [Evidence Record Specification](../standards/evidence-record-spec.md) and classification frameworks like [Evidence Strength Labels](../taxonomy/evidence-strength-labels.md).

# Lifecycle History
- Established as an active working group under the AAIF charter.
- PR #16 scheduled presentation tracks for human-backed agent credential architectures [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-16].
- PR #17 introduced the authority-at-dispatch comparison catalog and CI verification workflow for multi-provider authority traces [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-17].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated CI test harness and validation framework verifying operational agent skills, event lifecycle automation, and chapter management pipelines [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad]. Maintained within the AAIF community repository, the suite couples credential-isolated test runners with intent-matching graders to ensure agent skills trigger accurately on non-technical user input [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].

# Architecture / Specification

## Grader Architecture and Natural-Language Intent Verification
- **Skill Activation Graders**: Evaluates whether an agent runtime invokes the correct skill tool in response to conversational prompts without relying on explicit keyword triggers [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].
- **Setup Verification Pattern**: Implements frontmatter-based grader definitions matching regex invocations (e.g., `aaif-check-setup`) when non-technical inquiries such as "is it all working" are posed without containing keywords like "setup" or "check" [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].
- **Execution Isolation**: Runs verification checks inside isolated runner environments to evaluate [community event operations skills](../skills/community-event-operations.md) against regressions before changes are merged.

# Lifecycle History
- Established to provide regression testing and CI verification across event automation workflows.
- Authoritative commit added intent-matching graders in `evals/check-setup/graders/skill_fires.md` to evaluate tool activation against colloquial phrasing [^evt-community-events-file-cd95e0a9e63d-5578e7ad].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill suite and execution engines automating AAIF chapter intake, spreadsheet sanitization, immutable state backups, and design system sweeps.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Community Events Toolkit (`aaif-events`) provides an operational skill suite and script engines that teach AI assistants—such as Goose and Claude Desktop—how to orchestrate AAIF chapter operations, triage member intake, maintain event trackers, and enforce brand conformity across template estates [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04]. Built to support non-technical chapter operators, the suite adheres strictly to a proposal-execution split [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7], producing read-only reports and execution plans by default and mandating explicit operator approval before committing state changes to Google Drive, Slack, or Luma [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04].

# Architecture / Specification
The toolkit is organized around modular skills adhering to the AAIF skill layout and progressive disclosure model [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]:

- **Intake Data Sanitization (`aaif-clean-data`)**: Normalizes the Community Intake Ops sheet by canonicalizing URLs, standardizing text casing, deriving city locations, flagging malformed emails, and highlighting unassigned or ambiguous entries [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7]. The pipeline processes multi-role application gates (organizers, speakers, hosts, collaborators) [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7]. All cell values are injected via raw APIs without formula execution (`USER_ENTERED`), treating spreadsheet inputs as untrusted data to prevent prompt and formula injection [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7].
- **Immutable State Snapshots (`aaif-backup`)**: Captures local, timestamped snapshots (`backups/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>`) of Google Drive documents or local files prior to risky bulk edits [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]. Backups are strictly immutable and never overwritten, ensuring reliable diffing and rollback capabilities [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09].
- **Estate Design System Sweep (`restyle_design_system.py`)**: Conforms chapter decks, event trackers, and CRM workbooks to the Foundation's design tokens and agent artwork [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. The sweep operates strictly on named template files rather than custom event decks, separating SpreadsheetML cell data from XML styles and workbook themes (`xl/styles.xml`) [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601]. It archives un-styled versions to `backups/restyle-<UTC>/` before modifying assets and evaluates WCAG AA contrast to repair illegible text [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-b2c9a601].
- **Tooling and Runtime Constraints**: All Google Drive interactions are executed exclusively via Python driving the `gws` CLI; headless desktop suites such as LibreOffice or `unoconv` are strictly prohibited due to font substitution and silent OOXML stripping [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-0c489bc7] [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-36b98c09]. Credential resolution cascades from environment variables, to root `.env`, to the macOS keychain (`aaif-slack-read-token`, `aaif-slack-write-token`, `luma-api-key`) with execution-scoped caching [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

# Lifecycle History
Originally structured around monolithic maintenance scripts, the community events toolkit was refactored into modular skills compatible with `../standards/agent-skills.md` [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]. Integration enhancements added non-technical operator interfaces for Goose and Claude Desktop, automated role intake tab gating, and deterministic keychain credential resolution [^evt-community-events-file-06572a96a58d-9d2d11f7].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability and Authoring Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Packaging, manifest layout, and procedural authoring guidelines standardizing portable agent skills and multi-client plugin distribution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability guidelines establish packaging layouts, manifest interoperability standards, and authoring principles ensuring AI skills operate seamlessly across heterogeneous runtime harnesses such as Goose, Cursor, Claude Code, and Claude Desktop [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4] [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-f722dd04]. By decoupling procedural instructions from host-specific configuration files, the framework allows an agent repository to act as a unified, installable plugin while maintaining compatibility with diverse marketplace discovery mechanisms [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].

# Architecture / Specification
A portable plugin package combines root-level multi-client manifests with encapsulated, procedurally constrained skill directories [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]:

- **Manifest Interoperability**: The repository root serves as the primary plugin boundary. A top-level `plugin.json` specifies configuration for shared agent environments such as Codex and Cursor, while `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` provide metadata and marketplace discovery records for Claude Code environments [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].
- **Directory Encapsulation**: Skills reside in distinct subdirectories under `skills/<skill-name>/`, containing a primary `SKILL.md` procedural spine along with optional `scripts/` (and accompanying `test_*.py` test suites) and on-demand `references/` [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].
- **Procedural Spine Constraints**: `SKILL.md` files must remain strictly under 500 lines and approximately 5,000 tokens to prevent context window saturation and instruction distraction during tool execution [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]. Frontmatter requires explicit `name`, single-line `description` (identifying action and trigger condition "Use when asked to..."), `compatibility` declarations, and optional client argument hints [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].
- **Progressive Disclosure Architecture**: Supplementary documentation and specialized procedural guides must be placed in `references/`. Every reference document is required to open with a clear condition defining when it must be loaded, paired with a matching routing matrix in `SKILL.md` [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].
- **Action-Oriented Checklists and Gotchas**: Multi-step operations must be authored as ordered markdown task checklists with explicit approval checkpoints rather than descriptive narrative prose [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4]. Gotcha sections are reserved strictly for unintuitive runtime edge cases that defy common agent assumptions [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].

# Lifecycle History
Refined during the migration of operational community automation repositories, these guidelines addressed context overflow caused by oversized instructional files and fragmented client-specific plugin structures [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-4eaff5f4].

# References
- [../standards/agent-skills.md](../standards/agent-skills.md)
- [../skills/community-event-operations.md](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- [../resources/goose.md](../resources/goose.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill suite and execution engines automating AAIF chapter intake, diagnostic setup, local chapter creation, attendee messaging, and community pulse generation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite standardizes local community management, chapter onboarding, and communication workflows across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77][^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. Packaged as modular agent skills conforming to AAIF specifications[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77] (see [Agent Skills Standard](../standards/agent-skills.md)), the suite provides automated tooling to verify local environments, provision city chapters, draft attendee logistics, publish multi-channel community updates, and create versioned backups[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].

All skills adhere to strict operational boundaries designed to preserve brand asset fidelity and safeguard community privacy across public and semi-private channels[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708][^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a]. The suite is continuously validated by an automated test harness (see [Community Events Eval Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)).

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Operational Invariants

### Tooling Boundary: Google Workspace CLI and Python
Across all file read and write operations, the suite enforces a strict tooling rule: every interaction with Google Drive must execute via Python driving the `gws` command-line interface[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77][^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **Native Formats First**: Native Google files (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) must be modified directly through Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **OOXML Surgery**: Binary Office formats (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) undergo direct byte-level zip part surgery to preserve embedded fonts and untouched assets[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **Prohibition on Headless Office**: The suite strictly bans LibreOffice (`soffice`), `unoconv`, or desktop office suites for conversions or previews, as they substitute local system fonts for brand typography and drop unrecognized OpenXML tags[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. Previews must be generated via API rendering (e.g., Slides API PNG export or Google Doc PDF export)[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

### Public-Copy Rule and Privacy Protection
All text composed by community skills is treated as publishable copy[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e].
- **Prohibited Identifiers**: Agents must never output unverified attendee names, email addresses, phone numbers, or door access codes[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e].
- **Transcript Safety**: When an unpublishable field is omitted, agents must reference the field name rather than the value itself, preventing private details from leaking into conversation histories or transcripts[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e].
- **Standard Compliance**: Public communications append standard links to the Linux Foundation Code of Conduct (`https://events.linuxfoundation.org/about/code-of-conduct`) and Privacy Policy (`https://www.linuxfoundation.org/legal/privacy-policy`)[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e].

### Untrusted Data Boundaries
External data sources—including Slack messages (`#local-champs`), spreadsheet cells, and event RSVPs—are categorized strictly as untrusted source data, never executable instructions[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51]. Indirect prompt injections attempting to grant permissions or alter status fields must be flagged back to human operators rather than executed[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].

## Skill Catalog

| Skill | Scope | Primary Execution Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `aaif-check-setup` | Environment diagnostics | Read-only check of Python 3, `gws` OAuth, Slack API, Luma keys, and Chrome[^evt-community-events-file-3422d7005bbb-fcddfd77] |
| `aaif-create-chapter` | Chapter provisioning | Clones `TemplateCity` in Google Drive, substitutes city tokens, rebrands OOXML assets, and repositions map dots via Nominatim geocoding[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708] (see [aaif-create-chapter](aaif-create-chapter.md)) |
| `aaif-community-pulse` | Multi-audience updates | Executes 6-step gathering pipeline across Slack, Luma, and git commits to write 3 audience-tailored draft files into `.pulse-cache/`[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51] (see [aaif-community-pulse](aaif-community-pulse.md)) |
| `aaif-attendee-reminder` | Logistics messaging | Reads event tracker entries via `fetch_tracker.py`, masks private door/speaker details, and formats builder-to-builder RSVP reminders[^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-7315ad6e] |
| `aaif-backup` | Immutable snapshotting | Exports timestamped binary snapshots (`.xlsx`, `.docx`, `.pptx`) to local directories, keeping published repos free of binary tracking[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7] |

## Backup Architecture
The `aaif-backup` skill writes immutable, chronological file snapshots under `backups/<slug>/<UTC-timestamp>.<ext>`[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]. For local checkouts, snapshots are git-ignored; in packaged desktop installations (Goose, Claude Desktop), backups persist in application support paths to survive plugin upgrades[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7]. Restorations are deliberately manual to preserve cell formulas and conditional formatting[^evt-community-events-file-f922f666d0ff-e2dbe3f7].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Chapter Skill
proposed_concept.description: Automated chapter provisioning skill cloning TemplateCity Drive assets, executing OOXML rebranding, and geocoding map coordinates for new AAIF city locations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-create-chapter` skill automates the launch and provisioning of new AAIF city chapters within the Foundation's Google Drive infrastructure[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. Operating under the [Community Event Operations](community-event-operations.md) suite, it clones the standard `TemplateCity` directory structure—encompassing event trackers, attendee spreadsheets, and presentation slide templates—and systematically rebrands assets from the San Francisco baseline to the target municipality[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

In addition to text transformations, the skill resolves physical geographic coordinates to reposition visual map markers across presentation decks, ensuring brand compliance without requiring manual design adjustments[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

# Architecture / Specification

## Asset Transformation Pipeline
Chapter creation requires Python 3 and authenticated `gws` CLI access to the Google Drive `Chapters` workspace[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. The engine creates a new chapter folder containing:
- `Event Tracker.docx`
- `Attendee CRM.xlsx`
- `Event Template/` and `Banners (...)/` subdirectories housing design assets (`Slides.pptx`)[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

### Rebranding Substitution Matrix
The provisioning pipeline systematically swaps municipal tokens while isolating template placeholders (such as speaker bios, dates, or neighborhood venues)[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]:

| Source Token | Target Replacement | Rules & Context |
|---|---|---|
| `San Francisco` / `SAN FRANCISCO` | Target City Name | Case-matched replacement across text and file names[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708] |
| `SF` Abbreviation | Full City Name | Converted to uppercase in all-caps headings and title case in body copy[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708] |
| `aaif-sanfrancisco` | `aaif-<slug>` | Replaces Luma calendar handles and hyperlink URLs[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708] |
| File / Folder Names | Renamed City Name | Propagates name changes to files such as `<City> CRM.xlsx`[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708] |

### Map Dot Geocoding
On Slide 5 ("THE NETWORK") of `Event Template/Slides.pptx`, the engine repositions the green "you-are-here" indicator and its `<CITY> · TONIGHT` label[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. Coordinates are derived from CLI parameters (`--lat`/`--lon`) or resolved automatically using Nominatim keyless geocoding[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708]. If geocoding fails or operates offline, the dot remains at San Francisco with an explicit warning rather than aborting execution[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

## Execution Invariants
- **No Desktop Office Suites**: Office binary manipulation is performed via zip-level OOXML surgery or Google APIs; tools like LibreOffice (`soffice`) are strictly banned to prevent font corruption[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].
- **State Recovery**: Supports `--resume` and `--repair-existing` flags to recover cleanly from partial network failures or incomplete Google Drive transfers[^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-0c36b708].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Community Pulse Skill
proposed_concept.description: Multi-channel update drafting skill aggregating Slack, Luma, and git activity into separate organizer, member, and public communications under prompt-injection isolation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-community-pulse` skill drafts the periodic "AAIF Community Organizer Update" (the Pulse), summarizing recent chapter events, upcoming calendar schedules, and foundation operational updates[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51]. Operating under the [Community Event Operations](community-event-operations.md) suite, the skill executes a single data collection pass across Slack, Google Sheets, Luma, and git commits to synthesize three distinct, audience-specific drafts[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].

The skill enforces strict security and privacy boundaries: it writes local drafts only, never posts autonomously to external APIs, and isolates untrusted user messages to prevent prompt injection[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].

# Architecture / Specification

## Three-Audience Publishing Model
Because community groups require differing depths of operational detail, the skill creates three distinct text files in a local `.pulse-cache/` directory rather than duplicating content[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51]:

| Draft Variant | Target Audience | Primary Focus | Destination File |
|---|---|---|---|
| Organizer Post | `#local-champs` | Actionable requests, admin and tooling changes, chapter-specific asks[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51] | `.pulse-cache/pulse-local-champs.txt`[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51] |
| Member Post | `#general` | Event recaps, upcoming community calendar, participation links[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51] | `.pulse-cache/pulse-general.txt`[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51] |
| Public Post | LinkedIn / X | High-level foundation narrative, milestones, external awareness[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51] | `.pulse-cache/pulse-social.txt`[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51] |

The organizer draft assumes readers have already viewed the `#general` post and deliberately avoids repeating event listings, focusing exclusively on operational directives[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].

## Six-Step Workflow Pipeline
Execution proceeds strictly through six sequential phases[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51]:
1. **Gather Organizer Updates**: Fetches semi-private channel history from Slack `#local-champs` via `fetch_local_champs.py`[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
2. **Read Sheet Status**: Inspects community intake spreadsheets via `gws` to detect newly formed chapters and assigned organizers[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
3. **Query Luma Calendar**: Retrieves past and scheduled events across chapter feeds[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
4. **Inspect Git History**: Analyzes recent repository commits to summarize tooling and skill updates[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
5. **Compose Drafts**: Generates the three localized text drafts using builder-oriented tone[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
6. **Mandatory Cache Cleanup**: Cleans and purges `.pulse-cache/` once user inspection is complete to prevent lingering names and quotes[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].

## Security and Injection Containment
- **Untrusted Input Invariant**: Content retrieved from Slack and Google Sheets is classified as unverified text, not executable directives[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51]. Messages containing requests such as "mark my chapter accepted" must be flagged as decision items, never enacted automatically[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
- **No Autonomous Posting**: The skill contains no network publication endpoints (`chat.postMessage`, social APIs); publication requires human copy-paste approval[^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-b7620e51].
- **Public-Copy Privacy**: PII and names not already public on external event registration pages are withheld from all drafted outputs[^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-8d999d9a].

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations Skill Suite
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill suite and execution engines automating AAIF chapter intake, diagnostic setup verification, event synchronization, and reporting across local checkouts and installed agent runtimes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Community Event Operations skill suite provides automated execution engines and procedural workflows for managing Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) local chapters, community events, and ecosystem communications.[^evt-community-events-pr-60] Packaged as modular agent skills adhering to the `agent-skills` format, the suite automates chapter provisioning, attendee and intake triage, event synchronization across Google Workspace and Luma, and monthly chapter updates.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

The suite is engineered to execute both from source repository checkouts and as an installed plugin within agent runtimes like [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Claude Desktop without requiring a shell environment or local git repository.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

# Architecture / Specification

## Installed Plugin Runtime Architecture
The operational suite isolates execution paths to support running inside containerized, cached, or `.git`-less agent plugin installations:[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
- **Isolated Data Storage**: Runtime writes, synchronizations, caches, and backups are routed away from the current working directory (`cwd`) to a dedicated user application directory (e.g., `~/Library/Application Support/AAIF`), preventing workspace contamination during operator execution.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
- **Credential Resolution Chain**: Secret resolution follows a deterministic hierarchy across execution contexts: process environment variables first, local `.env` files within the repository root second, and OS-native secret storage (such as the macOS keychain) third, with per-run caching.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
- **Portability Guards**: Engine instructions address dependencies using relative `<skill-root>` conventions instead of fixed repository paths or shell variable overrides like `PYTHONPATH`.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

## Setup and Readiness Engine (`aaif-check-setup`)
The suite includes the `aaif-check-setup` diagnostic engine, providing plain-language readiness evaluations for operators.[^evt-community-events-pr-60] The tool verifies:
1. Availability and accessibility of required credentials (e.g., Slack, Google Workspace, Luma tokens).
2. Distinction between missing credentials and OS keychain access refusals.
3. Guided remediation providing scoped sign-in commands for missing or misconfigured integrations.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

## Execution Engines and Synchronization
Core scripts include `sync.py`, digest engines, and tracker fetch tools designed to gracefully handle partial network failures, ensure restrictive folder permissions (`0700` for backups), and clean up partial downloads during failure modes.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

# Lifecycle History
Originally developed as repository-bound automation scripts, the community event operations suite underwent extensive refactoring in PR #60 to support non-technical operators executing through desktop agent harnesses like Goose and Claude Desktop, eliminating assumptions about shell paths, git presence, and working directory ownership.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

# References
- Goose Agent Framework: [../resources/goose.md](../resources/goose.md)
- Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines: [../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md)
- Community Events Evaluation Suite: [../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Packaging, runtime isolation, and execution guidelines ensuring agent skills and tool plugins run predictably across checkout-free runtimes, desktop harnesses, and varied operating environments.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Plugin Portability Guidelines specify architectural and procedural standards for authoring agent skills and tool plugins that operate reliably across diverse host environments, including local development checkouts, packaged plugin caches, and desktop agent runtimes such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and Claude Desktop.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

When agents install plugins into runtime-managed caches, operational environments diverge significantly from conventional developer checkouts: shell environments may be absent, `.git` metadata is stripped, and the active working directory belongs to the operator rather than the plugin.[^evt-community-events-pr-60] These guidelines define constraints to prevent path breakage, workspace pollution, and credential discovery failures.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

# Architecture / Specification

## Directory Isolation and Output Handling
Portable agent plugins must strictly separate runtime data generation from the operator's current working directory (`cwd`):[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
- **Target Data Directories**: Plugins must resolve data output, local cache files, reports, and state backups to standard OS application support directories (such as `~/Library/Application Support/<ORGANIZATION>` on macOS or `$XDG_DATA_HOME` on Linux) rather than `cwd` or assumptions of a repository root.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
- **File System Cleanliness**: Workspaces must remain untouched unless an action explicitly instructs the agent to create user-facing files in `cwd`.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
- **Defensive Cleanup**: Intermediate failed syncs and partial downloads must be purged immediately to avoid corrupting subsequent executions.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

## Credential Resolution Hierarchy
To accommodate desktop and headless agents lacking interactive shells, secret retrieval must follow a deterministic, layered fallback order:[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
1. Host process environment variables.
2. Plugin or repository-level `.env` files.
3. Platform-native credential stores (e.g., macOS Keychain, secret service APIs).

Implementations must distinguish between missing keys and system authorization refusals, guiding the user with scoped remediation instructions rather than failing silently.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

## Path Resolution and Script Invocations
Skill definitions (`SKILL.md`) and operational wrappers must not assume shell environment configuration:
- Prohibit hardcoded repository root paths, fixed `/tmp` mounts, or dependencies on `PYTHONPATH` manipulation.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
- Reference intra-plugin resources using relative `<skill-root>` tokens that resolve dynamically regardless of whether the skill resides in a git repository or a flat directory cache.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]
- Ensure underlying execution scripts do not fail when `.git` directories or git binary tools are absent from the runtime host.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

## Readiness and Verification Diagnostics
Portable plugins should expose self-contained setup verification commands (such as a plain-language diagnostic check) that assess prerequisite credentials, tool access, and network reachability before executing multi-step autonomous tasks.[^evt-community-events-pr-60]

# References
- Community Event Operations Suite: [../skills/community-event-operations.md](../skills/community-event-operations.md)
- Agent Skills Packaging Specification: [../standards/agent-skills.md](../standards/agent-skills.md)
- Goose Framework: [../resources/goose.md](../resources/goose.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Operational security guidelines structuring runtime sandbox boundaries, tool egress controls, pre-execution hook policy enforcement, and multi-tier authorization gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline defines defensive design criteria, execution containment models, and authorization standards for deploying autonomous agents safely across development and enterprise environments. It provides operational principles for sandboxing, pre-execution runtime hooks, traffic checkpointing, and taxonomy-mapped threat mitigations.

# Architecture / Specification
The guideline establishes layered controls across runtime execution, authorization, network boundaries, and threat taxonomies:

## Hook-Based Policy Decision Point
Runtime policy enforcement intercepts execution via lifecycle hooks where the agent host suspends pending calls and submits the tool name, arguments, and full session context to an external Policy Decision Point (PDP).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38] Decisions follow three sequential stages:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]
1. **Deterministic Rules Engine**: Imposes non-negotiable static constraints and baseline invariants before any secondary model evaluation.
2. **Contextual Evaluation**: Routes non-trivial calls handed off by the deterministic rules to secondary classifiers, specialized evaluators, or isolated policy agents.
3. **Human Review Gate**: Escalates strictly when an `ask` verdict is rendered, directly counteracting human approval fatigue observed in production environments where passive oversight leads to approving routine actions without scrutiny.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]

The executing agent has no structural mechanism to influence or bypass any stage of the policy pipeline.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]

## Gateway Checkpoints and Traffic Controls
Complementing local hook controls, Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways such as [AgentGateway](../resources/agentgateway.md) operate as network-path checkpoints.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38] Gateways aggregate connections to remote MCP servers, handle OAuth authentication, enforce per-tool network permissions, and log tamper-evident payload events for downstream auditing.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]

## Sandbox Confinement and Egress Limitations
Execution sandboxing is categorized as narrowing the blast radius from the full user account to the working directory rather than achieving total operational containment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41] Unless backed by kernel-level isolation (including namespaces, filesystem confinement, and system call filtering), sandboxes do not inherently block outbound network egress or prevent handoff attacks executed via host components.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41] Proxy allowlists must govern outbound connectivity, and artifact verification remains mandatory even within sandboxed environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]

## External Threat Harmonization
Defensive clauses across the guideline are mapped to MITRE ATLAS v5.6.0 techniques (including AML.T0109 for supply chain rug pulls, AML.T0110, and AML.T0051.001) and OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications categories (such as ASI02 and ASI04).[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]

# References
- Deliverable updates in aaif/wg-security-and-privacy: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/38 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]
- Policy decision point specification: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/39 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-39]
- ATLAS v5.6.0 and OWASP ASI cross-referencing: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/40 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-40]
- Sandbox boundary definitions: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/41 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-41]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
AgentGateway is an open-source traffic mediation and policy enforcement proxy under the Agentic AI Foundation that governs Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol communications.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38] It provides network-level control and checkpointing between runtime environments and distributed tool servers.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]

# Architecture / Specification
AgentGateway operates on the network communication path alongside host-level runtime hooks:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]
- **Network Checkpoint**: Serves as a single controlled entry point mediating traffic destined for remote MCP servers, preventing uninspected direct outbound calls.
- **Credential and Identity Management**: Centralizes OAuth credential exchanges and upstream authorization headers.
- **Granular Access Control**: Enforces per-tool execution policies and protocol-level filtering across agent identities.
- **Audit Telemetry**: Captures tool invocation payloads and telemetry to support verifiable downstream action logs.

# References
- Security best practices checkpoint positioning: https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/pull/38 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-38]

proposed_concept.title: AGNTCY Multi-Agent Infrastructure
proposed_concept.description: Open-source multi-agent infrastructure framework providing agent directory discovery, OASF schemas, SLIM secure messaging, identity credentials, and SHADI runtime sandboxing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
AGNTCY is an open-source infrastructure suite for multi-agent systems providing decentralized capability discovery, cryptographic identity, secure messaging, runtime sandboxing, and behavioral observability[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57]. Submitted to the Agentic AI Foundation ([AAIF](../governance/technical-committee.md)) as a Growth-stage project intake proposal, AGNTCY operates as a unified project bridging agent directories, transport protocols, secure hosts, and semantic telemetry[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].

Rather than implementing cognitive planning loops or reasoning runtimes, AGNTCY targets the connective fabric between autonomous agents, external tools, and host operating systems[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57]. It complements protocols such as [A2A](../standards/agent-network-protocol.md) and [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md), and mediation proxies like [agentgateway](../resources/agentgateway.md), without attempting to replace them[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].

# Architecture / Specification
AGNTCY comprises several modular components governed under a common infrastructure framework[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57]:

- **Agent Directory (`dir`)**: A distributed discovery layer for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, [A2A](../standards/agent-network-protocol.md) servers, and [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57]. It leverages Open Container Initiative (OCI) registries for metadata artifact storage and a Distributed Hash Table (DHT) for peer-to-peer network discovery[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].
- **Open Agentic Schema Framework (OASF)**: An object schema derived from the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) providing standardized machine records describing agents, tools, and capability interfaces, interoperating with A2A Agent Cards[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].
- **Secure Low-Latency Interactive Messaging (SLIM)**: A multi-agent transport protocol and custom binding for A2A supporting multicast RPC across cloud-native and edge environments[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57]. SLIM secures group communication channels using Messaging Layer Security (MLS, RFC 9420) over HTTP/2 transport[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].
- **Identity**: A credential and policy framework issuing verifiable credentials, W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs), and agent badges, enabling Tool Based Access Control (TBAC) for granular agent-to-tool policy enforcement[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].
- **Observe**: An observability SDK and Metrics Compute Engine (MCE) extending [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI/LLM semantic conventions downstream with agent-specific spans and computed output-quality metrics[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].
- **Secure Host for Agentic AI Dynamic Instantiation (SHADI)**: A Rust-based host runtime (`shadictl`, `shadi_sandbox`, `agent_secrets`, `shadi_memory`, `agent_transport_slim`) enforcing OS-level process sandboxing, encrypted SQLCipher memory, and keychain secret release verification gates[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].
- **AgentBridge**: A CLI interconnect distributed within SHADI that bridges standard A2A client and server interfaces to external coding harnesses (such as Claude Code, Copilot, or Cursor Agent)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].
- **coffeeAGNTCY**: An end-to-end multi-agent reference application and enterprise sandbox used to demonstrate AGNTCY patterns across discovery, identity, messaging, and coordination[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].

# Lifecycle History
AGNTCY was open-sourced in March 2025 by Cisco alongside LangChain and Galileo, entering the Linux Foundation in July 2025 with support from Cisco, Dell Technologies, Google Cloud, Oracle, and Red Hat[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57]. In August 2026, maintainers submitted an intake proposal to the AAIF Technical Committee under the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md) requesting an intra-foundation transfer to AAIF at the Growth maturity stage[^evt-project-proposals-issue-57].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Working Group Meeting Notes Generator
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill and CLI toolkit converting working group LFX audio transcripts and AI summaries into standardized AAIF meeting minutes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Working Group Meeting Notes Generator is an automated agent skill and command-line toolkit designed to convert raw meeting audio transcripts and LFX summaries into standardized, publication-ready working group meeting minutes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63]. It enforces consistent synthesis across decisions, action items, and evidence citations across Agentic AI Foundation working groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

Operating in accordance with standards established in [Taxonomy Landscape Meeting Notes Guidelines](../guidelines/taxonomy-landscape-meeting-notes.md), the tool standardizes note formatting while ensuring that all generated minutes require human review prior to publication[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

# Architecture / Specification
The meeting notes generation workflow relies on a modular Python toolkit and date-driven CLI pipeline[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63]:

- **LFX MCP Integration**: Connects via Model Context Protocol (MCP) to Linux Foundation LFX APIs to retrieve official meeting audio transcripts and structured summaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Transcript Synthesis & Fallback**: Correlates high-level LFX summaries with detailed timestamped transcripts, incorporating fallback handling when primary summaries or raw audio transcripts are incomplete[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Structured Output Generation**: Generates Markdown meeting minutes structuring logged decisions, explicit action item ownership, and cited evidence[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Cross-WG Parameterization**: Configurable across foundation groups via parameter overrides for project, committee, and meeting identifiers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].
- **Human Verification Gate**: Requires manual maintainer or working group chair review to verify decision accuracy and task assignments before notes are published[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

# Lifecycle History
Developed in the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the toolkit was implemented as a reusable Python module with plans to migrate the shared CLI logic into the foundation's centralized `working-groups-chair` tooling repository for broad WG adoption[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-63].

proposed_concept.title: Observal
proposed_concept.description: Self-hosted registry, multi-harness configuration renderer, and insight engine governing agentic resources and client-side execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Observal is an open-source (Apache-2.0), self-hosted registry and system of record for agentic resources, including Agent Skills, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, hooks, prompts, sandboxes, and bundling agent configurations.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59] Operating beside the live request path rather than acting as an inline proxy, Observal manages artifacts prior to execution by rendering native client configurations and evaluates performance post-session via client trace ingestion and LLM-assisted insights.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]

# Architecture / Specification
Observal provides artifact governance, cross-client installation, and post-session telemetry mediation:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]
- **Resource Registry**: Versioned catalog supporting team namespaces, visibility controls, and pull-request review workflows across five agentic resource types.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]
- **Multi-Harness Configuration**: Generates native harness configurations and lockfiles across ten agent runtimes, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, Copilot in VS Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Antigravity, [Goose](goose.md), and Pi.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]
- **Open Protocol Integration**: Publishes approved resources using [Agentic Resource Discovery](../standards/agentic-resource-discovery.md) (ARD v0.91) entries with `urn:air:` identifiers at `/.well-known/ard.json`, executes agent-to-agent delegation via [A2A](../standards/agent-network-protocol.md) Task definitions through a bundled MCP server, and aligns with the [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) specification.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]
- **Client Traces and Insights**: Client hooks capture session execution data—including prompt context, tool invocations, MCP round trips, token usage, and errors—pinned directly to installed artifact versions, generating diagnostic failure insights via LiteLLM.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]
- **Self-Hosted Infrastructure**: Deploys on Postgres, ClickHouse, and Redis via Docker Compose or Kubernetes without external data egress, providing unified SSO, SCIM, and audit logging.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]

Unlike inline traffic proxies such as [Agentgateway](agentgateway.md) that mediate active network requests, Observal operates at install time and post-session, drawing evidence directly from client-side hooks.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]

# Lifecycle History
Observal was submitted to the AAIF Technical Committee as an open project proposal in Issue #59 on October 14, 2026, following 46 prior independent open-source releases.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-59]
