proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining the six-step intake, review, voting, legal formation, and onboarding workflow for prospective AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process is the operating procedure implementing the [Project Lifecycle Policy](project-lifecycle-policy.md) for proposing, reviewing, approving, and onboarding open-source projects into the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333] The procedure is structured into six sequential steps plus parallel contributor paperwork, defaulting to offline, asynchronous execution to accommodate a globally distributed Technical Committee (TC).[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]

# Architecture / Specification
The intake and approval pipeline coordinates defined actor roles across six steps:[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]
- **Step 1 - Initial Intake**: The CTO, assisted by an automated compliance intake agent, screens applications for completeness, performs smoke tests, and solicits input from [Technical Committee Chairs](../governance/technical-committee.md) on the proposal issue.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]
- **Step 2 - TC Q&A Window**: An asynchronous inquiry window on GitHub.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333] Advancement requires meeting an explicit engagement bar consisting of active TC member participation; if unmet, the TC chairs seek an on-demand TC supporter to champion the proposal, failing which the proposal is rejected.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333] Live presentations occur on demand only if requested by a TC member.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]
- **Parallel Step - Contributor Paperwork**: Contribution agreements, technical charters, and trademark assignments are prepared concurrently by LF PMO and LF Legal, and must be execution-ready before Step 4.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]
- **Step 3 - TC Vote**: The Technical Committee conducts an offline vote using LFX Vote to recommend admission and determine the initial lifecycle stage.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]
- **Step 4 - GB Vote**: The Governing Board votes offline via LFX Vote on organizational readiness and Foundation resource allocation.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]
- **Step 5 - LF Legal Formation**: LF Legal and AAIF staff execute final contribution and charter agreements via DocuSign.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]
- **Step 6 - Technical Onboarding**: Project maintainers and LF IT transfer code repositories, domains, credentials, and continuous integration infrastructure.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]

### Application Tracking Labels
Proposal issues submitted via the standardized issue form are tracked using specific workflow labels:[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7][^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-15a00e3a]
- `New`: The submission is placed in the initial intake backlog.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]
- `Approved`: The application has fulfilled all approval gates and completed foundation onboarding.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]
- `Declined`: The proposal has been formally rejected with documented rationale.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]
- `Waiting on Comment`: Review is paused awaiting answers or updates from the submitter.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]
- `Too Early`: The project is not yet mature enough for hosting; guidance is provided for subsequent reapplication.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]

Foundation project hosting does not require prior AAIF corporate membership, nor does project acceptance confer corporate membership tier status or a Governing Board seat.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-3d9290b7]

# Lifecycle History
Operating procedure v0.3 was published on August 28, 2026, codifying the engagement bar, automated intake agent responsibilities, and LFX Vote mechanics.[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-9c234333]

mutations.rationale: Captures the architectural pattern proposed in WG Identity & Trust for binding human approvals to hardware-protected keys, witnessed actions, and freshness appraisal.

proposed_concept.title: Hardware-Bound Human Authorization
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern binding human approval to hardware-protected keys, witnessed actions, and explicit freshness appraisal.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Hardware-Bound Human Authorization is an architectural security pattern establishing cryptographic verifiable accountability for agent actions by binding explicit human approvals to hardware-protected signing keys, correlated with independent execution witnesses and freshness appraisals.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19] Conforming to the separation of evidence, appraisal, and reliance defined in the IETF Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) architecture (RFC 9334), the pattern ensures that a verifier distinguishes between cryptographic key possession and actual user authorization intent.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern structures verifier appraisal across five orthogonal dimensions:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]
- **Source Evaluation**: Evaluates who asserted each claim, how the source was authenticated, and its relative independence from both the agent and operator.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19] Hardware protection alone does not confer source independence.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]
- **Construction Integrity**: Verifies the strict binding among human approval, agent identity, delegated scopes, and execution constraints (such as destination, amount, and expiry) recorded in an [action record](../taxonomy/action-record.md) or [approval checkpoint](approval-checkpoint.md).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]
- **Hardware Assurance**: Validates cryptographic evidence of key protection, provenance, and platform measurements where supported; unverified hardware claims remain explicitly unestablished.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]
- **Freshness, Expiry, and Revocation**: Checks challenge freshness, execution timestamps, credential validity, and status evidence age, keeping revocation checks and temporal age separate.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]
- **Observation Scope and Witnessing**: Correlates separate witness records across request submission, execution context, and final outcome.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19] Unavailable evidence is explicitly differentiated from contradictory evidence.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]

### Hardware-to-Cloud Boundary
Edge hardware devices provide strong evidence regarding local key operations and user approvals within their demonstrated local capture scope.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19] However, local hardware protection does not establish what occurred inside a remote agent model or service, which requires independent execution evidence bound to the relevant request and outcome.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) via Issue #19 as a worked example contribution to the AAIF Patterns deliverable.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-19]

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: Technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for project intake, working group governance, and architectural coordination.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) serves as the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), an initiative organized as a directed fund of The Linux Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. The TC assists the Governing Board (GB) by evaluating technical project proposals, establishing and overseeing working groups, and enforcing the foundation's project lifecycle policy[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Operations and Governance
Adopted on March 3, 2026, the TC Charter outlines the committee's scope, voting mechanics, and operational procedures[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

### Composition and Leadership
Each Platinum Member organization of the AAIF designates one voting representative to the TC[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. For the founding term running from March 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026, members appointed by the Governing Board include[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0]:
- **David Soria Parra** (Chair) - Anthropic
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (Co-Chair) - Microsoft
- **Alan Blount** - Google
- **Bradley Axen** - Block
- **James Ward** - Amazon Web Services
- **Nick Cooper** - OpenAI
- **Sambhav Kothari** - Bloomberg
- **Steve Faulkner** - Cloudflare

### Core Responsibilities
Under its charter, the TC is tasked with[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]:
- Establishing, managing, and archiving working groups across domain areas relevant to AAIF's scope.
- Coordinating technical priorities, shared vision, and cross-project integration between Technical Projects.
- Recommending projects to the Governing Board for acceptance and designating stage progressions under the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md).
- Recommending resource allocation and mentorship priorities to support technical initiatives.
- Maintaining and applying technical policies subject to Governing Board approval.

### Decision Making and Voting
While operating primarily on consensus, formal voting proceeds on a one-vote-per-voting-member basis[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]:
- **Quorum**: Requires at least 50% of voting TC members present to take formal binding action[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Lazy Consensus**: Proposals achieve approval through a 7-day silent review window if no formal objections are filed[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04]. If an objection is lodged, resolution requires an electronic vote decided by a majority of all TC voting members[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Escalation**: Unresolvable votes may be referred to the Governing Board for final resolution[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].
- **Charter Amendments**: Require approval by a two-thirds majority of the TC and final ratification by the Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04].

# Hosted Projects
The TC oversees technical projects admitted under the lifecycle model, including foundational efforts such as[^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0]:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** (Impact Stage): An open standard protocol facilitating client-tool and data source integration for LLM-powered applications.
- **goose** (Impact Stage): An open-source, extensible local-first agent framework supporting automated tool execution, multi-turn file edits, and testing across foundation models.

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Governance policy defining intake requirements, stage transitions, evaluation criteria, and annual reviews for Agentic AI Foundation technical projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy sets the authoritative criteria and processes for technical projects seeking entry into and progression within the foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]. Originally created on March 18, 2026, and updated on October 15, 2026, the policy regulates the complete project lifecycle across admission, graduation, and annual review cycles[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

# Proposal Requirements
New or existing open-source technical projects submit proposals via the foundation's project proposals repository[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]. Every submission must provide verified information, including[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]:
- Project name, descriptive purpose, origin, and evolutionary history.
- Alignment statement articulating how the effort supports the AAIF mission and interacts with existing foundation initiatives.
- Concrete use cases demonstrating adoption and utility across agentic workflows.
- Technical Committee sponsor designation (optional, providing mentorship and onboarding guidance).
- Permissive licensing under an OSI-approved open-source license.
- Public source code repository, automated CI/CD and release pipelines, public issue tracker, and transparent contribution guides.
- Analysis of external software dependencies and corresponding license compatibility.
- Identification of maintainers, leadership composition, and documented governance processes (`GOVERNANCE.md`).
- Official communication forums, project websites, social presence, existing funding sources, and technical infrastructure prerequisites.

# Lifecycle Stages
The policy defines four sequential progression stages, providing tiered foundation mentorship, visibility, and resource backing[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]:
1. **Sandbox Stage**: Entry-level incubation for early-stage or experimental projects meeting core baseline open-source standards and architectural alignment[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
2. **Growth Stage**: Intermediate maturation stage for projects exhibiting sustained community adoption, multi-organization maintainer distribution, and healthy governance processes[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].
3. **Impact Stage**: Production-grade foundational projects showing widespread ecosystem adoption, robust governance, cross-vendor deployment, and strict architectural stability (e.g., Model Context Protocol and goose)[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2][^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-8f2953e0].
4. **Emeritus Stage**: A planned retirement or archived state for projects that have completed their lifecycle, reached end-of-life, or whose maintainers have transitioned support elsewhere[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

# Review and Maintenance
Progression between stages requires review and approval by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in coordination with the Governing Board[^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-b0f27f04][^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2]. Projects participate in mandatory Annual Reviews to assess ongoing governance vitality, dependency hygiene, community growth, and continued alignment with AAIF strategic priorities[^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-04c1d0b2].

mutations.rationale: Update working group submission guidelines to reflect member eligibility constraints, GitHub issue intake workflow, review status labels, and lifecycle progression.

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Proposal Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Operating guidelines governing proposal preparation, membership eligibility, issue tracking, and approval workflows for AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Proposal Submission Guidelines instruct contributors on preparing and submitting formal proposals to establish new Working Groups (WGs) or revive Concluded WGs under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2][^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b]. Last updated on October 15, 2026, the guideline operationalizes the [Working Group Lifecycle Policy](../policies/working-group-lifecycle-policy.md) and standardized GitHub issue application workflows[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].

# Eligibility and Scope
Working groups represent enduring bodies organized around long-lived problem domains relevant to agentic AI[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]. Focused, short-term, or single-deliverable tasks (such as individual whitepapers, benchmarks, or specific reference architectures) must be chartered as workstreams within existing working groups rather than creating independent groups[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].

Eligibility constraints require[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]:
- **Submitters**: Proposals must originate from a representative of an AAIF member organization in good standing (Platinum, Gold, Silver, or Associate tier)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]. Non-member contributors must obtain sponsorship from a member organization representative to submit on their behalf[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
- **Chairs**: Designated working group chairs must belong to Platinum, Gold, or Silver member organizations[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
- **Participants**: Working group meetings, discussions, and technical activities remain open to the public and all community members regardless of formal membership status[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].

# Proposal Structure and Review Process
Proposals are submitted through GitHub issue templates within the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository and tracked on the public Working Group Proposals Board[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-87b3376703c5-313cc435][^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b]. Submissions require eight structured components[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2]:
1. **Submitter Information**: Name, affiliation, role, contact info, and AAIF tier[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
2. **Identity**: Proposed title and a clear, jargon-free one-sentence scope summary[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
3. **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Documented industry gap, agentic relevance, alignment with foundation objectives, and justification against existing working groups[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
4. **Scope & Concrete Deliverables**: In-scope and out-of-scope boundaries and tangible year-one technical deliverables (e.g., specifications, benchmarks, architectures)[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
5. **First-Year Plan**: Milestone timeline and regular meeting schedules[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
6. **Leadership & Committed Participants**: Proposed chairs and initial committed contributors[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
7. **Overlap & Coordination**: Touchpoints with other AAIF groups and external standards bodies[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].
8. **Impact, Risks & Resources**: Operational requirements, infrastructure dependencies, and risk mitigation strategies[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-a2eb51a2].

# Review Tracking and Lifecycle Onboarding
Following intake verification by foundation staff, the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) reviews proposals asynchronously directly on the GitHub issue[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b]. Review states are categorized by workflow labels[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b]:
- `New`: Newly filed submission queued in backlog triage[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers require clarification or supplementary data from submitters[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
- `Too Early`: The proposal concept lacks maturity or readiness; guidance is provided for potential reapplication[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
- `Declined`: The proposal is formally declined with rationale documented in issue comments[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].
- `Approved`: Formal endorsement by both the TC and the Governing Board[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].

Upon approval, the working group launches into **Sandbox** stage, initiating regular meetings and monthly reporting while formalizing its operating charter[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b]. Transition to **Active** status requires subsequent TC evaluation and approval of the completed charter[^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-6c29ea3b].

proposed_concept.title: Guardrail
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining a model-level constraint that prescribes intended actions or prevents unwanted actions and disclosures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Guardrail is a universal taxonomy term defining a form of constraint on a model that prescribes intended actions or prevents unwanted actions or disclosures[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-91]. While guardrails apply directly to models, agent harnesses host and provide their runtime execution boundaries and enforcement mechanisms[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-91].

# Architecture / Specification
Within the AAIF taxonomy schema, guardrails represent targeted operational constraints governing model input and output boundaries[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-91]:
- **Target of Evaluation**: Guardrails specifically target models, prescribing intended behavior or restricting unwanted disclosures and tool invocation sequences[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-91].
- **Harness Integration**: The agent harness acts as the hosting environment providing context and executing pre- and post-generation guardrail checks[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-91].
- **Constraint Specialization**: Connects to the broader concept of constraint, formalizing active policy enforcement rules rather than ambient runtime limitations[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-91].

# Lifecycle History
The term was introduced as a universal taxonomy definition in PR #91 within the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-91]. Category assignments and broader term hierarchies were deferred pending alignment with related governance entries[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-91].

# References
- Taxonomy & Landscape PR #91: https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape/pull/91

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugins Specification
proposed_concept.description: Open packaging format and client configuration standard combining Agent Skills and Model Context Protocol servers into distributable plugins.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent Plugins is an open, vendor-neutral packaging standard that bundles reusable components—specifically [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server configurations—into distributable plugins across compatible agent clients[^evt-project-proposals-issue-56]. Governed by a cross-vendor Technical Steering Committee, the standard establishes a client configuration contract and conformance test suite while reserving client-specific extension namespaces[^evt-project-proposals-issue-56].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification defines a vendor-neutral package directory structure and manifest format[^evt-project-proposals-issue-56]:
- **Component Composition**: Combines instructions packaged under the [Agent Skills](../standards/agent-skills.md) format with configuration blocks for discovering and connecting to local or remote MCP servers[^evt-project-proposals-issue-56].
- **Protocol Separation**: Retains MCP as the authoritative wire and lifecycle standard, and Agent Skills as the authoritative skill format, standardizing only client packaging and discovery configuration[^evt-project-proposals-issue-56].
- **Extension Namespaces**: Provides reserved, client-owned namespaces to support proprietary host features and custom policies without compromising the portable core[^evt-project-proposals-issue-56].
- **Conformance Suite**: Maintains JSON schemas, client test suites, and migration tools to validate cross-client compatibility[^evt-project-proposals-issue-56].

# Lifecycle History
Originating from the Open Plugin initiative, version 1.0.0 of the specification was published under Apache-2.0 and CC-BY-4.0 licenses before being submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in Issue #56 for consideration as an official AAIF standard[^evt-project-proposals-issue-56].

# References
- Agent Plugins Project Proposal: https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/56
- Agent Plugins Specification Repository: https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec

proposed_concept.title: Agent Context and Memory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: Proposed AAIF technical working group defining standards, reference architectures, and lifecycle semantics for agent context and memory systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Context and Memory Working Group is a proposed AAIF technical working group established to develop vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and lifecycle semantics for how agents acquire, organize, retrieve, retain, and share context and memory[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-5]. Chaired by Stephen Chin (Neo4j), the group addresses interoperability challenges spanning context graphs, knowledge graphs, vector retrieval indexes, and episodic memory stores[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-5].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group proposal identifies key technical focus areas across agent memory architectures[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-5]:
- **Memory Models and Representation**: Standardizing data structures for working, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory across graph, vector, relational, and document stores[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-5].
- **Context Management**: Formulating patterns and best practices for context retrieval, ranking, assembly, summarization, compression, caching, and token budgeting[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-5].
- **Lifecycle and Security Semantics**: Establishing rules for memory retention, eviction, cross-session sharing, and privacy controls[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-5].
- **Benchmarking and Evaluation**: Creating evaluation methodologies to measure memory recall quality, execution latency, cost, and task completion impacts[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-5].

# Lifecycle History
The working group proposal was submitted to the AAIF Working Group Proposals repository in Issue #5, coordinating alignment with the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) working groups[^evt-working-group-proposals-issue-5].

# References
- Working Group Proposal Issue #5: https://github.com/aaif/working-group-proposals/issues/5

proposed_concept.description: Platform-neutral 16-question evaluation instrument measuring production deployment stages, failure frequencies, and governance priorities across agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Production Survey is a platform-neutral 16-question evaluation instrument produced by the [Accuracy and Reliability Working Group](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) to quantify deployment maturities, failure distributions, and operational pain points across production agentic AI workloads[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14]. The survey provides benchmark data on human oversight topologies, failure factors, and safety trade-offs[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].

# Architecture / Specification
The instrument organizes evaluation metrics across four structured sections[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14]:
- **System Topology and Oversight**: Assesses single-agent and multi-agent coordination architectures alongside human verification patterns and organization scales[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].
- **Reliability Degradation Factors**: Evaluates common failure modes in Question 10, specifically capturing quality decline caused by underlying system updates (such as model, prompt, or version changes) and failures to recover safely after an error (such as leaving partial, uncompensated actions behind)[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].
- **Benefits and Constraints**: Collects comparative data on production business benefits against engineering, regulatory, and latency constraints[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].
- **Data Custody and Consent**: Incorporates aggregate reporting commitments, AAIF storage policies, and formal respondent consent terms governing anonymous survey collection[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained under deliverable D2 (`deliverables/arwg-survey.md`) within `aaif/wg-accuracy-and-reliability`, the survey was revised in PR #14 to refine failure factor granularity for post-error recovery and regression tracking, reorder organizational questions, and add participant consent terms[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-14].

# References
- Accuracy and Reliability Survey PR #14: https://github.com/aaif/wg-accuracy-and-reliability/pull/14

proposed_concept.title: nono
proposed_concept.description: Open-source agent runtime security tool providing kernel-enforced sandboxing, credential isolation, and Sigstore-based instruction attestation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
nono is an open-source agent runtime security tool designed to secure AI agents, their tools, credentials, and configuration files via kernel-enforced sandboxing with composable policies and low latency [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]. Created in February 2026 by Luke Hinds, nono isolates host and execution privileges for general-purpose and coding agents including [Goose](goose.md), Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, as well as frameworks such as ADK, Pydantic AI, and LangChain [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61].

# Architecture / Specification
nono enforces least privilege and policy-driven isolation around the agent process, its child executions, and connected external servers [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61]:

- **Kernel-Enforced Sandboxing:** Restricts file system visibility, host capabilities, and sub-process execution paths for running agents and tools [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61].
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Confinement:** Isolates MCP server processes to explicitly defined network endpoints, files, and credentials, providing OS-level guardrails beneath application-level authorization [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61].
- **Sigstore Instruction Attestation:** Integrates Sigstore cryptographic signatures to verify the provenance and integrity of agent instruction files such as `AGENTS.md`, rejecting unsigned or tampered prompts before runtime ingestion [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61].
- **Host vs. Network Demarcation:** Operates on the host side of agent execution, relaying outbound network traffic to mediation proxies like [Agent Gateway](agentgateway.md) or performing optional host-level network filtering [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61].
- **Policy as Code:** Implements composable, per-command security policies governing CI pipelines and production enterprise toolchains outside the agent's internal reasoning loop [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61].

# Lifecycle History
In March 2026, nono was proposed for intake into the AAIF Sandbox stage under Technical Committee sponsorship from Sambhav Kothari [^evt-project-proposals-issue-61].

# References
- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/nolabs-ai/nono
- Proposal Issue: https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/61

mutations.rationale: Documents URACE, an open-source blueprint specification and recursive orchestration loop proposed for the AAIF Sandbox.

proposed_concept.title: Universal Recursive Autonomous Co-Founder Engine (URACE)
proposed_concept.description: Blueprint-first agent orchestration specification and recursive runtime loop composed of reusable patterns, cognitive compaction, and rule-graph tracking.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Universal Recursive Autonomous Co-Founder Engine (URACE) is an open-source, blueprint-first agent orchestration and context-governance specification designed to provide a portable alternative to rigid software agent libraries [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60]. Formatted as a single install-as-bootstrap standard document (`URACE.md`), the specification defines 72 independent, reusable structural primitives—spanning authority boundaries, cognitive resumes, and regression gates—released under the CC0 1.0 Universal public domain dedication [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

# Architecture / Specification
URACE decouples high-level lifecycle governance from execution mechanics by orchestrating pluggable runtime tools [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60]:

- **Decoupled Execution:** Treats Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients and servers or agent runtimes like [Goose](goose.md) as modular executors tasked with code modifications, while URACE validates systemic boundaries and rule invariants [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Dynamic Context Compaction:** Implements the `urace /compact` lifecycle protocol to progressively compress linear conversation and execution logs into semantic Cognitive Resumes, mitigating [context exhaustion](../taxonomy/context-exhaustion.md) across long recursive loops [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Deterministic Rule-Graph Tracking:** Employs `urace /rules` to map codebase changes against queryable snapshots of active permissions and policy constraints, tracing agent decisions back to explicit human authorizations [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].
- **Zero-Dependency Blueprint:** Operates natively within code repositories via bootstrap specifications rather than external runtime dependencies, providing a dynamic counterpart to static repository guidance files [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

# Lifecycle History
Submitted by joaoalbertocsjunior in March 2026, URACE was proposed to the AAIF as a Growth/Sandbox project to establish standardized, reusable agent blueprint patterns [^evt-project-proposals-issue-60].

# References
- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/joaoalbertocsjunior/URACE
- Proposal Issue: https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/60

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, verification test suites, and trust models for agent identity, delegation trees, and key recovery.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group is an AAIF technical body developing vendor-neutral identity primitives, cryptographic attestation frameworks, delegation protocols, and lifecycle verification test cases for autonomous agent systems [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18]. The group defines how agents, their human principals, and mediating infrastructure establish provenance, enforce least privilege, propagate delegated authority, and recover from key compromise [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18, ^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20].

# Architecture / Specification
Key focus areas and technical workstreams within the working group include:

- **Agent Identity & DIDs:** Specifying decentralized identifiers, key bindings, and machine-verifiable credentials under standards such as the [Agent Network Protocol](../standards/agent-network-protocol.md).
- **Delegation Trees & Disputed Revocations:** Modeling hierarchical subagent delegation lifecycles, including test vectors where a parent identity is revoked while child delegations remain presented, or where revocation signals are delayed or unenforced [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18, ^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20].
- **Re-Registration & Artifact Binding:** Defining test suites that tie signed action records and requests across identifier rotations and re-registrations [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18, ^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20].
- **Key Recovery Semantics:** Developing recovery record rules signed jointly by registries and responsible entities under software attestation matching; recovery records carry forward history, revocations, and disputes while preventing unauthorized re-grants following compromise [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20].
- **Evidence Verification:** Coordinating with external test vector suites such as `agent-evidence-vectors` to ensure deterministic validation across verifiers [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18, ^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20].

# Lifecycle History
The working group actively evaluates identity and delegation lifecycle use cases. In late 2026, test suites covering disputed delegation revocation, identifier re-registration, and lost-key recovery workflows were integrated into the group's test harness [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-18, ^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-20].

# References
- Working Group Repository: https://github.com/aaif/wg-identity-and-trust
- Delegation Lifecycle Test Cases: https://github.com/aaif/wg-identity-and-trust/pull/20
